### Added
- **A new courses experience for students (`/{lang}/learn/courses/`, Arabic and English; on `release/uat`, not live).** The school-courses pilot is re-presented as three pages built for a student's real jobs. The home is a finder: school system, grade, subject, with no dropdown and no script needed. The course map shows every strand and lesson of a course on one page, with what is done and what is next. A lesson is a loop of five numbered steps: what the class asks, a thought before starting, the lesson with the museum's discoveries woven between its sections on a gold thread, where it leads, and a self-check. Every discovery card opens its record in the museum; a Qur'an card prints the verse from the museum's frozen text and links the passage; a record that is not written yet is named but never linked. Progress is kept in the browser only (no account, nothing sent). A classroom view shows one step at a time for a projector, and a print layout turns a lesson into a handout. Measured on the built pages: every one of the 16 lessons is two taps from the home at phone width, and all of them are reachable and complete with scripts switched off. Design and reasoning: `docs/courses-mission/DESIGN.md`. The Urdu courses page is unchanged, byte for byte; no Urdu page or string is part of this work.

### Fixed
- **Arabic lesson pages no longer pass English off as Arabic.** The pilot stored the English sentence under `ar` for all 29 curriculum expectations. The new lesson page shows such a text in its own language and direction, labelled "official wording, not yet translated", and treats a text as translated only when the record carries a real translation.
- **Two lesson cards now open real records.** `person/al-jazari` and `person/sultan-bin-salman` were links to empty stubs; an alias search showed both subjects have records under other ids (`person/al-jazari-engineer`, `person/sultan-bin-salman-al-saud`), and the two pilot lessons now link those.

### Tests
- **Courses mission, phase 1: a measured audit of the school-courses pilot.** Before the courses surface is redesigned, the 23 records of the Ontario Grade 6 Science pilot and their pages were inventoried by a committed script (`scripts/courses/o01_audit.py`) and checked against the Ministry's own text by a fresh reviewer. The audit (`docs/courses-mission/AUDIT.md`) found that none of the pilot's 29 curriculum expectations is the Ministry's wording and 17 sit under the wrong code, that its Arabic and Urdu expectation texts are copies of the English, that 5 of its 14 linked records are empty stubs, and that no enrichment card is written from its own record's sources. Nothing is changed by this entry: it adds the audit, its evidence and an alias-search tool (`scripts/courses/find_entity.py`) that later phases use before linking a lesson to a record or declaring one missing. No Urdu page or string is part of this work.
- **Courses mission, phase 2: the claims about the new courses pages are measured.** Four committed checks stand behind the new surface: `o03_taps.mjs` walks from the courses home to every lesson with real taps in a phone-sized browser and counts them; `o10_nojs.mjs` repeats the walk with scripts off and checks every step, card and question is on the page; `o11_boundaries.py` builds the neighbouring pages before and after and compares them byte for byte; `o09_vision.py` reads the screenshot review register. Five review rounds by fresh reviewers found 100 visible defects on the new pages; each is either fixed and confirmed gone by a later reviewer on a re-taken screenshot, or listed with the reason it stands.

### Tests
- The feature-export test now covers the Ibadat Browser: detection by corpus and kind, worship topics, the false-god and «احتجّ» gates, du'a inheritance from `isDuaPassage`, and a book harvested later entering automatically.

- **Hudud Allah and Kaba'ir Browser: متصفح حدود الله والكبائر (`/{lang}/hudud/`).** A new browser over the one graph gathering every mention of the limits of God and the major sins in the museum's sources: the «تلك حدود الله» and «ومن يتعد حدود الله» verses, the prescribed penalties — stoning, flogging, the amputated hand and ta'zir — and the crimes they answer in the two Sahihs, the Muwatta and the Sunan, the «اجتنبوا السبع الموبقات» and kaba'ir lists, the carrying out of penalties in the seerah and the reports of the Companions and Successors, and every mention in every harvested book. Passages are detected at build time by a guarded lexicon in `scripts/hudud.ts` — strong signals («حدود الله»، «حدوده»، إقامة الحد، رجم، تعزير، قطع اليد، punishment جلد forms، كبائر، موبقات) admit a passage directly; weak signals (ungated «حدود»/«الحد»، bare «جلد»، the hadd crimes، قصاص، «كبيرة») count only beside a strong signal or two at a time — so a book harvested later joins by itself. Verified false positives are excluded by id («رجماً بالغيب»، the accidental hand cuts of Yusuf's women, «تجلد» the mu'allaqa's "endure") and by pattern («ترجمة» biography can never reach «رجم»، «انقطع» is not «قطع»، «تعزّروه» is not «تعزير»). Ships with 48 detected passages (21 Qur'an, 27 sunnah and books), 9 curated records led by the new umbrella `concept/hudud-allah-wal-kabair` with trilingual prose, `mentions` edges on every detected passage, a landing card and an Explore menu entry, and `/api/v1/hudud.json`. In Arabic, English and Urdu; the new records are drafts until a human reads them.

## v1.22.0 — 2026-11-11
### Added
- **Hasanat and Sayyi'at Ledger, Calculator and Counter: قائمة وآلة حاسبة وعدّاد الحسنات والسيئات (`/{lang}/hisab/`).** A new page over the one graph with three parts. The **list** gathers every text in the Qur'an, the Sunnah, the seerah and the harvested books that counts, writes, multiplies, erases, weighs or reckons a deed — the tenfold and the seven-hundredfold, the writing of an intention, the erasing and expiating of bad deeds, ranks and the qirat, the Scale, the recording angels and the record, the bankrupt, the reckoning — found at build time by a guarded lexicon, so a book harvested later joins by itself. The **calculator** has one row per act for which a named text states a figure (a good deed done, a letter of the Qur'an, a hundred tasbihs, prayer in congregation, a step to the mosque and twenty more): you enter a count, it multiplies by the stated figure and shows good deeds written, bad deeds written, bad deeds erased and ranks as four separate sums, a range where the text gives a range, and the result in words where the text gives no number. The **counter** is a tally for remembrance kept in your own browser. The page describes what the texts state and gives no ruling: every figure links to its passage, narration variants are shown and not ranked, and a caveat sits above the tool. In Arabic, English and Urdu, with a landing card, an Explore menu entry and `/api/v1/hisab.json`.

### Data
- **New lesson series record: Omar Abdelkafy's "The Hereafter" (al-Dar al-Akhira), episodes 1-3.** The first three of thirty-three lessons are written up in Arabic, English and Urdu: the questions the series sets about the grave, the etiquette of visiting the healthy and the sick, the Prophet's death, dying, wills, the first stage of the grave and the angels' questioning, condolence customs, and Abu Bakr's will to Umar. Every point cites its episode and timestamp, the lecturer's own opinions are labelled as his, and unclear stretches of the recording are marked as needing a source. The record is a draft until a human reads it.

- **"The Hereafter" (al-Dar al-Akhira), episode 30 added.** A lesson on the believer of Pharaoh's household and scenes of Paradise: the worst theft being from one's prayer, the straight path and the line drawn by the Prophet, a parable of the desert travellers, the abode of settled permanence, honour in obedience, the two resurrections, friends on the Day of Resurrection and vessels of gold, in Arabic, English and Urdu. Verses are paraphrased and never typed; unclear stretches and political digressions are marked or excluded.
- **"The Hereafter" (al-Dar al-Akhira), episode 31 added.** A lesson on joining what God ordered joined, fear of the evil reckoning and the seven in God's shade, patience and repelling evil with good, the gardens of Eden and their open doors, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and the building of the Kaaba, Abraham's generosity, the widow who raised orphans, and the three groups of the sura of the Event, in Arabic, English and Urdu, with the lecturer's answers to questions. Verses are paraphrased and never typed; reports without a chain are marked as such and unclear stretches are marked as needing a source.
- **"The Hereafter" (al-Dar al-Akhira), episode 32 added.** A short lesson, heavily garbled in the transcript, on scenes of Paradise in the suras al-Waqia, al-Haqqa, al-Dhariyat and al-Tur: the dying hour, the three kinds at death, the instruction on glorification in bowing and prostration, the record in the right hand, the righteous and the sealed drink, night prayer and the joining of offspring to their parents, in Arabic, English and Urdu. Verses are paraphrased and never typed; most points are marked as needing a source.
- **"The Hereafter" (al-Dar al-Akhira), episode 33 added.** The last harvested lesson, on the sura of the Human and a description of Paradise: the righteous and their drink, fulfilling vows and the report on voluntary acts, feeding the poor for God's face, the handkerchiefs of Sad ibn Muadh, couches, vessels and the spring of Salsabil, a description of Paradise read from an unnamed text, the call to the people of Paradise, the lifting of the veil and the day of increase, in Arabic, English and Urdu. The lecturer announces two summary episodes to come. Verses are paraphrased and never typed; unclear stretches are marked as needing a source. This completes the 33 harvested episodes of the series.
- **New record: Ahl al-Hikma (People of Wisdom), episodes 1 to 4.** A daily Ramadan series in which Omar Abdelkafy explains one aphorism a day from the Hikam of Ibn Ata Allah al-Iskandari. The first four episodes cover freedom from covetousness, the remembrance of the heart and the limbs, God's giving and withholding, and breaking one's own habits, with the stories he tells (Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, Said ibn al-Musayyab, Ibrahim ibn Adham, Harun al-Rashid), in Arabic, English and Urdu. The record is labelled contested because it carries his own opinions on customs, and unsupported reports are marked as needing a source.
- **"Ahl al-Hikma", episodes 5 to 8 added.** Four more daily lessons on the Hikam of Ibn Ata Allah: resting from planning while taking the means, the small and the great sin, travelling from creatures to the Creator with the Prophet and Abu Bakr in the cave, and the sin that bequeaths humility against the obedience that bequeaths pride, in Arabic, English and Urdu. His opinions are labelled his own, reports without a chain are marked as such, and unclear stretches are marked as needing a source.
- **"Ahl al-Hikma", episodes 9 to 12 added.** Four more daily lessons on the Hikam of Ibn Ata Allah: the need for God's forbearance in obedience, the delay of an answered prayer and the times and conditions of prayer, tasting the world's pain so parting is easy (with the lecturer's opinion on zakat), and what God has set you in as a measure of your standing, in Arabic, English and Urdu. His opinions and figures are labelled his own, reports without a chain are marked as such, and unclear stretches are marked as needing a source.
- **"Ahl al-Hikma", episodes 13 to 16 added.** Four more daily lessons on the Hikam of Ibn Ata Allah: the tongue loosed to ask as a sign God wishes to give, certainty about oneself against people's surmise, voluntary deeds against neglected duties, and demanding good manners of oneself and not haste of one's Lord, in Arabic, English and Urdu. His opinions are labelled his own, reports without a chain are marked as such, and unclear stretches are marked as needing a source.
- **"Ahl al-Hikma", episodes 17 to 20 added.** Four more daily lessons on the Hikam of Ibn Ata Allah: making one's need of God true so gifts come, supply according to readiness with al-Ghazali's dream and death, estrangement from creatures as the door to intimacy with God and the night journey, and the favour God creates then ascribes to you with the story of Zayd al-Khayl, in Arabic, English and Urdu. His opinions and figures are labelled his own, reports without a chain are marked as such, and unclear stretches are marked as needing a source.
- **"Ahl al-Hikma", episodes 21 to 24 added.** Four more daily lessons on the Hikam of Ibn Ata Allah: a creature's gift as a deprivation and God's withholding as kindness, the wise looking at what God will do with him while still planning, seeking every request through God and not through oneself with the manners of supplication, and understanding in being withheld with the story of Yusuf, in Arabic, English and Urdu. His opinions and figures are labelled his own, reports without a chain are marked as such, and unclear stretches are marked as needing a source.
- **"Ahl al-Hikma", episodes 25 to 27 added, completing the series.** The last three daily lessons on the Hikam of Ibn Ata Allah: episode 25 turns out to repeat the talk of episode 24 and is marked as such, then following what is heavier on the self when two matters are confused, and the forerunners of aspirations never piercing the walls of destiny with the story of Musa and Pharaoh, in Arabic, English and Urdu. His opinions and figures are labelled his own, a sweeping unsourced remark on two groups is recorded as his claim and not endorsed, and unclear stretches are marked as needing a source.
- **Qur'an fragments paraphrased in the "Hereafter" record.** Three short phrases in the Arabic text of episodes 2, 7 and 11 that echoed Qur'anic wording are now plain paraphrase, because the museum never types the Qur'an.

### Data
- **538 hadith reports that count a deed, harvested from the open hadith-api editions.** The reports of al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah and the Muwatta that state a number of good or bad deeds, an erasure, a rank, a qirat, an equivalence, the Scale, the record or the reckoning are now passage records with a matn excerpt, sources and provenance (drafts until a human reads them). They also widen the Hasanat and Sayyi'at browsers.
- **25 new concept records for the ledger.** The article «حساب الحسنات والسيئات» with full prose in three languages, and 24 calculator rows, each explaining one counting text; the `concept` schema gains a `reckoning` block that holds the figure and the passages it is read from.

- **73 seerah pages for the ledger's seerah section.** Pages of Zad al-Ma'ad, al-Bayhaqi's and Abu Nu'aym's Dala'il al-Nubuwwa, al-Waqidi's Maghazi, Ibn Hisham's Sirah, Ibn Kathir's Sira, Uyun al-Athar and al-Rawd al-Unuf that state a number, a multiple, an erasure, a rank, the Scale or the record of deeds were found in the OCR'd books, read one by one, and filed as passage records with a page number and an excerpt of at most forty words (drafts until a human reads them). The seerah section of the page is no longer empty.
- **Hilyat al-Awliya, volume 10: Ruwaym, Abu Turab al-Nakhshabi and Muhammad ibn Ulayyan (microsd-books batch 17).** Ruwaym ibn Ahmad (notice 574) gained a trilingual "In Hilyat al-Awliya" section built around his own treatise on why seekers go wrong: hurrying to a rank before its time and neglecting piety. Abu Turab al-Nakhshabi (462), the transmitter of Hatim al-Asamm's teaching who died in the desert between Mecca and Medina, and Muhammad ibn Ulayyan al-Nasawi (649) now have draft pages. Every paragraph cites volume and page.

### Tests
- The feature-export test now covers the ledger: detection by corpus and kind, a calculator row, the gated false positives and a book harvested later.

### Data
- **Canon cornerstones, batch 7: Safavid Iran finished in three languages.** The importance-1 page held one sentence and a note that the data named no shahs and no events. It now gives the dynasty's history in about 1,400 words of English, with Arabic and Urdu versions: the Sufi order of Ardabil from Shaykh Safi al-Din to Junayd and Haydar, the boy Isma'il's entry into Tabriz in 907/1501 and his making Twelver Shi'ism the religion of the state, the defeat at Chaldiran and what it did to him, Tahmasp's fifty-two years between Uzbeks and Ottomans and the Treaty of Amasya, 'Abbas I's standing army, his new Isfahan and the expulsion of the Portuguese from Hormuz, and the three causes the encyclopaedia gives for the decline that ended with the Afghan capture of Isfahan in 1135/1722. Written from section I of the Encyclopaedia of Islam article (2nd edition, vol. 8 pp. 820-826), each fact cited to the page read. The page is academic history and says so: the encyclopaedia's judgements are attributed to it, and the Sunni account of the dynasty from al-Sallabi stays in the record's summary, unchanged. The Arabic and Urdu are draft translations by Claude Haiku 5.5 from the English.

### Data
- **Canon cornerstones, batch 8: the Seljuk Empire finished in three languages.** The importance-1 page held two Wikidata dates and a capital recorded as Nishapur. It now gives the dynasty's story in about 2,000 words of English, with Arabic and Urdu versions: the world of Buyid-ruled Baghdad and the Fatimid threat that the Seljuks entered, their Oghuz origins and defeat of the Ghaznavids at Dandanqan, Tughril's entry into Baghdad and his place beside the caliph, Alp Arslan and Malik Shah with Nizam al-Mulk and the true story of Manzikert as the encyclopaedia tells it, the succession wars after 485/1092, Sanjar's rise, his defeat by the Kara Khitay and capture by the Ghuzz, and what the dynasty changed — Turkish migration, the iqta', the pairing of caliph and sultan, the Persian language of administration. A closing section reports how historians have judged the Seljuks, including the Turkish nationalist and earlier European views. Written from sections I, II and III.1 of the Encyclopaedia of Islam article (2nd edition, vol. 8 pp. 1002-1009), each fact cited to the page read and linked to about thirty records already held. The Kirman, Syrian and Rum branches, administration, art and literature are left for later passes. The Arabic and Urdu are draft translations by Claude Haiku 5.5.

### Data
- **Omar Abdelkafy's «البيوت الآمنة» (Safe Homes) series: a new lecture-series page, episodes 1 to 3, in three languages.** The series is a weekly programme from the Dubai channel on building the Muslim home. Episode 1 covers good choice of a spouse (the Qur'anic stories of Musa in Madyan and of the Prophet's marriages, istikhara, and religion and character as the measure), episode 2 the five rulings on marriage, parents' role and the limits between suitor and fiancee, and episode 3 the manners of the engagement, with the viewers' calls summarised. Every point cites the episode and timestamp; the lecturer's views on disputed matters are marked as his, 14 garbled or unsourced points carry `needs_source`, and the page is a draft pending a human read. Adds `work/albuyout-alamena` with 37 links to existing records.

- **Canon cornerstones, batch 9: ten records finished in three languages by ten parallel agents.** Tabriz, Shiraz, Edirne, Samarra, San'a', Mosul, Basra, Kufa, Tunis and the Battle of Hattin, all importance-1 records that were short stubs, now each carry a full account in English, Arabic and Urdu of roughly 1,200 to 2,700 words, with a three-language summary, each fact cited to the page of the Encyclopaedia of Islam (2nd edition) it was read on. Ten Claude Sonnet 5.5 agents each took one record and one source article under a fixed brief (own files only, nothing from memory, attribute the article's judgements, no parentheses in Arabic or Urdu); the citations and links were then counted and matched across the three languages for every record, and every link target was confirmed to exist. Where the scan of an article was damaged the pages say so and leave the passage out — most of the Almohad and Hafsid centuries of Tunis, two pages of Shiraz and three of Tabriz, the scholarly side of Kufa — rather than guessing. Sections the earlier pages held from other sources were kept: the Ibn al-Athir account of Hattin, al-Salabi's account of Tunis's founding, the early-sources section of Shiraz, the Yaqut text on Tabriz, and the learner-level sections for Basra, Mosul and Tunis. The Hattin page gives both dates the encyclopaedia offers, 4 and 5 July 1187, without choosing. The Arabic and Urdu are draft translations by Claude Sonnet 5.5.

## v1.21.0 — 2026-11-12 (release/uat: the Grand Tour run)
### Added
- **The Grand Tour, entered through the River of Time (`/ar/grand-tour/`, `/en/grand-tour/`).** One new section and one new link on the Arabic and English homepages. The threshold is the River of Time: fourteen Hijri centuries as one band that flows in reading direction, widest where the canon is densest, with the Tour's 42 stops surfacing on it in order; without JavaScript the same stops are a plain numbered list under century headings. Each stop is a room built from the record itself: its name and date, its wings, the lead section of its own prose with its citations, one line counted from the graph (relations arriving at the record, records linked to it, pathways through it), the next stop, and the record's own strongest relations as side doors. A ribbon of centuries fills as the visitor walks. The completion room draws the route on the graph, states how many records hang directly off the path (counted at build time) and opens doors to the nine wings and the graph explorer. The manifest, `tour/grand-tour.yaml`, is an ordered list of record ids and nothing else; every stop is a cornerstone, and `scripts/fable/o02_tour_coverage.py` proves from the manifest that the stops span all nine wings and all fourteen centuries. No `/ur/` page is built and no existing page, layout or stylesheet changes; new strings are in `ar.yaml`, `en.yaml` and `ur.yaml` under one new key.

### Fixed
- **A unit test the Grand Tour broke is repaired: the education reading list now says the conquest of Mecca has a Brief.** When the Tour's narratives were finished, the Arabic page of `event/conquest-of-mecca` gained a `## موجز` heading so that its opening paragraphs form a lead. The approved list of 100 records for leveled reading (`edu/leveled-100.yaml`) records, for each record, whether its Arabic page already has that Brief section, and a test keeps the list and the pages in step; the list still said no. The flag is now true and the list's own total reads 95, not 94. The selection the founder approved on 23 October is unchanged: one derived flag and one count. The mission never ran the full test suite (its brief set two other gates), so this was found only when the validation run of the merge onto `release/uat` failed, and that failure also made the release branch's build cancel itself.
- **The UAT release branch builds again: main's repair to the page check is brought over.** Every build of `release/uat` failed at the last step, before and after the Grand Tour was merged onto it, on three pages: the changelog in Arabic, English and Urdu. The changelog prints these release notes word for word, an older note quotes the internal source marker as code, and the post-build check read that quotation as a leaked marker. Main fixed the check in its v1.18.1 (commit `96c90186fb`, pull request #6035): text inside a code element is no longer tested, and a marker that really leaks into a page is still caught, because it arrives as plain text. This is the same change, cherry-picked, so the release branch can be built and released to UAT. Nothing a visitor sees changes.
- **Grand Tour, after a second fresh look at its screenshots: the Arabic arrows point forward again, and the river's edge fades.** A second reviewer, who had not seen the first round, looked for each of the 50 earlier defects on the re-captured screenshots (22 gone, 13 still there, 15 changed) and listed 12 new ones, none major. Four are fixed here. In Arabic the arrow on the homepage's Grand Tour button and the arrows after the nine wing names in the completion room pointed right, back at their own label: the site's mirroring rule is a transform, which a browser does not apply to an inline box, so these arrows now get a box of their own and point left, the reading direction. The fade at the far end of the river was drawn underneath the stop cards, so cards were still cut hard at the edge; it now sits above them and is wider. On a phone the ribbon of centuries is two rows whose columns now line up. The button on the Arabic homepage has a little more room under the headline. Everything else the second round listed is in the defect register with the reason it stands. Not deployed.
- **Cross-record contradiction sweep, after its own re-check: 130 found, 38 fixed from already-cited sources, 84 registered with their evidence, 8 read and found consistent.** A fresh-context verifier then attacked the 44 corrections first claimed. It found two wrong (a birth year renamed a death year on a page that says nothing of the death; a ruler attached to a revolt he reigned through for ten weeks) and three resting on nothing the event itself cites: those five were reverted and their findings re-opened. A sixth was quiet only because the event it concerns is misdated in its own record; it is registered as hidden, not fixed. The verifier also showed the detectors could not see a date written only in the Hijri calendar; taught to read one, they raised eight more findings, all registered. The first count, kept here as it was written:
- **Cross-record contradiction sweep: 122 found, 44 fixed from already-cited sources, 70 registered with their evidence, 8 read and found consistent.** The detectors in `scripts/fable/contradictions.ts` compare records with each other: a person in an event after death or before birth, an event placed in the reign of a ruler dead or unborn, a child older than a parent, a one-way relation written both ways, a page that gives a different death year from the person's own record. Every finding was read by an adjudicator against the records and their cited sources. Forty-four are corrected, each from a source the edited record already cited: one unsourced death year on the Cairo caliph al-Mu'tadid (1341, where his own cited page says Jumada I 763 AH) had been putting 25 events of his caliphate after his death; al-Safadi was linked to the wrong Ibn Sayyid al-Nas, a grandfather who died 37 years before the student was born; five events of the last Almohad years pointed at a caliph strangled forty years earlier; a father was written as his own son's child. Seventy stand in the register because the cited sources cannot settle them, most of them dates from an earlier enrichment pass that the record's own source does not carry, where the only fix would be a removal: those are proposed to the founder, not enacted. Nothing was deleted and no source was added. The whole register, entry by entry, is `docs/fable-run/CONTRADICTIONS.md`; `scripts/fable/o05_contradictions.ts` fails if any finding is unaccounted for.

### Fixed
- **What the run's own verifiers caught in the Tour's narratives, and what was done (two commits: verifier A, then B and C).** Three agents with no part in the writing read all 730 sentences of the 41 new leads against the records and the cited pages. They found 5 errors, 56 weaker problems and 10 places where the Arabic and the English said different things. The errors: two phrases in the Kaaba lead that reproduced the wording of Qur'an verses, one of them added by the rewrite; a superlative about al-Ghazali in the museum's own voice, lifted from a biographer without his name; a sentence in the Qur'an record's lead that was false ("the museum does not type the text of the verses on its pages": three other records do); and a count of nights at al-Bukhari's death that the cited page gives differently. Fifty-seven findings are now fixed, always by removing, softening or naming the source, never by adding a fact: the pledge to Abu Bakr is told as Ibn al-Athir tells it, with those who held back; the account of Malcolm X's death is cut to what the record states without dispute; Baghdad's "seat of the caliphate until 1258" now carries the same article's Samarra years. Ten stand with their reasons, mostly page numbers that follow a scan or an edition not on hand. **The Qur'an record leaves the Tour**: its only cited source is the text itself, so nothing about revelation, compilation or transmission can be written from it, and its rewritten lead is reverted. The Tour has 40 stops. The reports and fix logs are in `docs/fable-run/verifier/`.

### Data
- **After the re-check, 17 of the 82 new relations were taken out again.** A verifier with no part in adding them re-read every one against its record: 65 are stated by the record with a citation; 16 said more than the sentence behind them (the Sulaymaniyya "patronized by" Suleiman, where the record says only that Sinan built it and it bears his name; a period "has part" an event that the record names only as its boundary; sharia "has part" the schools, where the record says schools differ within it), and 1 had no support. All 17 are removed and each evidence file says so. That puts five cornerstones back among the dead ends: the count goes from 29 at the baseline to 12, not to 7 as first reported. The first report, as it was written:
- **Twenty-two dead-end cornerstones now lead somewhere (evidence files first, then the 25 data files in one batch).** At the baseline 29 of the museum's cornerstones were dead ends in the graph: 23 had no relation to any record and 6 had exactly one, so a visitor who reached the Sulaymaniyya Mosque, the Blue Qur'an, the Thousand and One Nights or the concept of sharia could go nowhere. Each was read against its own cited text, and 82 relations were added to 22 of them, every one resting on a sentence the record already stated with a citation (the Sulaymaniyya is in Istanbul and was built by Sinan; the Taj Mahal is in Agra and is the burial place of Shah Jahan; the Battle of Nahrawan gains its place and nine participants). `docs/fable-run/relation-evidence/` holds one file per record with the sentence behind each relation and the names that were looked for and have no record. No relation was added on general knowledge and none uses the fallback `related_to`. Seven cornerstones could not be opened honestly and are left as they are: the Ardabil carpet (its two sentences name no place of weaving), three periods and three polities whose text names no other record or whose natural neighbours no registered predicate can reach.

- **The Grand Tour's narratives are finished: 41 cornerstone records now open with a full lead in Arabic and English (two batches: stops 1-21, then 22-41).** Each Tour stop shows the lead section of the record's own prose, so finishing the Tour meant finishing those records. Before this change the leads ran 11 to 127 words and 54 of the 84 had a sentence with no citation; now every lead is 150 to 250 words in both languages and every sentence carries a citation. Nothing was written from memory and no source was added: each fact was already in the record, or was read on the page of a book the record already cited, and `docs/fable-run/prose-evidence/` holds one file per record saying, sentence by sentence, where it was read and which citations were carried across without re-reading. The writers dropped uncited claims they could not source (for example "the most famous Islamic building in the world" on the Taj Mahal, cited to a database entry). Each record keeps its review state and gains a provenance note that the lead is AI text awaiting a human read. The Urdu files are untouched and now lag these leads. One stop could not be finished honestly, the contemporary era (its two cited books are not on hand and one predates the era), so it left the Tour and is entered in `docs/fable-run/GAP-REGISTER.md`; the Tour has 41 stops. `scripts/fable/o03_tour_prose.py` proves the length, the citations, the no-new-source rule and the publication bar.

### Fixed
- **The canon register's "not in the graph yet" list was wrong about 24 of its 31 subjects.** The list named Timur, Shah Jahan, Aurangzeb, Selim I, Hafiz, Sa'di, Ibn Jubayr, the Battle of Tours and others as having no record. A verifier with one job, to find each of them under another spelling, epithet or slug, found records for 24 (Timur is `person/timur-lang`, labelled only in Arabic; the Battle of Tours is `event/balat-al-shuhada`; Las Navas de Tolosa is `event/al-uqab-609`); seven of them were in the same file's canon list under a different slug. One (Luqman) is a stub; six are absent after the search: Firdawsi, Ibn Majid, the Battle of Plassey, aqida and usul al-fiqh as concepts, and the Maturidi school. `docs/canon.md` now lists only those, `docs/fable-run/ABSENCES.md` gives every spelling that was searched and every near miss that was opened and rejected, and `scripts/fable/o07_absences.py` re-runs the search and fails if any record matches a published spelling without an explanation. `scripts/fable/find_record.py` is the search tool: any record, under any spelling, Arabic or Latin.

### Tests
- **The Grand Tour mission's branch is merged onto the UAT release branch (`release/uat`), so the founder can release it to UAT and walk it before anything reaches main.** The merge conflicted in this file only: both sides had opened a `v1.17.0` block. The mission's block is this one, renumbered `v1.19.0`, because main already uses `v1.18.0` for other work that is not on this release branch; `docs/coverage.md` was regenerated from the merged tree. Checked on the merged tree before the merge was pushed: validator `0 errors`, cite-check `0 fail` on the Tour's 40 stops, and a production build of the homepage, the nine wing landings and the Tour. Nothing is deployed by this merge: the UAT release is the founder's to start. The seven pull requests to main (#6022 to #6033) are unchanged and still open.
- **The Grand Tour mission's ledger is closed: the final board, the numbers, the account of the run and the two-page public summary.** `docs/fable-run/VERIFICATION.md` holds the board as a program wrote it from the last run of every check at one commit: 11 of 13 rows green. Not green, and said so: twelve cornerstones are still dead ends and 7,114 of 18,699 published records are within three relations of a cornerstone (statement 4); on the live site 2 of 50 fixed searches return the canon record first, and the repair lies in a page this run was not allowed to change (statement 6). The same file lists what the run's own verifiers caught and where the run may still be wrong. `NUMBERS.md` is the before and after, each figure with the output it was read from; `SHOWCASE.md` tells the run for a public reader; `PUBLISH.md` is the two-page version; `PROPOSALS.md` gains four questions for the founder (a second source for the Qur'an's record, the visible defects on older pages and the one-line cause of the Arabic arrows that do not mirror, the release-notes block at merge, and whether fame may gate the canon). The third fresh look at the screenshots is recorded: the register ends at 135 visible defects, 23 fixed and confirmed gone, 112 standing with a reason. Main was merged into a scratch copy at its newest commit and the checks re-run there. Documentation and captured outputs only; nothing a visitor sees changes, and nothing is merged or deployed.
- **The Grand Tour's integration script now prepares the merged tree the way the site's own build does, and says whether it built.** Its first run against today's main left the homepages unbuilt: the script skipped the time browser's preparation step, whose output the homepage reads, so the no-JavaScript check ran on an incomplete build and failed for a reason that had nothing to do with the merge. The script now runs that step and writes a line of its own for the build (`build.out`), so a failed build can no longer hide inside another check's result. Tooling only; nothing a visitor sees changes.
- **The Grand Tour's 90 screenshots were taken again after the second round of fixes, for a third fresh look.** The committed set now shows the pages as they stand (captured at `e2c16d9083`), and the decisions file records what was done about every one of the 133 defects the reviewers have listed so far; a defect seen again in a changed form is recorded as standing, not as fixed. Evidence only; nothing a visitor sees changes in this entry.
- **Two more measurements for the Grand Tour's ledger: the wing pages after, and a second look at every fixed defect.** The probe that showed the live Living hall does not list the prayer, the pilgrimage, the fast or zakat (3 of 12 probed cornerstones listed on production) can now be pointed at this branch's built pages (`o13_production_wings.py --dist`), so the same twelve have an "after"; the board captures both. The vision oracle now reads a second-round review: a reviewer who looks for each earlier defect again on the re-captured screenshots, and the oracle fails if anything is called fixed that the second round still sees. Tooling only; nothing a visitor sees changes, and nothing is deployed.
- **The Grand Tour's board can re-run one statement without pretending about the rest.** `python3 scripts/fable/board.py --only 8,11` re-runs those oracles and reads every other row from its captured output, and only when that output was produced at the same commit; the ledger's self-check now also fails if any run on the board saw an uncommitted file. Tooling only; nothing a visitor sees changes.
- **The Grand Tour's ledger now checks itself, and the run's last measurements are repeatable by one command each.** A new oracle (`scripts/fable/o10_ledger.py`) reads the board in `docs/fable-run/VERIFICATION.md` and fails if any row is not, word for word, the last line of a captured run at the commit the board names, if any oracle is not a committed file, or if anything measured has changed since; the board runs it last and adds its row, so statements 10 and 13 are no longer taken on trust. The merge with main that the run tests itself against is now a script (`scripts/fable/integrate.sh`: a scratch copy, never committed, never this checkout), and the report of what main did meanwhile computes its claims from git instead of stating them. The reachability oracle can be pointed at a graph built from another commit (`--graph`), which is how its "before" was measured again at the true baseline (7,081 of 18,699 published records within three hops, not the 7,087 first printed, which was measured after the run had begun); the Tour's "before" was measured again the same way (1 of 80 leads in range, 50 with an uncited sentence). The vision pass has its register: `scripts/fable/defects.py` joins the reviewers' own tables with what was done about each defect, and the vision oracle refuses a defect with no decision. Nothing a visitor sees changes in this entry; nothing here is deployed.
- **Canon-first search is now a test, and production fails it.** `scripts/fable/search-queries.json` fixes 50 queries a visitor would type (25 Arabic, 25 English: Muhammad, Mecca, Baghdad, the Battle of Badr, Avicenna, Saladin, the Taj Mahal) with the canon record each must return first. `scripts/fable/o06_search.mjs` runs them through the site's own search page against any built site. On production today (the deploy of 10 November) 2 of 50 return the canon record first: a search for Mecca returns an event of 571 AH, a search for Muhammad returns the record of a tafsir edition. This branch changes nothing in the search path (the brief allows one new section and one link) and could not be built on the machine it was written on, so the test stands as a measurement of production and a proposal (P-5), not a fix.

### Changed
- **Main is merged into the UAT release branch, and every difference between the two is kept where it belongs.** `release/uat` held the Grand Tour mission; main had moved 61 commits on (new browsers, four canon batches, the rebuilt Place wing map). Five files conflicted. The canon script and its register: main and the mission had each corrected the same wrong list of missing subjects, main by deleting it and taking twelve of its subjects into the canon, the mission by replacing it with a verified list of the six that are really absent; the twelve are records the mission's verifier had found, so both stand (840 canon records, 271 cornerstones, the century floor, the verified list). The Delhi Sultanate: main's summaries from the Encyclopaedia of Islam, with the mission's wing and relation. These notes: every line of both sides, with this block on top as `v1.21.0`. `docs/coverage.md` was regenerated. Main's re-selection also promoted three cornerstones that sat in no wing; they received one by the mission's class rule, and all 40 Tour stops are still cornerstones. Checked on the merged tree: validator `0 errors`, the whole unit test suite (482 passed), cite-check `0 fail`, a production build of the homepage, wing landings and Tour, and the mission's checks, which stand as before except that 13 cornerstones are now dead ends, not 12. Nothing is deployed.
- **The Tour's pages revised after three reviewers looked at the screenshots (the screenshots themselves are re-captured from the revised pages in the commit that follows).** Ninety screenshots of the Tour, the homepage and the nine wing landings (Arabic and English; phone, tablet and desktop) were committed, and three reviewers who had not built the pages and did not see their source listed every visible defect: 121 in all, 44 of them on the Tour's own pages. What changed in answer: the river's stream now runs behind the stop cards and the band fades at the edge where it continues, so the stops read as standing on the river; its controls sit in one row with the slider beneath and go quiet at either end; the ribbon of centuries breaks into two readable rows on a phone, and its caption now says how far the walk has reached; a room's sources are numbered to match the footnotes, page references keep their order inside Arabic lines, and on a wide screen the counted line and the sources stand beside the narrative; the completion room says when its route drawing scrolls sideways, labels its lanes in readable ink and sets its nine wing doors three to a row; the homepage button is a pill under the headline, on the first screen, and wraps as one piece on a phone. Counts on the Tour no longer include the fallback relation `related_to` (the completion room's number is the stricter one), and a work whose own record names its author is now dated by that author. The 77 defects the reviewers found on existing pages are registered, not fixed: this run may not rework them. (The commit that added the screenshots carried no entry here; this is it.)
- **The completion room's route drawing no longer fails the accessibility scan.** The site's own standard (axe-core, WCAG A and AA) flagged the drawing: it was marked as one image while holding forty links. It is now a labelled group. `scripts/fable/o09_nojs.mjs` runs that scan on the Tour's pages in both languages, light and dark, with a run of the whole Tour with JavaScript disabled: the River as a plain list, every one of the 40 rooms reached in order by its own "next" link, the completion room's count equal to the one counted from the graph. The same run records a defect that predates the Tour and is not fixed here: with JavaScript disabled, the site's header menu is wider than a phone screen on every page.
- **The Grand Tour's script is now a plain file, and the homepage link no longer touches `/ur/`.** A byte-for-byte comparison of the homepage and the nine wing landings, built once with the baseline's site source and once with this branch's over the same data, caught two side effects of the first version. The Tour's script went through the site's bundler, which renamed the hashed script files that the Place wing's map loads; on a full build a rename like that can mean re-uploading every page that loads a bundled script. And the homepage link, written on its own line, left one extra space in the Urdu homepage. The script is now `site/public/shell/grand-tour.js`, a plain file beside `shell.js` and `entity.js` as the site's own rule asks, and the link sits on the line that already held the day cards. `scripts/fable/o08_unchanged.py` now proves the result: every compared page is byte-identical except the Arabic and English homepages, whose only difference is the one link.

- **Canon: a century floor.** The canon's class quotas rank within each class and never look at time, so a century could come out with no cornerstone; at this morning's baseline the 12th Hijri century (1101–1200 AH) had none. `scripts/report/canon.py` now checks every Hijri century from the 1st to the 14th after the quotas are filled and, where one is empty, raises the canon record anchored there that the museum's own graph leans on most (inbound relations, prose links, pathway appearances; the Wikipedia count plays no part). Today that raises one record, Sultan Ahmed III, to cornerstone (271 cornerstones, 824 canon records). A new `--floor-only` mode re-applies the rule and rewrites `docs/canon.md` without the network. Proposed to the founder as P-1 in `docs/fable-run/PROPOSALS.md`; why it matters: the Grand Tour that follows walks all fourteen centuries and each of its stops must be a cornerstone.

### Data
- **Every cornerstone now sits in a wing (two batches of 25).** At the baseline 48 of the 270 cornerstones had an empty `wings` list and appeared on no wing page: the Living Islam hall did not list the prayer, the pilgrimage, the fast or zakat; the Words hall did not list the Qur'an record, the Muwatta or the two Sahihs; no period or major polity stood in the Time hall. `scripts/fable/complete_wings.py` gives each the wing the plan assigns its class (period and polity to Time, practice to Living, work to Words, group to People) and prints the tally of existing tags it rests on. Three additions go beyond the class rule, each with its reason in the script: the contemporary era (Time, Today), Al-Azhar (adds Today, the plan's own example) and the Kiswa (adds Made; its own prose says it is woven today in Mecca). Only the `wings:` line changes and no wing is removed. Proposed to the founder as P-2.

### Tests
- **Oracles for the Tour's prose, reachability and the contradiction sweep, with their "before" runs.** `o03_tour_prose.py` checks each Tour stop's narrative in Arabic and English: 150 to 250 words, a citation on every sentence, no source the record did not already cite at the baseline, the publication bar (`cite-check`). `o04_reachability.py` measures dead-end cornerstones and the hop distance from every published record to its nearest cornerstone, and prints the whole distribution. `contradictions.ts` detects cross-record contradictions (a person in an event after death or before birth, an event placed in the reign of a dead or unborn ruler, a child older than a parent, a one-way relation written both ways, prose that gives a different death year from the person's own record) and `o05_contradictions.ts` holds every finding to a register. Measured before any repair: 83 of 84 Tour leads outside the length range; 29 dead-end cornerstones; 7,087 of 18,699 published records within three hops of a cornerstone; 122 cross-record contradictions, all now entered in `docs/fable-run/CONTRADICTIONS.md` with their evidence. The briefs given to the delegated writers are in `docs/fable-run/briefs/`.

- **Oracles for the canon and the baseline.** `scripts/fable/o00_baseline.py` measures the headline counts of a graph artifact (records, relations, draft and published, cornerstones, records with no relation) and proves the mission branch still stands on its frozen baseline with no merge from a moving `main`. `scripts/fable/o01_canon.py` proves the canon from the repository alone, with no network: the field exists, 824 records carry it and 271 are cornerstones, every record passes the structural floor or is a named editorial include (315 qualify with the Wikipedia count set to zero, 489 pass the floor and need it, 20 are includes), the canon script writes nothing to a record but its `importance` line, the register matches the data, every Hijri century from the 1st to the 14th holds a cornerstone and every cornerstone sits in a wing. Each oracle ends with `RESULT: GREEN` or `RESULT: NOT-GREEN`; the captured output of the baseline run is in `docs/fable-run/oracle-output/`. The first captured runs on the branch (baseline, canon, Tour coverage) are there too, each headed by the commit and graph artifact it measured.

## v1.21.0 — 2026-11-11
### Added
- **Sacred Places Browser: متصفح الأماكن المقدسة والهامة وذات القيمة في الإسلام (`/{lang}/places/`).** A new browser over the one graph listing every place of sanctity, importance and value in Islam the museum's sources mention — the three sanctuaries (Mecca, Medina, Jerusalem and their mosques), the stations of the hajj and the miqats, the sites of the seerah and the campaigns, the towns, lands and mountains the Qur'an names, other venerated sites, and every place or building a passage names. Membership is graph membership: `places-browser`-tagged `place` and `building` records plus every record with a `mentioned_in` edge from a passage, so a place named in a book harvested later appears automatically. Six sanctity sections on the home page (sanctuaries, hajj, seerah, quran, sacred, mentioned) with trilingual cards showing per-corpus mention counts; subject pages at `/{lang}/places/<slug>/` group each place's mentions into Qur'an ayahs (frozen Tanzil text by reference), Sunnah reports, seerah reports and other books. `/api/v1/places.json`, an Explore-menu entry and landing card, trilingual ar/en/ur pages, plan `docs/plan/49-places-browser.md`, acceptance spec `docs/engineering/37-places-browser-requirements.md` (`PLACE-R..`), lane `places`. Records are draft until a human reads them.

### Fixed
- **Place wing map: five corrections after review (`/{lang}/place/`).** A place lit by a record dated to one year is no longer lit the year after (a record of 624 kept its place bright in 625). The page, its script, its styles and the data it fetches now always come from the same build (each is asked for by a fingerprint of its content), so a returning reader cannot meet today's page with yesterday's places or yesterday's script. A place can be found by its name in any of the three languages from any of them ("Konya" on the Urdu page). While the years run, the panel's list and the names round a place follow the year, and the year label names the era of the region in view, not the one before it. The change-gate label for the map is corrected to `submission-impacting`; the row proposed for the claims register is in `docs/site/place-map-review.md`.
- **Main build repaired: the Sacred Places Browser's landing page could not be built.** `/{lang}/places/` imported the places detector from one folder too high (`../../../../scripts/places`), so every build of `main` and of every open pull request failed at that page. The import now points at the repository's `scripts/` folder.

### Data
- **Omar Abdelkafy's Ramadan series on the servants of the Most Merciful: lessons 10 to 13.** `work/silsilat-ebadu-al-rahman` gains four more lessons in Arabic, English and Urdu, each point cited to the recording by episode and timestamp. Lesson 10 reads "nor do they commit fornication" as a call to close the ways to it: making marriage easy as the Companions did, lowering the gaze, the young man the Prophet reasoned with instead of rebuking, and the lecturer's own views on media, schooling and women's work, each marked as his view. Lesson 11 turns to the outcome the verses threaten and to the six rights of a Muslim as he lists them; lesson 12 to the exception for those who repent, with the rule "emptying before adorning"; lesson 13, which survives in the archive only as a five-minute fragment, opens the attribute of not bearing false witness. Eight new `about` links (verses 25:69, 25:70 and 25:72, repentance, lowering the gaze, marriage and dowry); four points carry `needs_source`.

- **Omar Abdelkafy's Ramadan series on the servants of the Most Merciful: lessons 6 to 9.** `work/silsilat-ebadu-al-rahman` gains four more lessons in Arabic, English and Urdu, each point cited to the recording by episode and timestamp. Lesson 6 covers the prayer to be spared Hell and the manners of supplication (Umar asking Hudhayfa whether he was on the list of hypocrites; why those promised Paradise feared most; al-Shafi'i's "physician of heaven"). Lesson 7 is the middle course in spending: waste measured against one's means, the miser, "servants of Ramadan" against servants of the Most Merciful, and moderation in emotions as well as money. Lesson 8 is pure monotheism: "the word of unity and the unity of the word", one Book and one qibla, the loaf of bread as a lesson in providence, and Musa who went for a firebrand and came back with a message; it also records that the programme aired on the Sharjah satellite channel. Lesson 9 is the sanctity of life and what the lecturer calls "moral killing". Nineteen new `about` links; five points carry `needs_source`. Because lessons 9 onward include the lecturer's own opinions on disputed matters, the record is now labelled `sensitivity: contested` and each such point is marked as his view (decision record in `docs/decisions/records/`).

- **Omar Abdelkafy's Ramadan series on the servants of the Most Merciful: lessons 3 to 5.** `work/silsilat-ebadu-al-rahman` gains three more of its twenty-eight lessons in Arabic, English and Urdu, each point cited to the recording by episode and timestamp. Lesson 3 completes humility with affection (mawadda): what blocks it — envy, pride, a hard heart, miserliness — the "brothers of purity", seeking seventy excuses for a brother, and the saying he attributes to Ja'far al-Sadiq on a year's affection becoming kinship. Lesson 4 reads "they say: peace" as forbearance with the ignorant: Ibrahim's parting peace to his father, three kinds of people who wrong you, spreading the greeting, God's forbearance toward those who deny Him, and a call to produce rather than only consume. Lesson 5 opens the night prayer: Ata ibn Abi Rabah's household dividing the night, a graded half-hour-before-dawn programme for the whole year, and al-Hasan al-Basri on the light of those alone with God at night. Sixteen new `about` links (verses 25:63–64, forbearance, the night prayer, envy, sincerity and others) put the series on those pages; four points whose wording or attribution could not be confirmed from the transcript carry `needs_source`.
- **Four places the map could not draw now have real positions.** Fourteen place records carried the placeholder coordinates `[0, 0]`, a point in the Gulf of Guinea, left by an enrichment run wherever the Wikidata item had no coordinates; the Place wing map rightly kept them off. Four of them are real places whose position a registered source gives, and they now carry it: the villages of Buhut in the Nile Delta and Samail in Oman and the upland of Jabal Amil in southern Lebanon from GeoNames, and Baghdad's Wardiyya cemetery (seventeen people in the museum are buried there) at the mosque of Shaykh Umar al-Suhrawardi, which stands inside it. Each has its region tag in place of "Global", and each reading is recorded in the authenticity ledger with the revision read. The other eighteen records the map review listed are unchanged: four real sites with no citable position, six places of the geographers' marvels that cannot be located, and eight records that are not places at all (four dynasties, a period, two institutions and Wikidata's "unknown"). They are written up for the founder, with a recommendation for each, in `docs/delegation/place-coordinates-held-proposal.md`; the one judgment call made is decision record dec-20261112-239.

- **Sacred Places Browser, wave 1: the membership tagged and the Qur'an's named places linked.** Sixty-two existing `place` and `building` records — the three sanctuaries and their mosques, the hajj stations and miqats, the seerah sites and Medina environs, the lands the Qur'an names and other venerated sites — gained `places-browser` and `places-<section>` tags in place, so the browser's sanctity sections list them. Thirty-eight `mentions` edges were added to Tanzil ayah records for places named in the verse text itself (Bakka, the Sacred Mosque, Safa-adjacent Muzdalifa, Badr, Hunayn, Yathrib, Quba's mosque, al-Aqsa, Madyan, Babylon, Iram, al-Judi, al-Ahqaf, al-Hijr, Saba's Yemen, al-Sham, Tur Sina, Misr, and Mecca's oaths), each cited to `source/tanzil-quran`. Missing trilingual prose for `building/al-haram-al-sharif` was written in Arabic, English and Urdu, draft until a human reads it.
- **Hilyat al-Awliya, volume 10: six Sufi notices read from the scan (microsd-books batch 14).** Abu Yazid al-Bistami (notice 458), al-Shibli (646) and Ibn al-A'rabi (647) gained a trilingual "In Hilyat al-Awliya" section each, and three shaykhs who had no page now have one: Ahmad ibn Khidruya al-Balkhi (459), Ibrahim al-Harawi known as Sitanba (460) and Abu Amr al-Zajjaji (648). Readers get Abu Yazid's sayings on self-criticism and his refusal to treat marvels as proof of sainthood, Abu Nu'aym's warning that a hadith was falsely attached to him, al-Shibli's hospital, deathbed and Ibn Mujahid stories, and Umm Ali's visit to Abu Yazid. Every paragraph cites volume and page; the three new pages are drafts awaiting a human read, and none records a faith value because the notices state none (decision dec-20261112-237).
- **Hilyat al-Awliya, volume 10: al-Sari al-Saqati, Amr al-Makki, Ibn Khafif and four new pages (microsd-books batch 15).** Al-Sari al-Saqati (notice 469), Amr ibn Uthman al-Makki (573) and Ibn Khafif (660) gained a trilingual "In Hilyat al-Awliya" section each: al-Sari's scruple over food and his exchanges with al-Junayd, Amr's dictated answer on God's oneness and his "discipline of the self", and Ibn Khafif's definitions and his teaching on remembrance. The page for the book itself now explains the three places in volume ten where Abu Nu'aym states his method, ending with the ascetics of Isfahan. New draft pages: Dawud al-Balkhi (461), Ali ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Ghada'iri (644), Abu Bakr ibn Abi Sa'dan (650). Every paragraph cites volume and page; none of the new pages records a faith value.
- **Hilyat al-Awliya, volume 9: Dhu al-Nun, Mansur ibn Ammar and four frontier ascetics (microsd-books batch 16).** Dhu al-Nun al-Misri (notice 456, opening pages) and Mansur ibn Ammar (455) gained a trilingual "In Hilyat al-Awliya" section each: Dhu al-Nun's prayers, his letter to a sick friend and his audience with al-Mutawakkil; Mansur's reply to Bishr al-Marisi on the Qur'an, his meeting with Sufyan ibn Uyayna and the story of the young man of Kufa. New draft pages for four ascetics the museum did not yet have: Abu Abd Allah al-Saji (450), Ali ibn Bakkar of al-Massisa (452), al-Qasim ibn Uthman al-Ju'i (453) and Mada' ibn Isa (454). Every paragraph cites volume and page, and the pages say plainly where the notice gives no date.


- **المكاتبات browser, books waves 2–8: companions, biography, geography, chancery, usul, creeds, Quran sciences, fiqh, aqeedah, hadith and tafsir shelves mined (~1,280 new draft passages).** The harvest library's non-seerah shelves were scanned with the calibrated mukatabat detector and strong-signal triage; after dropping generic document, scripture, author-book and isnad noise, **~960 new `passage` records** were written across nine shelves — adab & zuhd (41), usul (36), creed reports (19), hadith sciences (27), Quran sciences (33), fiqh (108), aqeedah (80), hadith collections (350) and tafsir (266) — plus the companions/biography cluster (258: sahaba 193, sahabiyat 22, tabaqat 14, rijal 10, khutab 3, shamail 5, travel 11) and geography (65). Highlights: Ibn Hisham's letter to Heraclius preserved in *al-Isaba*, *al-Isti'ab*, *Usd al-Ghaba* and *Marifat al-Sahaba*; caliphal correspondence in *al-Khitat* (14), *Ahsan al-Taqasim* and *Nuzhat al-Mushtaq*; the kings' letters in Sahihayn commentaries and musnads (*Musannaf* Abd al-Razzaq 19, Ibn Abi Shayba 10, Musnad Ahmad 16, Bayhaqi's Sunan al-Kubra 30); and correspondence reports inside tafsir (*Ibn Kathir* 27, *al-Tabari* 23, *al-Shawkani* 29, *al-Tantawi* 27). Fifteen new `work` records and five new `source` records were created where the graph lacked them (Kandahlawi's *Hayat al-Sahaba*, al-Azraqi's *Akhbar Makkah*, al-Maqrizi's *al-Khitat*, Ibn Uthaymin's sermons, *Fi Zilal al-Quran*, *Jami' al-Bayan*, the two Musannafs, Bayhaqi's Sunan al-Kubra edition, Kahhala's *A'lam al-Nisa'*), each cited to its scanned title page. Every record is a ≤40-word excerpt with `mentions` edges to `concept/al-mukatabat` and detected parties, tagged `mukatabat-browser`, draft pending human review.
### Data
- **Canon cornerstones, batch 6: the Timurid Empire finished in three languages.** The importance-1 page held two Wikidata dates and a note that a second source was needed. It now tells the dynasty's history in about 1,150 words of English, with Arabic and Urdu versions: Timur's rise in the Ulus Chaghatay and his campaigns from the Golden Horde to Delhi and Ankara, Shah Rukh's reunion of the realm and Ulugh Beg at Samarqand, the wars after 850/1447 and the murder of Ulugh Beg, Abu Sa'id, the Herat of Sultan Husayn Bayqara, and the Uzbek conquest of 913/1507 that sent Babur to Kabul — then how the state was run through two sets of scribes, how tax-free grants and endowments ate away its revenue, and the world of Jami, Nawa'i and the Naqshbandiyya. Written from the history section of the Encyclopaedia of Islam article (2nd edition, vol. 10 pp. 538-540), each fact cited to the page read and linked to some thirty records already held. The article's sections on literature, art and architecture are left for later.
- **The iDAI.gazetteer link reaches fifty-nine cities: the Maghreb, al-Andalus, Iran and Arabia.** A third verified batch adds the German Archaeological Institute's gazetteer id to twenty-five more place records, so each page can point a reader to a scholarly anchor for where the town is and what it has been called: Annaba, Béjaïa, Biskra, Oujda, Sétif, Sfax, Sousse, Gabès, Oran and Tétouan; Almería, Cartagena, Toledo, Tortosa, Úbeda and Uclés; Isfahan, Shiraz, Tabriz, Hamadan, Tustar and Urmia; Aden, Zabid and Tayma. Every link was checked against the live gazetteer record before it was written — the name, the populated-place type, the Arabic name where the gazetteer gives one, and coordinates within 1.2 km of the museum's own. Candidates that failed a check were left unlinked and logged with the reason in the lane ledger (for example Asilah, where the gazetteer entry is the ancient site of Zilil, and Casablanca, whose entry carries no place type).

## v1.20.0 — 2026-11-12
### Added
- **Nubuwat Browser: متصفح النبؤات وأسرار القرآن ومعجزاته (`/{lang}/nubuwat/`).** A new browser over the one graph listing every prophecy of the Prophet, every proof of prophethood, every secret and marvel of the Qur'an, every miracle of the Prophet, every report of unseen knowledge and every eschatological prediction the museum's sources carry — the Qur'anic announcements, the «من بعدي» reports of the two Sahihs, the Muwatta and the Sunan, the proofs-of-prophethood genre, the inimitability and secrets literature, the seerah and history books, and the stories and quotations of the Companions and Successors. Passages are found at build time by a guarded lexicon in `scripts/nubuwat.ts` in seven topic families — prophethood & proofs, prophecies, miracles of the Prophet, the Qur'an's inimitability, its secrets, unseen knowledge and signs of the Hour — while bare nature vocabulary and ambiguous forms count only beside their domain collocations, and verified false positives are excluded by id. About 1,160 passages detected across the Qur'an, Sunnah and books plus curated `nubuwat-browser` records, grouped into five sections (quran, sunnah, seerah, books, curated) with topic chips, `/api/v1/nubuwat.json`, an Explore-menu and landing card, trilingual ar/en/ur pages, and the acceptance spec `docs/engineering/36-nubuwat-browser-requirements.md` (`NUB-R..`) for production validation. Plan `docs/plan/48-nubuwat-browser.md`; lane `nubuwat`. A book harvested later brings its prophecies and marvels here automatically once its passage records land. Records are draft until a human reads them.

### Removed
- **The old Place wing map component is out of the build.** The map was rebuilt as a plain script in v1.18.3, and the Svelte component it replaced (`MapViewer.svelte`) was kept for one release as an unused build entry so that the rebuild would not re-upload the whole site. It is now deleted, with the three packages only it used (`motion`, `@floating-ui/dom`, `@lucide/svelte`) and the map strings only it read (19 strings and eight class names, in the three languages). Nothing a reader sees changes. **Deploy note: this change renames the script files the depth dial loads, so it re-uploads every entity page (about 160,000); it is labelled `rewrites-all-pages` for the weekly batch.** The measured list of renamed files and changed pages is in `docs/site/place-map-review.md`.

### Performance
- **Every entity page loads less script, and every wing page is 11 KB lighter.** With the old map gone, the shared script files no longer carry the Svelte runtime code that only it needed: the depth dial on an entity page loads 4 files and 38.9 KB (16.0 KB compressed) instead of 7 files and 53.4 KB (22.1 KB compressed). The nine wing pages no longer carry the old map's 11 KB of styles in their HTML, and the site ships 143 KB less script in all.

### Data
- **Canon cornerstones, batch 3: the Delhi Sultanate finished in three languages.** The importance-1 page for the chief Muslim kingdom of northern India held two sentences from Wikidata and a note asking for a second source. It now tells the whole span in about 1,700 words of English, with Arabic and Urdu versions: the Ghurid conquests and the two battles of Tarain, Aybak and Iltutmish, Raziyya and Balban, 'Ala' al-Din Khalji's defence against the Mongols and his southern campaigns, Muhammad ibn Tughluq's second capital and twenty-two rebellions, Timur's sack of Delhi, the Sayyids and Lodis, Panipat, and the Sur restoration — then how the sultans dealt with their Hindu subjects and how the state was run and paid for. Written from P. Hardy's article in the Encyclopaedia of Islam (2nd edition, vol. 2 pp. 280-287), each fact cited to the page read, with links to some forty records already in the museum. Hardy's own judgements are given as his: on whether the sultans levied the jizya as a separate tax he doubts it, and the page says, as he does, that the opposite view is the more usual one. The record's start and end dates keep their Wikidata values, with the encyclopaedia's different reckoning added as a cited note.

- **Nubuwat Browser data wave: the dalā'il books mined and the curated section populated.** Eleven new draft passage records mined page-by-page from the two proofs-of-prophethood works already on the harvest shelf — six from al-Bayhaqi's *Dalā'il al-Nubuwwa* (the moon's splitting, water from between the fingers at al-Hudaybiyya, the pebbles' glorification, the palm trunk's lament, the prophets seen on the Night Journey, and the edition's discussion of the chest-opening) and five from Abu Nu'aym's *Dalā'il al-Nubuwwa* (the moon's splitting on three authorities, Quraysh's mission of Utba ibn Rabi'a, water gushing on journey and at home, Ja'far's defence before the Negus, and the letter to Chosroes and its tearing) — each with its chapter or hadith reference, printed page, scanned-edition provenance and a matn excerpt of at most forty words, all draft until a human reads them. Twenty-five existing records — the prophethood, miracle, inimitability and eschatology concepts, the prophethood-related events and the two dalā'il works themselves — gained `nubuwat-browser` tags in place with `nubuwat-<topic>` chips, so the browser's curated section now lists them alongside the detected passages; existing `miracles-browser` tags are preserved. Both works carry `genre: [sira]`, so their passages land in the seerah section of `/{lang}/nubuwat/` and `/api/v1/nubuwat.json`.
- **Canon cornerstones, batch 4: Granada finished in three languages.** The importance-1 page for Granada held two sentences and a note that nothing had been checked against a reference work. It now tells the city's story in about 1,150 words of English, with Arabic and Urdu versions: Roman and early Muslim Elvira and the walled village once called Granada of the Jews, why the Zirids moved their capital there (in the words of their last amir's memoirs), the Almoravid and Almohad governors and the night relief of the besieged citadel, Ibn al-Ahmar's founding of the Nasrid state and his first works on the Alhambra, the closed and faithful Nasrid capital, and what still stands in the city — the Zirid walls and gates, the Banuelo bath, the madrasa's prayer hall, the Corral del Carbon. Written from the Encyclopaedia of Islam (2nd edition, vol. 2 pp. 1054-1058), each fact cited to the page read, with three sourced relations. Several dates the scan misprints (the Ibn Hamushk attack, Ibn Hud's death) were left out rather than corrected by guess.


### Data
- **Canon cornerstones, batch 5: the Almohad Caliphate finished in three languages.** The importance-1 page held two dates from Wikidata and a note asking for a history book. It now covers the whole story in about 1,500 words of English, with Arabic and Urdu versions: Ibn Tumart's movement among the Masmuda at Tinmal, 'Abd al-Mu'min's twenty-year conquest of Morocco and his rapid march east to Tripoli, the three great caliphs, Alarcos and Las Navas de Tolosa, the break-up into Hafsid, Zayyanid and Marinid states, and then how the empire was governed, why Maliki law outlasted the new doctrine, the square dirham, the treatment of Christians and Jews, the workshops of Fez and the treaties with Pisa and Marseilles, Ibn Tufayl and Ibn Rushd at court, and the plain, vast mosques. Written from M. Shatzmiller's article in the Encyclopaedia of Islam (2nd edition, vol. 7 pp. 855-860), each fact cited to the page read and linked to some forty records already held. The harsh passages — the brutality of the conquest, the choice of conversion or death put to the Jews — are reported as the article reports them, with its sources named. The record's dates keep their Wikidata values, with the encyclopaedia's reckoning added as cited notes.

You can drag, zoom with the wheel, a pinch or a double click, and move with the keyboard; find a place by name in Arabic, English or Urdu; open a region, a place, then a person or event tied to it, with a trail to go back and a link that returns to the same place (`#p=mecca`). ## v1.18.2 — 2026-11-12
### Fixed
- **Main build repaired: the `needs_source` page check no longer flags marker syntax quoted inside `<code>`.** The v1.15.2 release note quotes the exact marker forms — `(needs_source)` and `(needs_source: …)` written as code — and the changelog renders CANARY.md verbatim, so the literal marker landed inside `<code>` on all three language changelog pages and `check:site` failed the build. The check now strips `<code>…</code>` elements before testing: a genuinely leaked marker still renders as page text — every prose path runs `stripNeedsSource` before markdown rendering, so a marker can never legitimately arrive inside `<code>` — while release notes and docs quoting the syntax stay publishable.

### Data
- **Canon cornerstones, batch 1: Lahore and Mimar Sinan finished in three languages.** The first two importance-1 records were rewritten in full from the Encyclopaedia of Islam (2nd edition), each fact cited to the volume and page read. Lahore went from a two-line placeholder that asked for a historical source to a full account: the first mention of 372/982, the Ghaznavid capital, the Delhi sultans and the Mongol sack of 639/1241, the Mughal city of Akbar, Jahangir and Shah Jahan, the Afghan, Sikh and British periods, then the Fort, the mosques, the tombs and the gardens — with links to thirty related records and three new sourced relations. Mimar Sinan had no prose at all; his page now covers his recruitment in the devshirme, the 477 buildings the sixteenth-century lists give him and why the article's author doubts he oversaw them all, the Shehzade, Suleymaniye and Selimiye, four smaller works, and six `built` edges to mosques already in the museum. Both enter as AI drafts with provenance; where the OCR of the source dropped a line (the opening of the Selimiye paragraph) the dates were left out rather than guessed.
- **Canon register corrected.** The first register listed subjects "not in the graph yet" that in fact exist under other names (Timur, Selim I, Shah Jahan, Aurangzeb and others); the check matched slugs, not labels. The list is removed, and twelve real omissions join the canon as editorial includes — Timur, Usman dan Fodio, Shah Wali Allah, Hafiz, al-Junayd, the prophets Idris and Hud, the Battle of the Zab, Balat al-Shuhada, the Abbasid da'wa in Khurasan, the Ash'ari school and the Mahdi. The canon is now 840 records (270 at importance 1); sixteen others changed level as the graph grew.

### Data
- **Canon cornerstones, batch 2: Muhammad Iqbal and Konya finished in three languages.** Both importance-1 pages were one-line stubs. Iqbal's page (his English summary read only "Muhammad Iqbal.") now follows his education in Lahore, Cambridge and Munich, the turn to Muslim revival, each of his books from the Asrar-i khudi to the Armaghan-i Hijaz, the Allahabad statement of 1930, and A. Schimmel's account of his thought on the self, love, destiny and the Qur'an, with her critical remarks attributed to her by name. Konya's page now runs from the Byzantine base the Arab raids avoided, through the Seljuk capital and its townspeople, the Mongol-era decline, the Karamanids and the Ottoman annexation of 880/1475, to the Alaeddin mosque, the shrine of Rumi and the three great madrasas, linking the eight Konya events and four buildings the museum already held. Written from the Encyclopaedia of Islam (2nd edition), vol. 3 pp. 1090-1092 and vol. 5.1 pp. 287-290, every fact cited to the page read; new sourced relations on both records. One garbled sentence in the source scan (on the Karamanids in 713/1313) was left out rather than guessed.
