## v1.17.0 — 2026-11-11
### Changed
- **Canon: a century floor.** The canon's class quotas rank within each class and never look at time, so a century could come out with no cornerstone; at this morning's baseline the 12th Hijri century (1101–1200 AH) had none. `scripts/report/canon.py` now checks every Hijri century from the 1st to the 14th after the quotas are filled and, where one is empty, raises the canon record anchored there that the museum's own graph leans on most (inbound relations, prose links, pathway appearances; the Wikipedia count plays no part). Today that raises one record, Sultan Ahmed III, to cornerstone (271 cornerstones, 824 canon records). A new `--floor-only` mode re-applies the rule and rewrites `docs/canon.md` without the network. Proposed to the founder as P-1 in `docs/fable-run/PROPOSALS.md`; why it matters: the Grand Tour that follows walks all fourteen centuries and each of its stops must be a cornerstone.

- **UAT can now be released from a release branch as well as from main.** `build.yml` also builds pushes to `release/**`; `deploy-uat.yml` takes a `source_branch` input (default `main`) naming the branch the deployed build must come from, and the shared deploy procedure (`deploy-env.yml`) resolves the latest successful build of that branch and accepts a build only from it. Production is untouched and doubly guarded: `deploy.yml` passes no source branch, and the shared procedure refuses any non-main source for the production environment outright. This lets work such as the Fable 5.2 run be merged to a release branch (e.g. `release/uat`), deployed to UAT and iterated there without main moving. Deployment remains manual and the founder's alone.

### Data
- **Every cornerstone now sits in a wing (two batches of 25).** At the baseline 48 of the 270 cornerstones had an empty `wings` list and appeared on no wing page: the Living Islam hall did not list the prayer, the pilgrimage, the fast or zakat; the Words hall did not list the Qur'an record, the Muwatta or the two Sahihs; no period or major polity stood in the Time hall. `scripts/fable/complete_wings.py` gives each the wing the plan assigns its class (period and polity to Time, practice to Living, work to Words, group to People) and prints the tally of existing tags it rests on. Three additions go beyond the class rule, each with its reason in the script: the contemporary era (Time, Today), Al-Azhar (adds Today, the plan's own example) and the Kiswa (adds Made; its own prose says it is woven today in Mecca). Only the `wings:` line changes and no wing is removed. Proposed to the founder as P-2.

- **Tathbit Dalail corpus mined into the graph.** «تثبيت دلائل النبوة» of the Qadi Abd al-Jabbar al-Hamdani ⁦(d. 415 AH)⁩ — the Mu'tazili compilation of proofs of prophethood and the Prophet's miracles — is now mined from its Arabic Wikisource edition into 195 `unit: chapter` passage records (`passage/tathbit-j1-*`, `passage/tathbit-j2-*`), each carrying a cited excerpt of at most 40 words, trilingual draft labels and summaries, a `part_of` edge to the work and `mentions` edges to the Prophet and the author. `source/ar-wikisource` records the edition (CC BY-SA 4.0, draft pending ledger onboarding), the work record gains its author, genre and language, and 42 passages already surface in the Miracles Browser's books section; any further harvested book joins the same way through the detector.

### Tests
- **Oracles for the canon and the baseline.** `scripts/fable/o00_baseline.py` measures the headline counts of a graph artifact (records, relations, draft and published, cornerstones, records with no relation) and proves the mission branch still stands on its frozen baseline with no merge from a moving `main`. `scripts/fable/o01_canon.py` proves the canon from the repository alone, with no network: the field exists, 824 records carry it and 271 are cornerstones, every record passes the structural floor or is a named editorial include (315 qualify with the Wikipedia count set to zero, 489 pass the floor and need it, 20 are includes), the canon script writes nothing to a record but its `importance` line, the register matches the data, every Hijri century from the 1st to the 14th holds a cornerstone and every cornerstone sits in a wing. Each oracle ends with `RESULT: GREEN` or `RESULT: NOT-GREEN`; the captured output of the baseline run is in `docs/fable-run/oracle-output/`.

### Added
- **Miracles Browser: متصفح المعجزات الإلهية ومعجزات الرسل (`/{lang}/miracles/`).** A new browser over the one graph listing every mention of the divine miracles and the prophets' miracles in the Qur'an, the Sunnah, the seerah and every harvested book — the miracle of the Qur'an and its inimitability, the cosmic signs of creation, the Prophet's signs (the moon-split, the Isra' and Mi'raj, the descent of 'Isa, water from between the fingers, the weeping trunk, the eclipses), and the narrated miracles (the staff, the parting of the sea, the she-camel of Salih, Nuh's ark, Musa's basket, Ibrahim's fire, the clay bird, the cradle speech, the heavenly table, Sulayman's signs, Yusuf's dreams, the annunciation of Yahya, the covenant chest, the destruction of the deniers' nations and the People of the Elephant). Passages are found at build time by a guarded lexicon in `scripts/miracles.ts` — corpus-aware (the general book corpus requires the miracle lexicon, the Qur'an/Sunnah/seerah are judged on the patterns), orthography-normalized, gated on the ambiguous lexemes («معجز» the verb «to defeat» in the Qur'an, «أعجاز نخل» palm-roots, «صالح» the adjective, «عاد» «returned», «موس» inside «موسم», «فر» «flee», «حبا» «love», «قدير» the attribute, «خسف» humiliation, «الكرامة» generosity, «المن» manna-context, «مائدة» dining-table, «التابوت» the covenant chest), with bounded co-occurrence windows and verified false-positive exclusions — so a miracle mentioned in any book harvested later appears here the day its passage record lands. Subject pages gather the verses, reports and stories per miracle-bearing prophet, concept and event (musa, sulayman, isa-ibn-maryam, the concepts of i'jaz and the cosmic signs, the Isra' and Mi'raj event and more); passages join through the topic→subject map and the canonical `mentions` edges. `/api/v1/miracles.json`, an Explore-menu and landing card, and the acceptance spec `docs/engineering/32-miracles-browser-requirements.md` (`MIR-R..`) for production validation. Plan `docs/plan/44-miracles-browser.md`; lane `miracles`. Records are draft until a human reads them.
- **Sayyi'at Browser: متصفح السيئات (`/{lang}/sayyiat/`).** A new browser over the one graph listing every mention of the sayyi'at and the sins theme the museum's sources carry — the Qur'anic verses from «إن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات» to «إلا اللمم», the hadith of the servant who intends a sin and the reports of major and minor sins, the sins and repentances of Companions and Successors in the seerah, and every sin mention in every harvested book. Passages are found at build time by a guarded lexicon in `scripts/sayyiat.ts` — the «سيّئ» and «ساء» families, the names of sin, guilt and disobedience (إثم، ذنب، معصية، فاحشة، خطيئة), the words of major and minor sins (كبائر، صغائر، and the gated كبيرة/صغيرة pair), and the verdicts لمم، فسق، فجور، إجرام — while «النساء» never matches «ساء»، «تكبيرة» never matches «كبيرة»، and verified false positives (waterskins «ذنوب»، the tailbone «الذنب»، the kunya «أبو العاصي») are excluded by id. 412 passages (330 Qur'an ayahs, 73 sunnah reports incl. a first Riyad al-Salihin batch — tawba, major and minor sins, prohibited matters, istighfar — 9 book/poetry passages; sayyi/related kinds) plus seven curated records tagged in place — the new umbrella `concept/al-sayyiat` with trilingual draft prose, `dhanb`, `ithm`, `minor-sins-saghair`, `tawba`, `istighfar` and `event/angels-report-the-intended-sin` — grouped into five sections (quran, sunnah, seerah, books, curated), `mentions → concept/al-sayyiat` edges on every detected passage, `/api/v1/sayyiat.json`, an Explore-menu and landing card, and the acceptance spec `docs/engineering/32-sayyiat-browser-requirements.md` (`SAY-R..`) for production validation. Plan `docs/plan/44-sayyiat-browser.md`; lane `sayyiat`. A book harvested later brings its sin mentions here automatically once its passage records land. Records are draft until a human reads them.
- **Hasanat Browser: متصفح الحسنات (`/{lang}/hasanat/`).** A new browser over the one graph listing every mention of the good deeds (الحسنات) the museum's sources carry — the Qur'anic verses that write, multiply and efface them («إن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات»، «من جاء بالحسنة فله عشر أمثالها»، «فأولئك يبدل الله سيئاتهم حسنات»، «أقرضوا الله قرضا حسنا»), the hadiths on the recording of intentions and deeds (the hadith qudsi «إن الله كتب الحسنات والسيئات»، «كل عمل ابن آدم يضاعف الحسنة بعشر أمثالها إلى سبعمائة ضعف»، «من سن في الإسلام سنة حسنة»، the gecko report), «الحسنى» the reward of ihsan, and every mention in the seerah, the stories, the Companion and Successor reports and every harvested book. Passages are found at build time by a guarded lexicon in `scripts/hasanat.ts` — «الحسنات»، «حسنات»، «الحسنة»، «حسنة» match as nouns, «الحسنى» counts only when it is not the divine-names formula «الأسماء الحسنى» or a «good word» adjective, the fixed collocations «قرضا حسنا» and «بدل حسنا بعد سوء» are caught, and bare «حسن»/«الحسن» (personal names, the hadith grade), the «حسنا» adverb and «حسنة» as a feminine adjective on a host noun («أسوة حسنة»، «الموعظة الحسنة»، «شفاعة حسنة») stay out; verified false positives are excluded by id, and every book harvested later brings its mentions here automatically once its passage records land. Sixty-seven passages detected at build time (43 Qur'an ayahs, 23 sunnah reports, 1 poetry record) plus curated records joining through the `hasanat-browser` tag — the new umbrella `concept/al-hasanat` with trilingual draft prose and thirteen existing records tagged in place (qard-hasan, kitab-al-amal, istighfar, dhikr, hamm, azm, ikhlas, gecko, al-salat-ala-al-nabi, intercession-shafaa, asbab-suqut-al-uquba, people-of-the-heights-and-the-scales and the angels-report event) — grouped into five sections (quran, sunnah, seerah, books, curated), `basis_for → concept/al-hasanat` edges on the seven kitabat-al-hasanat hadith-qudsi passages and the intention-report event, `/api/v1/hasanats.json`, an Explore-menu and landing card, and the acceptance spec `docs/engineering/33-hasanat-browser-requirements.md` (`HASANAT-R..`) preserving the founder's original brief for production validation. Plan `docs/plan/45-hasanat-browser.md`; lane `hasanat`. Records are draft until a human reads them.

### Fixed
- **Miracles detector alternation leak.** Concatenated `new RegExp(normalizeMiracleArabic("a|b") + …)` patterns let the `|` split the whole expression, so a lone context word («خلق»، «ماء»، «سماء») fired clay-bird, healing and table on unrelated ayahs — ayah 3:190 was tagged with three miracle events it does not narrate. Every alternation is now wrapped in `(?:…)`, corpus counts dropped from thousands of false hits to ~490 true ones (cosmic signs 5,368 → 129), and `scripts/miracles.test.ts` pins normalization, the defeat-verb and palm-roots exclusions, challenge/staff/sea/cosmic-sign fixtures, the books-corpus lexicon gate and matn-only detection.

## v1.15.2 — 2026-11-11
### Fixed
- **Second build break repaired: `needs_source` markers stripped on every remaining render path.** The new build check caught 226 pages still printing the internal sourcing annotation — entity `perspectives` summaries injected raw, prose perspective labels, table/heading chunks the Markdown renderer skipped, browser card helpers that read `summary` directly (angels, messengers, signs, magic, bayt, dreams, madhahib, dua, jinn-devils, nature), subject-page passage summaries, the revelation-order edge notes, and the angels meta description. Every one of those paths now strips the marker through `stripNeedsSource`, and the check itself was narrowed to the actual marker syntax — `(needs_source)` / `(needs_source: …)` — so prose that merely names the mechanism (release notes, decision records) no longer false-positives.

## v1.15.1 — 2026-11-11
### Fixed
- **Main-branch build repaired.** A delegation manifest (`maghazi-waqidi.yaml`, the al-Waqidi *Kitab al-Maghazi* harvest registry) had been committed inside `data/_stubs.d/`, where every file must be a YAML list of `class/slug` stub entries; the loader folded the mapping into the stub list and the site build died in Astro with «Missing parameter: slug». The manifest now lives beside its delegation doc at `docs/delegation/library/maghazi-waqidi.yaml`, the bayt plan and requirements point there, and `loadStubs` rejects any non-list stub file — or a stub id that is not `class/slug` — with a clear error at load time instead of a cryptic build failure.

The record now explicitly identifies al-Wāqidī's recension (author, genre `sira`, Shamela/Jones provenance) for the bayt harvest, and the Mūsā ibn ʿUqba identity is preserved as a separate draft `work/kitab-al-maghazi-musa-ibn-uqba` keeping the Wikidata id; `source/al-waqidi-maghazi` was upgraded to the primary-source record for the Shamela text of the Jones edition with an honesty note that the Jones print edition itself is not open access.
- **Household of the Prophet Browser corpus tagged and two records added.** Fifty-three existing records joined the browser through `bayt-browser` + `bayt-<section>` tags: the family persons (Fatima, Ali, Hasan, Husayn, the Prophet's daughters, Khadija, Abd al-Muttalib, Abu Talib, al-Abbas, Hamza, Ja'far, Umm Ayman), all eleven wife records, the imams line (al-Sadiq, al-Baqir, al-Rida, Zayd ibn Ali), the clan groups (Ahl al-Bayt, Banu Hashim, Banu Abd al-Muttalib, Mothers of the Believers), the household events (Ghadir, Karbala, Fadak, the family deaths) and the mubahala and twelve-imams concepts, plus four seerah works. Two previously-missing core members — `person/ummayma-bint-ali` and `person/fatima-bint-ali`, daughters of Ali and Fatima — were created as draft records with trilingual labels, summaries and prose.
- **Four Madhhabs Browser corpus seeded from the graph and the harvested books.** 136 records joined the browser through `madhahib-browser` + `mh-<section>` tags: the four school groups and their imams, the Zahiri, Ja'fari and Ibadiyya records kept in the labelled «مدارس أخرى» section, the salaf forebears (Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Hasan al-Basri, al-Awza'i, Sufyan al-Thawri, Ibn Sirin, al-Zuhri, the Kufan and Basran traditionists) and the formative students of the imams (al-Shaybani, Abu Yusuf, Zufar, al-Quduri, Ibn al-Qasim, al-Layth, al-Muzani, al-Buwayti, al-Za'farani), the school scholars (Ibn Abidin, al-Kasani, al-Sarakhsi, Ibn Rushd, al-Dardir, al-Nawawi, al-Rafi'i, Ibn Hajar, the Subkis, Ibn Qudama, Ibn Taymiyya, Ibn Rajab, al-Buhuti), 59 canonical and comparative books, and the fiqh/usul concepts (madhhab, ijtihad, qiyas, istihsan, taqlid, ikhtilaf, mujtahid, ijma, maslaha, tarjih, rukhsa and more). 82 `mentions` edges now tie those books to the schools they treat — each school's manuals to their own group, the comparative works (Bidayat al-Mujtahid, the Kuwaiti Fiqh Encyclopedia, Subki's Fatawa of the Imams, al-Muwafaqat, the Madkhal) to the madhhab concept and all four schools — so they surface in the browser's «ما قيل في المذاهب» corpus section with their editions' provenance, and any book harvested later joins the same way the day its edges land.
- **Household of the Prophet Browser corpus seeded from al-Wāqidī's Maghāzī.** Nineteen family-relevant chapter passages were mined from al-Maktaba al-Shamila's digital text of Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar al-Wāqidī's *Kitāb al-Maghāzī* (book 23680, the Marsden Jones Oxford 1966 edition; printed pp. 9–1127) and landed as `passage/waqidi-maghazi-*` draft records with `work: work/kitab-al-maghazi` (`genre: [sira]`), so they join the browser's **seerah** section automatically — the first seerah-book passages in the corpus. The harvest covers Hamza's first sariyya, Badr's call to Banu Hashim, Hamza's martyrdom and Safiyya bint Abd al-Muttalib at Uhud, the Ifk affair and Zaynab bint Jahsh's exoneration, the wives' rotation at the Trench, the Banu Qurayza chapter, Fadak, Umm Qirfa, Hudaybiyya, the twenty women of Khaybar, the Mu'ta condolence to Fatima, the Conquest, Hunayn's steadfast hundred of the household, Ta'if, al-Fils, Tabuk, Ali's Yemen mission, the Farewell Pilgrimage and Usama's final expedition. Each record carries bounded ≤40-word excerpts with honourifics stripped, `mentions` edges to the existing people/groups/events, and page-precise provenance. Delegation `docs/delegation/library/maghazi-waqidi.md` updated: wave B landed, wave C (deeper per-chapter mining) remains. All records draft until a human reads them.
- **Four Madhhabs Browser: formative-generation scholars added.** Two new person records mined from the harvested Tabaqat al-Fuqaha of Ibn Abd al-Barr (edition al-Abbas, Dar al-Ma'arif 1981): al-Ashhab ibn Abd al-Aziz (d. 204, Malik's Egyptian successor) and Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Dinar (d. 182, of whom al-Shafi'i said he saw none more learned among Malik's companions). - **Jinn & Devils Browser: wave-10 remaining shaytan reports.** Five more records close out the Muwatta and Muslim shaytan passages not yet in the browser: the two prostrations of forgetfulness as a rebuke to the shaytan (Muwatta 1:252, mursal noted); the one who passes before the praying person is a shaytan (1:421); the lone rider is a shaytan, two riders two shaytans, three a riding party (31:2801); coming to the mosque with disheveled hair like a shaytan (31:2732); and saying «if only» opens the shaytan's work (Muslim 2664). ## v1.10.1 — 2026-11-11
### Added
- **Jinn & Devils Browser: ninety-seven passages now point at their beings.** A conservative harvest (`scripts/harvest/jinn-devils/mentions.py`) scanned every Qur'an ayah and harvested hadith record for unambiguous jinn/devil/dream vocabulary — الجن as a whole token (never الجنة or الجنود), إبليس, شيطان/شياطين, وسواس, لوّامة, سحر-domain words, كهانة, قرين in hadith corpora, and the jinn kinds (مارد، عفريت، غول، سيّاط) — and added `mentions` edges to the graph records those words name. Edges cite each passage's own registered source; the run is idempotent so future harvested books get the same treatment by re-running it.
- **Jinn & Devils Browser: graph seeds begin.** Twenty-nine existing records — the jinn, the qareen, Iblis, the shayatin of humans and jinn, waswas, sihr, kahana, the ghul, the dream-science concepts and the Prophet-era kahins — now carry `jinn-devils-browser` tags with section tags (`jd-jinn`, `jd-devils`, `jd-angels`, `jd-dreams`), and three new records open the interaction stories: the kinds of jinn, the delegation of the jinn to the Prophet, and the bewitching done on him by Labid ibn al-Asam. New `jinn` and `devil` concept kinds join the schema alongside the angels browser's `angel`. Draft-tier throughout; the browser page and API export follow in later commits.

### Fixed
- **Battles API: ghazwa flags come from the shared edge rule.** `/api/v1/battles.json` now derives its `ghazwa` flag through `scripts/ghazwa.ts` — the same rule the battles pages use — so the endpoint cannot drift from the site. The live split is 57 ghazawat and 15 saraya of 72 prophetic-era records (3,250 military records total); the 53/22/75/3,251 figures in the requirements doc were its implementation-time snapshot and have drifted with the graph, not with a second derivation.

### Added
- **`meta/deploy.json` gains a `pages` count, and Backstage gets its fill-in script.** The deploy stamp now records the number of HTML pages it published, and `site/src/scripts/backstage-stats.ts` is ready to fill the Backstage entry and page figures from `/api/v1/meta/counts.json` and `meta/deploy.json` — the same single sources the homepage reads.

### Fixed
- **Map: every city in a region is now reachable.** Hundreds of places share fallback positions around their host city, so region markers piled up and a click on the pile opened whichever marker painted last — a Baghdad click could open Adana. The clicked city is now honoured even when the year slider sits outside its activity window (the old code silently substituted the region's first city), a click on a pile opens a chooser listing every place at that spot with its linked-record count, and a scrollable list of all the region's places sits beside the map so any city can be picked by name. Markers for places with no activity in the selected year dim instead of disappearing. Palette, pan and basemap are unchanged.
- **Object pages show their photographs again.** Detail pages only looked for `depicted_in` edges, but remote museum photographs reach objects through the media record's own `depicts` field — the same field the objects gallery already reads. Depiction media are now indexed once per build worker from that field, so records like the Coronation Mantle render their image, licence and attribution on the detail page.
- **Internal `needs_source` markers can no longer reach a published page.** Transcript-mining annotations stayed in prose and rendered literally on pages like the Prophet's biography and the Battle of Badr. A single strip pattern now removes them — bare, parenthesised, and isolate-wrapped forms — in the Markdown renderer, plain-text summaries, entity metadata and Nature descriptions, and the site checker fails the build if the literal ever appears in generated HTML. The markers stay in the data as honest sourcing state.
- **Battles pages use the shared ghazwa/sariyya rule.** The battles index and the ghazawat page now call the same `scripts/ghazwa.ts` derivation the API uses, so index tile, ghazawat page and `/api/v1/battles.json` always agree.
- **Teacher-pathway pages explain the † mark.** The curriculum-review date renders a dagger when the Hijri date is computed; the page now carries the same footnote legend entity pages use, so the mark is never dangling.
- **Backstage counts and date are live.** The page no longer hard-codes "49,505 entries / 99,000 pages" and a stale date; it shows graph-derived figures with no-JavaScript fallbacks and lets the fill-in script replace them with the live counts and deploy timestamp.
- **The People hall lists people.** Graph nodes are stored class-by-class, so the hall opened on the concepts and events cross-listed into the wing before its 11,000 persons; every hall now lists its own class first. The "full hall arrives in a later phase" note is gone from every populated wing.
- **Changelog route templates render as paths.** CANARY entries name routes as `/{lang}/place/` or `/[lang]/asma/<slug>/`; the changelog now renders the concrete path of the reader's language (`/ar/asma/…/`) instead of the literal template, while `{cite:… <fiche>}` and `<details>` prose stay untouched.
- **Qudsi browser: the unthemed groups get a heading.** Seven hadith groups carry no theme and rendered a blank "· 7" heading; they now gather under a localized "Other themes" label in Arabic, English and Urdu.
- **Battles joins the ready explorers.** The Explore card no longer shows "under preparation" while `/battles/` is live.
- **Graph explorer reads parent/child the right way round.** Child edges were labelled «ابن/ابنة» where entity pages group the same people under «والد/والدة»; edge direction is now honoured, so a parent's neighbours read as parents/children consistently.
- **Search opens on its query.** A direct load of `/ar/search/?q=…` now seeds the box and runs the search once Pagefind finishes initialising, instead of showing an empty page until the visitor types.

## v1.10.0 — 2026-11-10
### Added
- **Battles browser: testable requirements spec.** `docs/engineering/20-battles-browser-requirements.md` lists every requirement for the browser — the routes in all three languages, the derived ghazwa/sariyya split, `/api/v1/battles.json`, search indexing, the register rows, the record-level rendering rules and the data-state baseline — each with the concrete production check to run. Linked from plan 31 and the battles lane so any agent can validate the shipped browser against it.

### Fixed
- **Timeline explorer chronology restored.** Two death dates carried the same Hijri year as the event that caused them but a different derived CE year, so the timeline placed the deaths before the fatal event: `person/muadh-ibn-jabal` (d. 18 AH — now 0639 like `event/plague-of-amwas`, was 0638) and `person/thabit-ibn-qays` (d. 12 AH at Yamama — now 0634 like `event/battle-of-yamama`, was 0633). The `time-browser-explorer` chronology test passes again.
- **Asma name pages: citation footnotes render again.** The divine-name pages rendered `{cite:…}` markers as `#note-N` links but never emitted the footnote list, so the site link-checker failed the whole build with 915 dead-anchor errors across the three languages. The page now re-numbers citations globally (same pattern as `EntityLayout`) and renders the sourced footnote list at the bottom of each name page.
- **Nature and teacher-pathway pages: same footnote-anchor gap closed.** The Nature Explorer subject page rendered `{cite:…}` markers in its lede without emitting the footnote list (12 dead-anchor errors on `nature/asal` in build 42807915315), and the two teacher-pathway templates (landing + printable pack) had the same latent gap in their teacher-note rendering. All three now re-number citations globally and emit the footnote list, matching `EntityLayout`; the kids' read page was checked and is safe (`plainChildMarkdown` strips citations by design).

### Data
- **The canon: 824 records marked as the museum's cornerstones and major subjects.** A new optional `importance` field (1 cornerstone, 2 major) now sits on 824 records across eleven classes — 412 people, 130 places, 76 events, 63 concepts, 34 polities, 29 buildings, 20 works, 20 groups, 15 practices, 13 periods and 12 objects — with 270 at importance 1. It is the list the museum finishes first and will show first: until now nothing told a wing landing, the homepage or search which of 53,000 records a first-time visitor expects to find. A record enters when both the museum's own graph leans on it (inbound links, prose mentions, pathway appearances) and the subject is widely known (Wikipedia language editions linked from its recorded Wikidata item), plus 59 named editorial includes whose signals are still weak. The register `docs/canon.md` lists every record with its state — 37 have no Arabic prose, 444 are under 300 words, 526 are still draft — and names subjects not in the graph yet (Timur, Osman I, the Abbasid revolution, usul al-fiqh and others). Nothing changes on any page or in the API yet; the field ranks editorial priority only and says nothing about a subject's standing. Generated by `scripts/report/canon.py`; decision record dec-20261110-230.
- **Battles browser: `during_reign` backfill + two place-region corrections.** A ruler-interval pass over person `story_roles` (167 sovereign intervals) added 36 `during_reign` edges to 26 military events where the event year matched exactly one theatre's reigning ruler — Rashidun caliphs on the 634–656 boundary years, late Abbasid caliphs on the 1225–1231 Khwarazmian-era campaigns, Ottoman sultans on WWI Sinai and Caucasus engagements, Abbasid/Fatimid caliphs on medieval fronts. Non-Islamic sovereigns (e.g. Heraclius) were deliberately excluded as outside the predicate's established convention, and ambiguous multi-theatre matches were left unfilled rather than guessed. Two mislabeled place regions surfaced by the pass were corrected: `place/antalya` (Antalya, Turkey — was `andalus-europe`, now `anatolia-balkans`) and `place/qajar-iran` (was `levant-iraq`, now `persia-central-asia`).
- **Battles browser: geo wave 6 — admin divisions and sites, coverage ~70%.** The last usable slice of Wikidata location items — municipalities, governorates, communes, archaeological sites and geographic terms — became 114 more draft `place/` stubs (Jaén folded into the existing `place/jaen`, which gained its Wikidata id). `occurred_at` edges reached 147 more engagements with locator maps on the same set; coverage is now 71% `occurred_at` (2,363 of 3,293) and 70% maps (2,325). One pre-existing data error surfaced and was fixed: `language/indonesian` carried Vienne's Wikidata id — corrected to Q9240. Remaining unlinked events are mostly items with no Arabic label (~350), polity-like entries for the entity lanes, or records whose Wikidata item declares no location.
- **Battles browser: geo wave 5 — 191 more place stubs, coverage now ~2/3.** The remaining Wikidata location items (rate-limited fetch completed) yielded 191 further draft `place/` stubs — again skipping items already held as `building/` records (Gerdkuh, Lambsar) and polity-like entries. `occurred_at` edges reached 187 more engagements and the locator-map pass placed the same set. `occurred_at` coverage is now 67% of military records (2,216 of 3,293) and 2,178 carry a map — two-thirds of all military events now show where they happened.
- **Battles browser: 299 new place records + geo coverage jumps to ~60%.** Wikidata location claims on military events pointed at towns, cities, rivers, mountains and regions the museum did not yet have; 299 of them were created as draft `place/` stubs (labels, description and P625 coordinates from Wikidata, `source/wikidata` cited, `status.review: draft`) — castles and towers that already exist as `building/` records were not duplicated. Those stubs plus existing `building/` targets unlocked `occurred_at` edges on 453 more engagements (~480 edges), and the locator-map pass then placed 667 more events. `occurred_at` coverage is now 61% of military records (2,029 of 3,293) and 1,991 carry a map. Five stub candidates that would have duplicated existing `building/` entities were dropped; polity-like items (states, kingdoms, empires) were left for the entity lanes.
- **Battles browser: 219 more locator maps + ~250 new `occurred_at` links.** Places whose coordinates were stored in YAML list form (previously skipped by the map pass) now yield maps for 219 engagements. Separately, 87 existing place records gained their Wikidata identifier where the label matched uniquely — unlocking `occurred_at` edges on 211 more military events (~250 edges). Four identifier collisions were resolved in favour of the already-registered entity (the three empire places keep their polity's QID; Alamut keeps the region item, not the castle's). `occurred_at` coverage is now 47% of military records (1,576 of 3,293) and 1,324 carry a map.
- **Battles browser: locator maps on 412 more engagements.** Every military event that gained (or already had) an `occurred_at` edge to a place with coordinates now carries a minimal `map` block in the same shape as the earlier locator pass — kind mapped from the event kind (battle/siege/naval/campaign), locality precision, centre from the place's coordinates, extent by kind, one `event_point` feature citing the record's own source, and `date_for_borders` from the event's EDTF year. Around 1,050 military events now render a map.
- **Battles browser: Wikidata location links — ~630 engagements placed on the map.** Military records whose linked Wikidata item declares a `located in the administrative territorial entity` (P276) claim gained an `occurred_at` edge to the matching graph place — only where the Wikidata place ID resolves to exactly one existing `place/` record, so no ambiguous or invented locations. Three place records (Béjaïa, Bornu, Gibraltar) gained their Wikidata identifier to close the mapping. Combined with the earlier locator-map pass, roughly 700 military events now carry a `map` block on their event pages. `occurred_at` coverage rises to ~41% of military records (1,365 of 3,293); records with multiple or unresolvable location claims were left untouched.
- **Nature Explorer: production acceptance spec.** `docs/engineering/21-nature-explorer-requirements.md` now lists every requirement the founder set — the six-section taxonomy, trilingual pages and records, Qur'an/hadith edges from the frozen passage records, separation from the Time Browser (own routes, menu item, landing card, API, lib), `/api/v1/nature.json`, Pagefind indexing, draft-tier provenance, the labelled-reading rule (qaswara, talh) and the classical-lore labelling for the al-Damiri/al-Qazwini wave — each with a verbatim production check (curl + grep) and the regression baseline (119 records, ~650 edges), following the battles-browser spec's format.
- **Nature Explorer wave 6 — the book of beasts.** Two classical zoology works registered as sources — al-Damiri's *Hayat al-Hayawan al-Kubra* (the alphabetical animal encyclopedia with its fiqh rulings) and al-Qazwini's *Aja'ib al-Makhluqat* (the famous illustrated cosmography) — and ten creatures joined on their authority, each summary labelled as tradition, not Prophetic text: the crocodile of the Nile (with its fiqh debate), the proud peacock, the ungettable phoenix (anqa), the long-lived vulture, the noble bustard of the falconers, the bear, the fire-proof salamander of the marvel books, the featherless bat, the house-carrying turtle, and the patient one-legged heron. 119 records — still `status.review: draft`.
- **Nature Explorer wave 5 — the barnyard, the pantry and the orchard.** Five more creatures joined with six new hadith passage records created from the canonical collections: the rooster whose crowing means it has seen an angel (Bukhari 3303), the gecko of the graded-stroke reward and the seventy good deeds (Muslim 2240a, Abu Dawud 5263-64), the mouse of the ghee and the lamp (Muwatta 2785, 2686), the dove whose egg was the likeness of the Seal (Muslim 2344), and the shrike — the fourth protected creature of the prohibition hadith (Abu Dawud 5267, now a passage record, linking ant, bee and hoopoe too). The ant finally gained its full report family: the prophet stung by one ant who burned the colony, in six collections. Then the orchard wave: ginger and camphor of Paradise's cups, the talh tree (banana or acacia — both readings labelled), the tamarisk of Sheba's ruined gardens, the fruits of "let man look at his food" (80:24-32) and the unending fruits of Paradise, and the existing fiqh honey record tagged in beside the "give him honey — God spoke true, your brother's belly lied" report (Bukhari 5684). 109 records, ~650 links — still `status.review: draft`.
- **Nature Explorer wave 4 — the Muwatta's ark.** Twelve more creatures joined, nearly all from the Muwatta's hunting and ihram books: the lizard Khalid ibn al-Walid ate before the Prophet's eyes ("not unlawful, but not the food of my people"); Umar's ransom quartet for game killed in ihram — the hyena for a ram, the gazelle for a goat, the hare for a she-kid, the jerboa for a weaned lamb; Malik's sanctuary line between the attacking beasts (leopard, cheetah, with lion and wolf) and the spared ones (fox, hyena, cat); the owl the Prophet freed from the Arabs' omen ("no contagion, no hama, no Safar"); the sparrow that can stand for the aqiqa; the earth-creature that ate Solomon's staff in Saba 34:14; and the mule of the Bees' riding verse. 98 records, ~597 verse and report links — still `status.review: draft`.
- **Nature Explorer wave 3 — the raptors and the mounts.** Four birds joined from the Muwatta's reports: the falcon, the hawk and the eagle — the trained hunting birds whose catch is lawful when God's name is uttered at release — and the kite, one of the five vermin whose killing is permitted in and out of ihram. The land records deepened too: the horse gained the chargers of al-Adiyat, "tethered horses" of preparation, Iblis' cavalry and the mounts of the fighters; the camel gained the pagan taboo camels of al-Ma'idah, the camel's-load verses of Yusuf and the yellow camels of the sparks; the she-camel of Salih gained the hamstringing and the "she-camel of God, a sign to you"; and livestock gained the an'am verses of "in them is warmth and uses". 86 records, ~575 verse and report links — still `status.review: draft`.
- **Nature Explorer wave 2 — the heavens and the elements.** Twelve new records joined the explorer (82 subjects, ~543 verse and report links): the planets (Yusuf's eleven stars, the Brilliant Star of the Lamp verse, the stars scattered on the Last Day), the shooting stars thrown at the jinn, the deep sea of "darkness upon darkness", the fish (the Sabbath-town trial, the lawful game of the sea), the lion of the fleeing wild asses (with its two readings labelled), the scattered moths of the Last Day, the splitter of grain and the seven ears, the tree of Eden, fire kindled from the green tree, the dust and clay man was made of, hoarded and paradisal gold and silver, and the two easts and two wests. The sea record gained the sea-as-ink and the ships-as-mountains verses, iron gained the barrier of Dhul-Qarnayn, and zaqqum the thorn-food of al-Ghashiyah. Still `status.review: draft` until a human reads them.
- **Battles browser: sides enrichment waves 3–23 (plan 31).** The military-event browser's cards now carry attacker/defender data on hundreds more records. Wave 3 derived `sides` on 206 engagements from each record's own `had_participant` edges; then twenty researched waves added hand-cited sides to ~330 famous engagements across every era — the Rashidun canon (Covadonga, Karbala, Siffin, Fakhkh, Lepanto), Umayyad and early-Abbasid battles (Derbent, Mamma, Jurjan, Kopidnadon, the Zanj fronts), the Crusades–Ayyubid–Mamluk era (Hattin, Ain Jalut, Tyre, Kerak, Belvoir, the 1265–68 coastal falls), Ottoman and gunpowder engagements (Chaldiran, Mohács, Lepanto, Malacca, Diu, Tripoli, Golconda, Bijapur, Samarkand, Kandahar, Baghdad 1638), colonial-era wars (Atbara, Khartoum, the Mahdist wars), the WWI theaters (Gallipoli, Kut, Sinai) and the modern-era Balkan/Indo-Pak records. Modern records tied to designated terrorist organisations were deliberately skipped per the content-safety rule. Total `sides` coverage is now ~1,050 of 3,251 military records.
- **Battles browser: bulk sides pass — 103 conquest/siege records.** For the remaining records whose `during_reign` and `occurred_at` edges exist but have no participant edges, sides were generated conservatively from those same edges — side one is the reigning power's forces, side two the garrison/defenders of the place — restricted to kinds with a clear attacker/defender shape (conquest, siege, raid, campaign).
- **Battles browser: missing belligerent entities + full participant linking.** Fifty missing polities and peoples that appear as battle sides were created as draft records (Russian Empire, Holy Roman Empire, British Empire, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, Ethiopian Empire, Mahdist Sudan, Sharifian Empire, Kingdom of France/Italy/Greece/Hungary/Aragon/Asturias/León, Crown of Aragon, Taifas of Granada and Murcia, Sasanian Empire, Egypt eyalet, Regency of Algiers, County of Portugal, Habsburg monarchy, First Hellenic Republic, League of Lezhë, Soran Emirate, Khanate of Bukhara, Bruneian Sultanate, Kabardia, Tsardom of Russia, French Republics, Dutch Empire, Zand dynasty, Qara Qoyunlu, Spanish Restoration, Fulani Empire, Hamdanid emirate of Aleppo, Hispanic Monarchy, Republic of Venice, Kingdom of Kartli/Georgia/Wallachia, UK of GB&I and of the Netherlands; plus Javanese, Assyrians, Souliotes, Riffians and the Israel Defense Forces as groups). `external_ids.wikidata` was added to `polity/sasanian-empire`, `polity/adal`… correction: Adal's QID lives on `place/adal-sultanate`; `group/kurds` gained its QID. Battle-side `participants:` links now total ~1,080 — nearly every resolvable Wikidata participant points at a canonical graph entity.
- **Battles browser: Wikidata-participant sides wave — 668 records.** The remaining draft-card military records gained `sides` where their linked Wikidata item (already carried in `external_ids.wikidata`) declares exactly two distinct `participant` claims: each side's label is the participant's own Wikidata en/ar label, ordered Muslim-side first when the participant's religion claim resolves to Islam, and `source/wikidata` was added to the record's citations. Records with one or three-plus participants were left untouched — the flat claim list cannot show which participant stood on which side. `sides` coverage is now ~1,720 of 3,250 military records; four modern-conflict records were held back under the content-safety rule (Hezbollah, the designated group in Ramadi 2014, the Tulkarm Brigade and the 2024 Batroun raid); the remaining ~1,534 are draft cards whose Wikidata items carry zero or ambiguous participant claims and still need real source mining.
- **Prose visibility repair.** 964 prose files across all classes had body text but no `## ` heading, so the graph build's `splitSections` dropped their content — they rendered as empty sections. A standard summary heading was inserted into each; the compiled graph now has zero empty prose documents repo-wide.
- **Record corrections.** `event/siege-of-taif-8` was a duplicate stub and is now an alias of `event/siege-of-taif`; `battle-of-abraq-632` and `siege-of-tbilisi-628` were corrected to the Rashidun era.


### Added
- **Requirements doc for the Asma ul Husna Browser.** `docs/engineering/19-asma-browser-requirements.md` writes out every feature requirement with an id and a production check — catalog and data model, the `/{lang}/asma/` landing, name pages and their story sections, the API, registers, governance, deferred items, and a one-line curl smoke test — so any person or agent can verify the deployed site against what was promised.
- **سيرة وحياة · Seerah & Life (`/{lang}/seerah/`).** A new practice-guide page: the Seerah as a method of living, organised by time horizon (daily, weekly, monthly, yearly, life stages) and life domain (worship, Quran & knowledge, money & work, family, neighbours & society, self & time). Twenty-six cards cover morning/evening adhkar, the five prayers and rawatib, the daily Quran portion, Jumu'ah, Monday/Thursday and White Days fasting, the monthly budget and a standing sadaqa, a practical zakat walkthrough, Ramadan and the worship seasons, the annual review, and the life-stage cards (childhood, youth, learning a trade, honest work, marriage and parents, life mission, animals and the environment, volunteering, old age). Every card carries cited ayat linked to their frozen Tanzil passage pages (no verse text typed), cited hadith, numbered action steps and a "big picture" note; relevant cards carry fiqh notes (e.g. women's rulings, zakat nisab verification). Fully readable without JavaScript (each card is a `<details>`); the search box and horizon/domain chips in `site/src/scripts/seerah.ts` are progressive enhancement. The page ships in Arabic, English and Urdu in the same commit — the Urdu card prose is an AI draft awaiting human review. The Explore menu and the landing page gain a "Seerah & Life" card; the header block is Pagefind-indexed per `docs/site/browsers.md` §4.

### Changed
- **Landing card motif for Seerah & Life.** The landing-page card now carries a custom motif — a gold sun over a winding teal path, the Seerah read as a path of life — in the same abstract, figurative-free style as the other explorer thumbnails, plus a `wing-living` accent colour.
- **Requirements spec for Seerah & Life.** `docs/engineering/21-seerah-life-planner-requirements.md` records the founder's brief and the full acceptance spec — functional, content, language, surfacing, accessibility and a 17-row production checklist — so any agent can validate the live site against what was asked.

## v1.9.0 — 2026-11-10

### Added
- **Education Browser — school syllabus picker (`/{lang}/learn/courses/`).** Students pick country → province/board → grade → subject and open a syllabus page that weaves Muslim connections through each lesson. The pilot is the full Ontario (Canada, English board) Grade 6 Science course: 23 `course` records — jurisdiction → grade → subject → the four strands (Biodiversity, Electricity, Flight, Space) → 16 lessons — each carrying positioned connection cards (Qur'an, hadith, scholar, invention, career, story) that link into the museum's knowledge graph. Content is bilingual ar/en, `status.review: draft` pending human review, and cites *The Ontario Curriculum, Grades 1–8: Science and Technology* (2022). The picker has a no-JS fallback.
- **`course` entity class.** New graph class for school-curriculum trees: `kind ∈ {jurisdiction, grade, subject, unit, lesson}` nested by `part_of`, with `expectations[]` and `connections[]` documented in `docs/plan/02-content-model.md`. Course pages render on the generic entity route (`/{lang}/course/<slug>/`) with unit/lesson lists and connection cards (`ConnCard.astro`).
- **Syllabus pilot now ships Urdu too.** All 23 course records gained `ur` labels, summaries, expectation texts and connection-card copy, and `content/ur/course/` carries the full 23 Urdu prose files — the picker and course pages now render in Arabic, English and Urdu (AI draft pending human review).


- **Malformed YAML from earlier enrichment batches repaired.** Merging surfaced ~460 data files with duplicated top-level keys (`died`, `coordinate_note`, `coordinate_precision`), orphaned list items under scalar keys, source refs folded into `regions`, invalid `kind: locality` on places, and a duplicated `perspectives` block on `concept/mahdiyya` — all repaired so `npm run validate` is clean; `kind: locality` mapped to `town`; two dozen missing relation targets and sources registered in `data/_stubs.yaml`.

## v1.7.1 — 2026-11-09

### Content

- **i18n: `battles.*` block added to Arabic and English.** The Battles, Wars and Conquests Browser strings existed only in Urdu; `i18n/ar.yaml` and `i18n/en.yaml` now carry the full 24-key `battles.*` block (titles, section headings, filters, kind labels singular and plural), so the battles pages render real text in all three UI languages. Fixes the two pre-existing test failures about missing Arabic keys.


- **Hadith Qudsi Browser — corpus verified against the printed collection.** Every numbered narration of «الأحاديث القدسية» (Quran and Hadith Committee, Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs, Cairo, 10th ed. 1417/1997) was reconciled against the browser's records. Four hadiths present in the printed corpus but missing from the browser were added — the Fire's complaint, the dream of the Highest Assembly, the folding of the heavens ("I am the King"), and the Basin — as 15 narrations across Bukhari, Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi, Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, bringing the corpus to 117 hadiths in 350 narrations. The printed book is registered as `source/ahadith-qudsiyya-majlis`. Two browser hadiths that the printed corpus does not list (Muslim 2937 and Tirmidhi 2347) were re-read, confirmed as divine first-person speech and kept; the reconciliation notes are in `docs/plan/32-hadith-qudsi-browser.md` §7. All new records are `status.review: draft` until a human reads them.

## v1.7.0 — 2026-11-10

- **Realm extents and first caliph prose.** Each caliphate carries a dated schematic extent under `geo/polity/` (one representative year per polity, `precision: schematic`, cited) — the map layer the caliph pages read. The 30 caliph records created in the roster wave now have trilingual prose stubs (summary + sources, draft-tier pending human review).
- **Every roster caliph now has trilingual prose and reign events.** The last three caliphs without pages (Abd al-Rahman V, al-Mu'tasim, Sa'id al-Mutadid) gained draft stubs in ar/en/ur, and 73 more events were wired to their caliph after `occurred_at` place regions resolved the overlap-era ambiguity — 3,069 event records now carry `during_reign` edges.
- **Chronology audit: 162 impossible participation edges repaired.** A repo-wide sweep found `had_participant` edges where the person's documented life cannot intersect the event's date — mostly "dossier" events that file later decrees on the dated original record. Each was re-typed to `related_to` keeping its role text and sources, so the fact stays linked without claiming the person was present.
- **Gemini historian-check: both roster batches applied.** Batch 1 (150 records) fixed 14 reign spans, split interrupted reigns into separate `story_roles` (Cordoba fitna, Cairo Abbasids, Mustafa I), moved Abd al-Mu'min's start to 1130, and added the missing Hammudid caliph `yahya-al-mutali`. Batch 2 corrected the late Sokoto succession (Mai Turare to 1924, Tambari 1924–1931), added `hasan-dan-muazu` (1931–1938) and `ali-ibn-husayn` (Sharifian claimant, Jeddah 1924–25), and ended Husayn's claim in Oct 1924. Roster is now 165 caliphs; new records have trilingual draft prose.
### Added
- **Hadith Qudsi Browser (`/{lang}/qudsi/`, متصفح الأحاديث القدسية).** Every hadith qudsi of the six books and the Muwatta of Malik — 117 hadiths in 350 narrations — each hadith shown with its narrations in every collection and arranged by theme, with a filter box that also works without a server and a full list without JavaScript. It is in the Explore menu and has its own card on the landing page. The narrations are ordinary hadith passages in the graph (tag `hadith-qudsi`, one `qudsi-<slug>` tag per hadith); existing passages were tagged in place, not duplicated. Labels, summaries and grouping are draft until a human reads them. Plan: `docs/plan/32-hadith-qudsi-browser.md`.
- **`/api/v1/qudsi.json`.** The browser's dataset: every hadith qudsi narration with collection, number, matn excerpt (at most 40 words), hadith tag, themes and edges; in `docs/data/README.md`, the OpenAPI document and `llms.txt`.

### Data
- **Battles browser waves 1–2 (plan 31).** Sourced `sides:` blocks (labels, participants, commanders, tradition-status strengths) on 26 prophetic-era engagements: the Qaynuqa, Qurayza and Nadir sieges/expulsions, Badr al-Maw'ida, Usama, Dumat al-Jandal, Hamra al-Asad, the Yemen expedition, the Muslim–Quraysh war umbrella, al-Raji', Bi'r Ma'una, the Amr ibn Umayya mission, the two Hudhayl assassinations, and the remaining saraya (Abd al-Rahman to Dumat, Abu Ubayda, Ali to al-Fals, Kurz ibn Jabir, Zayd to Madyan, the Ibn Abi Hadrad raids and the smaller missions) — every block cited to the record's own filed sources. The Battles, Wars and Conquests Browser cards now show commanders and forces on 273 engagements.
- **315 new hadith passages and 16 tagged in place** from the open `fawazahmed0/hadith-api` Arabic editions (Unlicense, standard numbering), with Arabic, English and Urdu labels and summaries; new source record `source/hadith-api-fawazahmed0`.

## v1.6.0 — 2026-11-10

- **The caliphs' "Events of the reign" sections are populated.** A `during_reign` pass wired 2,996 event records to the caliph whose reign their dates intersect (regions disambiguate overlapping eras — Andalusian events to Cordoba, Egyptian to Fatimid or Cairo line, Sahel to Sokoto), citing the roster's reign source on each edge. Every caliph page now lists the engagements, foundations, decrees and appointments his reign saw — 3,385 reign links in the compiled graph.
### Added
- **The Battles, Wars and Conquests Browser «متصفح الغزوات والحروب والفتوحات» (plan 31).** The museum's record of armed engagement gets its front door: `/{lang}/battles/` opens on the prophetic expeditions — the ghazawat the Prophet witnessed or led and the saraya he sent, a split derived from each record's `had_participant`/`sides` edges — then browses all 3,251 military `event` records by kind (battle, siege, conquest, war, campaign, raid, revolt, civil-war, skirmish, naval-battle, mutiny) and by era, at `/{lang}/battles/ghazawat/`, `/{lang}/battles/kind/<kind>/` and `/{lang}/battles/era/<period>/`. No new class and no schema change — every card leads to the canonical `event` page. Exported at `/api/v1/battles.json` (with the derived `ghazwa` flag); the Explore entry ships marked «قيد الإعداد» (`ready: false`). Note: the Explore menu sits in `BaseLayout`, so this entry rewrites every page — batch it with the weekly deploy.
- **Proposal: the Battles, Wars and Conquests Browser (plan 31).** A new plan document proposes «متصفح الغزوات والحروب والفتوحات»: index pages over the existing military-kind `event` records — a prophetic section split into ghazawat and saraya by a graph derivation, pages by kind and by era — with no schema change, plus an enrichment lane for `sides`/`outcome`/`part_of` and newly mined engagements from the filed canon.
- **The Companions Browser — متصفح الصحابة (`/{lang}/companions/`).** A new front door over the museum's 606 Companion records, in Arabic, English and Urdu. The home page shows the Ten promised Paradise, the four circles (the Muhajirun, the Ansar, the Ahl al-Bayt, the Mothers of the Believers), the women Companions, clans and tribes, the events Companions took part in, deaths by Hijri decade, and an A-to-Z list with a name filter. Each group, event and decade has its own page. Everything is read from the existing graph — no new class or data — and every name links to its record. Also in the Explore menu and on the landing page, with abstract art (no figures). Plan: `docs/plan/29-companions-browser.md`.
- **`/api/v1/companions.json`.** Every Companion record with gender, roles, dates, the Ten flag, circle and clan groups, events, the Hijri death year and decade (flagged when converted from the Gregorian date), connections and prose languages. Documented in `docs/data/README.md`, the OpenAPI file and `llms.txt`.

### Fixed
- **Fixed: bare one-to-three-digit years no longer read as decades.** The EDTF parser treated an unpadded `"617"` as the 6170s (year ×10), which flipped chronology — the Time Browser's gate caught 39 "event before birth" inversions and person spans were inflated tenfold in every timeline and year snapshot. `edtfRange` now zero-pads each side of an interval to four digits, and the ten records the gate flagged were corrected: five "dossier" event relations (later decrees filed on the original treaty/expulsion/raid records) were re-typed `had_participant` → `related_to` keeping their roles and sources, and four death dates were set to the sourced ranges. A wider audit logged 182 anachronistic participant edges for a follow-up data-cleanliness pass.
### Data
- **Companions: 24 Companion records filled in from al-Isaba (Companions Browser Phase 5, batch 2).** Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba was read again with Apple Vision column OCR, and each fact is cited to its printed page.
  - Eleven Companions who had only a placeholder card now have a summary and a short article in Arabic, English and Urdu. Examples are al-Harith ibn Uqba and his uncle, killed at Uhud; Khuzayma ibn Aws, killed at the Battle of the Bridge; and Khudayj ibn Salama, at the second pledge of Aqaba. They also get their clan (Aws, Khazraj, Banu al-Najjar, Banu Salima, the Umayyads), their Ansar membership, and the battles they fought in, from Badr and Uhud to the Bridge. Where known, their place of death is added too.
  - Thirteen well-known Companions now have their Hijri death year from al-Isaba, with the place of death where it is given. They include Anas ibn Malik (93 AH, Basra), Usama ibn Zayd (54 AH, al-Jurf), Khabbab ibn al-Aratt (37 AH, Kufa) and al-Bara ibn Malik (20 AH, Tustar). Each replaces an uncited approximate year in the Gregorian calendar. Where reports differ, the date is marked debated and the other years are named.
  - Five uncited dates are removed because al-Isaba contradicts them. Examples: a birth after the person had already fought at Badr, and a death year that the cited book does not give.
- **Companions: wrong dates and three wrong roles fixed (Companions Browser Phase 5, batch 1).**
  - 29 birth and death dates came from the date-enrichment pass, which had matched the wrong namesake. Examples: Abu Khaythama got the hadith scholar Zuhayr ibn Harb's dates (d. 234 AH), and Amina bint Khalf a death year of 1275 CE. All 29 are removed. Each was a birth after 632 CE or an impossible death year on a Companion. The real dates come back from the Companion dictionaries in later batches.
  - Three later figures were tagged as Companions and are no longer: Abbasa bint al-Fadl (the wife of Ahmad ibn Hanbal), Umm Musa al-Qahramana (the Abbasid stewardess) and Yusuf ibn Mirdaw (12th century). The Companions Browser now lists 603 Companions.

Twenty new cited edges were added — Badr for al-Arqam, Hatib ibn Abi Balta'a, Bishr and Khubayb; the Aqaba pledges for al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur, As'ad and Bishr; the conquest of Mecca and Hunayn for al-Huwaytib; clan membership in Banu Makhzum, Hashim, Salima, al-Najjar and Abd al-Ashhal; and the Muhajirun circle for al-Arqam and Hatib — all keyed to al-Isaba page numbers.

- **Companions: seven more records get cited Hijri death years and edges (Phase 5, batch 23).** Salim, the freedman of Abu Hudhayfa (12, cut down holding the Yamama flag with both arms gone), Salama ibn Aslam (13, the Bridge), Sa'id ibn al-Harith al-Sahmi (15, Ajnadayn or Yarmuk debated), Salama ibn al-Mayla' (8, killed astray on the day of the conquest), Salit ibn Amr (3, Uhud), Samura ibn Jundab (~60, debated) and Salman ibn Amir al-Dabbi — the only Companion of Banu Dabba (in Uthman's caliphate). Sa'id gains Abyssinia and Sahm edges.
- **Companions: six more records get cited Hijri death years and edges (Phase 5, batch 24).** Suhayl ibn Amr (18 AH of the Amwas plague — he stayed in Syria ribat-ing and never returned to Mecca), Sulayman ibn Surad (65 at Ayn al-Warda, the ninety-three-year-old leader of the Tawwabun), Shammas ibn Uthman (3, the only Uhud casualty buried at al-Baqi'), Sinan ibn Abi Sinan (32), Sufyan ibn Awf al-Ghamidi of the summer expeditions (53, with 52 and 54 named) and Sufyan ibn Ma'mar al-Jumahi (in Umar's caliphate, an Ansari Zurayqi adopted into Jumah — he gains the Abyssinia edge).
- **Companions: five more records get cited Hijri death years and edges (Phase 5, batch 25).** Talha ibn Ubaydallah (36 AH — Marwan's arrow at the Camel, aged sixty-four), Thabit ibn Qays (12 at al-Yamama — his bequeathed armour ratified by Abu Bakr), Ubada ibn al-Samit (34 at al-Ramla, with Bayt al-Maqdis and 45 named), Ubada ibn al-Khashkhash (3 at Uhud) and Suwayd ibn al-Nu'man, who gains Uhud, Khaybar and the Ridwan-pledge notes.
- **Companions: six records gain cited clan, pledge and campaign edges (Phase 5, batch 26).** Umm Ruman joins the Muhajirun (died in the Prophet's lifetime); Umm Mubashshir, Umm Qays bint Mihsan (who witnessed Khaybar per Ibn Sa'd), Umm Atiyya, Umm Mu'adh and Umm Hisham gain Ansar and Banu al-Najjar membership.
- **Companions: seven more records gain cited dates and edges (Phase 5, batch 27).** Umm Salama's debated death (63 AH per al-Waqidi, weighed against Sa'd ibn Zayd's 50-52) and Unays ibn Qatada's martyrdom at Uhud are dated; Umm Sharik joins Banu Abd al-Ashhal, Umm Ziyad and Umm Sinan gain the women's Khaybar expeditions, Ka'b ibn Ju'ayl gains Siffin and Usama ibn Sharik the Farewell Pilgrimage.
- **Companions: eight more records gain cited dates and edges (Phase 5, batch 28).** Uthman ibn Talha (42 AH at Medina, Ajnadayn rejected), Wathila ibn al-Asqa (83 or 85, last Companion to die at Damascus), Waqid ibn Abdullah (early in Umar's caliphate), Uthman ibn Hunayf (in Mu'awiya's caliphate) and Uthman ibn Maz'un (2 AH) are dated; Uthman ibn Abd Ghanm and Uthman ibn Rabi'a join the Abyssinia emigrants, and Ya'la ibn Umayya gains Hunayn and Tabuk.
- **Companions: nine more records gain cited dates and edges (Phase 5, batch 29).** Yazid ibn al-Harith (martyred at Badr, casting dates into his palm), Yazid ibn Qays ibn al-Khatim (martyred at the Bridge of Abu Ubayd, 13 AH, after twelve wounds at Uhud), Zayd ibn al-Khattab (12 at al-Yamama, the banner-bearer Umar mourned), Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani (78 or 68 at Medina), Zayd ibn Thabit (45 per the majority — "the learned man of this umma") and Zaynab bint al-Harith (died returning from Abyssinia) are dated; three more Yazids gain Aqaba and Badr edges.
- **Companions: six more records gain cited dates and edges (Phase 5, batch 30).** The first records drawn from al-Isti'ab for this wave: Amir ibn Fuhayra (4 AH, martyred at Bi'r Ma'una) and A'isha bint al-Harith (died returning from Abyssinia, like her sister Zaynab); Anas ibn Mu'adh is debated between Bi'r Ma'una and Uthman's caliphate; al-Harith ibn Arfaja, Bujayr ibn Abi Bujayr and Abu Qays ibn al-Aslat gain Badr, Aws and Ansar edges.
- **Companions: nine more records gain cited dates and edges (Phase 5, batch 31).** Habbar ibn Sufyan is dated 13 AH at Ajnadayn (al-Waqidi preferred over Mu'ta); Kharash ibn al-Simma gains Badr and Uhud, Khudayj ibn Salama the second Aqaba; Hisham ibn Abi Hudhayfa, Mahmiyya ibn al-Jaz and Busra bint Safwan join the Abyssinia and Hijra emigrants; Jabbar ibn Sakhr joins the Ansar and two Fatimas gain Quraysh clan edges.
- **Companions: eight more records gain cited dates and edges (Phase 5, batch 32).** Sa'id ibn Khalid (13 at Marj al-Suffar, born in Abyssinia), Shayba ibn Uthman (59, ancestor of the Ka'ba keepers), Suhayb al-Rumi (38 at Medina, buried at al-Baqi') and Umm Haram bint Milhan (in the Cyprus campaign, wife of Ubada) are dated; Musa ibn al-Harith joins the children who died in Abyssinia, Ulba ibn Zayd the weepers of Tabuk, and Umm Ayyub and Umm Hani their circles.
- **Companions: two more records gain cited dates and edges (Phase 5, batch 33).** Uwaym ibn Sa'ida — at both Aqaba pledges, Badr, Uhud and the Trench — is debated between the Prophet's lifetime and Umar's caliphate; Wadi'a ibn Amr, the Juhani ally of Banu Sawad, gains Badr and Uhud.
- **Companions: seven more records gain cited dates and edges (Phase 5, batch 34).** Ruwayfi' ibn Thabit (56 AH, amir of Barqa) is dated; al-Mujadhdhar ibn Dhiad gains Badr (he killed Abu al-Bakhtari there); Ku'ayba bint Sa'd the women's Khaybar, Rufayda the Trench tent where Sa'd was nursed, Yusayra the first emigrant women, Amina bint Khalf the Abyssinia emigration with Khalid ibn Sa'id, and Sumayya — the first martyr — the early Muslims.
- **Companions: two more records gain cited dates and edges (Phase 5, batch 35).** Arbad ibn Humayra — read by Ibn Makula as ibn Humayr — joins the Abyssinia emigrants and the men of Badr; al-Harith al-Hamdani is dated to the end of Mu'awiya's days.
- **Companions: three more records gain cited dates and edges (Phase 5, batch 36 — queue exhausted).** Dhu al-Shamalayn — Umayr ibn Abd Amr, ally of Banu Zuhra — is dated 2 AH at Badr; Qurayba bint Abi Umayya, Umm Salama's sister, joins Banu Makhzum; and Umm al-Mundhir Salma bint Qays joins the Najjar of the Ansar. With this batch every remaining record in the enrichment queue has been reviewed against the dictionaries.

## v1.5.1 — 2026-11-09

### Added
- **The Khulafa Browser «متصفح الخلفاء» (plan 30, founder-approved).** The caliphs of Islam are browsable at `/{lang}/khulafa/`: ~160 caliphs as ordinary `person` records, grouped by the caliphate they ruled — Rashidun, Umayyad, Cordoba, Abbasid Baghdad and the ceremonial Cairo line, Fatimid, Almohad, Ottoman and Sokoto — with the Zubayrid, Hammudid and Sharifian counter-caliphates labelled as claims last. Each caliph page at `/{lang}/khulafa/<slug>/` shows his reign, his predecessor/successor strip inside the chain, the events his reign saw (the new `during_reign`/`reign_saw` predicate), and `perspectives` where the accession is contested. Exported at `/api/v1/khulafa.json` and `/api/v1/khulafa/chains.json`; landing card and Explore entry included.
- **The Asma ul Husna Browser «متصفح أسماء الله الحسنى» (plan 29, founder-approved).** The ninety-nine names of God are now records in the graph: 99 `concept` entities of the new kind `divine-name`, ordered on the Tirmidhi enumeration with transliteration, lexical root and `part_of` the umbrella `concept/asma-allah-al-husna`, each citing Jami' al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Qayyim's Jala' al-Afham. The browser at `/{lang}/asma/` shows the numbered grid with a vowel-insensitive filter, and each name's page at `/{lang}/asma/<slug>/` groups its cited stories — Qur'an passages, hadith, seerah events, Companions and the righteous — from `mentions`/`exemplifies` edges (seeded with the Hashr close 59:22–24, ayat al-kursi, the Fatiha and al-Isra 17:110, and Muslim 2677), plus curated trilingual prose as it lands. Exported at `/api/v1/asma.json`; landing card and Explore entry included. Schema gained `divine-name` plus `order`/`name_meta` on concept, and the validator now requires each name's order, enumeration and source.
- **Asma browser phase 4: stories and full edges.** Each name's story sections are now populated: 850 text-verified `mentions` edges (computed against each passage's own normalized text) give every name its real Qur'an and hadith occurrences; `exemplifies` edges carry sahaba/saliheen stories (Bilal, Salman, Rabi'a, Uways); 21 `related_to` pairs join the paired names; and all 99 names gained trilingual prose (brief, «في القرآن», «في السنة», people-stories) at draft tier with provenance.
- **Proposal: the Asma ul Husna Browser (plan 29).** A new plan document proposes «متصفح أسماء الله الحسنى»: the ninety-nine names of God as `concept` records of a new kind `divine-name` under the existing `concept/asma-allah-al-husna` umbrella, ordered on the Tirmidhi list with Ibn Majah differences labelled. Each name would get a page at `/[lang]/asma/<slug>/` grouping its cited stories — Qur'an passages, hadith, seerah events, sahaba and saliheen — through the existing `mentions`/`exemplifies` edges plus curated trilingual prose, with a `/api/v1/asma.json` export. It is a proposal only: no schema, data, site or i18n changes until the founder approves it.
- **Proposal: the Khulafa Browser «متصفح الخلفاء» (plan 30).** A new plan document proposes the caliphs browser: every caliph stays an ordinary `person` record, carrying a cited `story_roles`/`ruled_over` reign toward its caliphate `polity`, grouped as Rashidun, Umayyad, Cordoba, Abbasid Baghdad and Cairo, Fatimid, Almohad, Ottoman and Sokoto — plus labelled rival claims (Zubayrid, Hammudid, Sharifian) and the ceremonial Cairo line. Each caliph page at `/[lang]/khulafa/<slug>/` would show the reign in both calendars, the predecessor/successor chain, the events, buildings and works of the reign through a proposed `during_reign` predicate, the realm map, and `perspectives` where the accession is contested; exports at `/api/v1/khulafa.json` and `/api/v1/khulafa/chains.json`. A roster dataset drives the audit of ~140–160 caliphs; missing person records and reign edges are mined from the filed canon (Suyuti's Tarikh al-Khulafa, Tabari, EI2…) and harvested sources. It is a proposal only: no schema, data, site or i18n changes until the founder approves it.

### Data
- **Khulafa Browser data spine (plan 30).** The roster `datasets/khulafa-roster.csv` maps ~160 caliphs across 8 caliphates plus three labelled claims; every roster row now has `roles: [caliph]`, a cited `story_roles` reign, `ruled_over` and `successor_of` edges (Suyuti's Tarikh al-Khulafa, Ibn Idhari, Sicill-i Osmani, al-Maqrizi). Thirty missing person records were created (Cordoba, Cairo-line, Ottoman and Sokoto caliphs), and four polity records were added: `zubayrid-caliphate`, `hammudid-caliphate`, `abbasid-caliphate-cairo` (the ceremonial Cairo line) and `sharifian-caliphate`.
- **Khulafa Browser schema spine (plan 30).** The `during_reign`/`reign_saw` predicate is registered — events, buildings, works and inventions can now cite whose reign they fall under; the validator requires a person whose `story_roles` reign (or rival claim) points to a `caliphate` polity to carry `roles: [caliph]`, and warns where a `caliph` role still lacks its recorded reign. `person/hasan-ibn-ali` gains the `caliph` role for his six-month reign, the first record the new rule caught.
- **Provenance recorded for the 3D tour's records.** Thirteen records shown in the 3D tour previously failed the publication-standard cite-check on missing provenance. Eight (Junoon, the OIC, three living-culture listings, Fatima al-Fihri, Mimar Sinan, iftar practice and al-Fihrist) now carry a top-level `provenance` block naming the cited sources and the generating run. The five object records (Andalus dirhams, Umar ibn Yusuf's astrolabe, Birmingham mushaf, Iznik bottle, V&A mosque lamp) cannot carry one — the object schema declares `provenance` an array while the base schema declares it an object — so `cite-check` now honours their `status.generated_by` plus cited-sources convention instead. `npm run cite-check` on all 53 tour-referenced records: 0 fail.

### Fixed
- **Unbreak `main`: duplicate YAML keys in 513 place and person records.** Yesterday's geocoding and date-enrichment batches added a new `coordinates` / `coordinate_precision` / `coordinate_note` triple (466 place files) or a second identical `died:` line (47 person files) without removing the old line, and in nine files inserted the triple inside a list, so `npm run graph`, `npm run validate` and the build all stopped with "Map keys must be unique". Each file now keeps the new geocoded triple and drops the superseded "no reliably attested coordinates" note and precision; no coordinate, date or source value was changed.
- **Unbreak `main`: Urdu map-viewer strings mis-keyed under `hadith`.** Yesterday's Urdu map-viewer copy landed as `hadith.viewer.*` instead of `map.viewer.*` — the i18n parity gate failed (37 ur-only keys) and Urdu map chrome rendered raw key paths. Moved the block under `map:`; ar/en/ur key sets are identical again.
- **Unbreak `main`: MapViewer missing quote.** Yesterday's map-viewer merge left an unterminated string in the Arabic edge-label table (`born_in: "وُلد في` had no closing quote), so `npm run build` failed before any page compiled. Restored the quote; the site builds again.
- **3D tour QA fixes (`/{lang}/3d/`).** (1) Enter now crosses the doorway the visitor is facing even while a top-bar or strip button holds focus — jumps also move keyboard focus onto the 3D canvas, so the "press Enter to go through the doorway" prompt finally does what it says right after entry and after strip/map jumps. (2) The Exit button opens an in-page confirm dialog instead of `window.confirm` (which embedded/webview contexts can silently suppress, leaving a dead-looking button); confirming disposes the scene and returns to the museum home, cancelling restores focus to the tour. (3) First visit now shows a real spinner plus a line explaining that the 3D engine downloads once and later visits are fast; the load watchdog was raised from 9 s to 60 s, re-arms once the three.js import resolves, and can no longer declare failure after init succeeded. (4) The Umayyad dirham close-up is no longer a blank grey disc — both faces carry a stylised inscription-band-and-field coin face with a milled rim (still a stand-in model; the honest note stays), and closer-scene texture maps are now disposed on close. (5) Floating exhibit/wing label sprites clamp to at most 60% of the viewport width and shrink as their anchor nears a screen edge, so long Arabic names can no longer run off-screen. (6) The entry-card and page ledes in Arabic and English no longer claim the wing galleries are "on the way" — all nine are open today (the Urdu copy already said so). New i18n keys `tour.loading_first`, `tour.exit_yes`, `tour.exit_stay` ship in ar/en/ur in the same commit.

## v1.5.0 — 2026-11-09

### Fixed
- **Validation repair after the geo-enrichment merge.** `data/place/kufa.yaml` now quotes its `founded.edtf` year ("0638") so the date schema validates again, and the 3D tour's `tour/halls.yaml` Medina stop lists `source/wikidata` (and the Cordoba stop likewise) to match the records' updated source lists.

### Added
- **The Islam Map Viewer.** The Place wing (`/{lang}/place/`) now opens into a full-screen interactive map of the Islamic world: twelve hand-drawn regions on a Natural Earth world outline, collision-free place markers inside each region, city orbit and focus views that draw the real graph edges (people, events, buildings, works, journeys one hop from each place), a Hijri time slider from 74 BH to 1448 AH that dims everything outside its year, free pan and zoom, a parent-level preview button, and a black/ivory-gold theme toggle. All geometry is computed at build time from `world-atlas` topojson and the compiled graph — nothing is fetched at runtime — and readers without JavaScript still get the schematic MiniMap. The landing page and the Explore menu gain a localized "Islam map" card in Arabic, English and Urdu.
- **Wave 199 — the Kurdish scene joins the modern-figures graph.** Four people and two channel brands from Iraqi Kurdistan's Sorani dawah scene, each with dated audience counts: reciter Peshawa Qadir Al-Kurdi (1.67M YouTube subscribers), Sulaymaniyah Friday preacher Muhammad Mala Fayaq Sharazoori (398K), surgeon-professor and preacher Dr Abdulwahid Muhammed Salih (1.7M Facebook followers), Kifri preacher Mamosta Sabah Kifri (280K), and the Bangawaz TV (2.7M) and Tebinni Islam (117K) lecture channels — the brands name no individual operator, and the records say so honestly rather than inventing one.
- **Wave 199 §C — the founder-cleared Kurdish pair.** Abdullatif Ahmad Mustafa, the Sulaymaniyah preacher who founded Amozhgari TV, and the channel itself (1.8M Facebook followers) join the graph, built on the founder's ruling with the full public record carried openly in the entries — including his July 2026 dismissal from his university post after an official investigation, his denial of the allegations, and the fact that no criminal conviction is reported.

### Fixed
- **Place map QA fixes.** The Islam Map Viewer now lives in the page flow instead of a fixed full-screen overlay, so `/ar/place/`, `/en/place/` and `/ur/place/` scroll normally by touch and mouse and the card list below is reachable; vertical swipes scroll the page while horizontal drags pan the map. Pan is clamped to the zoom so the map can no longer be dragged off-stage; the toolbar is no longer clipped under the sticky header; the year step arrows work in all three languages with direction and icons matching each page's text direction; and all map chrome (breadcrumb, controls, year label, aria-labels) is localized through `map.viewer.*` keys in Arabic, English and Urdu. Early-year region highlighting now only inherits dates through place-dating predicates (born/died/lived/ruled/occurred), so 11 AH no longer lights up the whole map. Detail pages gain Urdu region names via `schema/enums/regions.yaml` and a safe label fallback, and the "In time" strip no longer clips its edge year labels.
- **Islam map requirements doc.** `docs/engineering/19-islam-map-requirements.md` records the map's full requirement set — palette, basemap, camera bounds, time slider, drill-down, orbits, localization, accessibility — with a production test checklist for validation.
