## v1.30.0 — 2026-11-14
### Added
- **The Medicine Browser opens** (متصفح الطب النبوي والطب والتشريح والجراحة والدواء والتداوي في الإسلام) at `/{lang}/tibb/`, in Arabic, English and Urdu, with a card on the home page and an entry in the Explore menu. It gathers in one place everything the museum's sources say about six subjects: prophetic medicine, medicine and illness, anatomy, surgery, drugs, and seeking treatment. A reader can go from the verse on the healing in honey to the reports on cupping and black seed, to Ibn al-Qayyim's chapters in Zad al-Ma'ad, to a page of Ibn Sina's Canon, and to the record of the physician or the hospital, each with its source. The page opens with a view of its own, "the apothecary's jars": six shelves, one for each subject, with a jar for every remedy, disease or procedure the texts name — cupping, honey, black seed, fever, plague, the stages of creation, the treatment of wounds — filled to the level of how often the sources mention it. A jar with a gold lid opens the museum's record on it.
- **A medical text in any book harvested later appears by itself.** The browser finds its passages when the site is built, by a guarded word list, so nothing has to be tagged. The guards keep out the words that only look medical: the "disease" of the hypocrites' hearts, the protected pasture that is spelled like "fever", the "justice" that is spelled like the drug costus, the honey of Paradise, and the wounds of the compensation chapters.
- **The medicine dataset** at `/api/v1/tibb.json`, described in the OpenAPI file, `llms.txt` and the data guide: every record with its section, its subjects and the words that admitted it.
### Data
- **al-Thurayya links added to fifteen more places.** Jaffa, Yazd, Zanjan, Oran, Khujand, Tayma, Yanbu, Zarqa, Zubala, Zibatra and five more now point to their record in the al-Thurayya gazetteer, matched by exact Arabic name and by position within 7 km. This completes the al-Thurayya files whose names match one of our places, 343 in all, apart from the Ascalon place and ambiguous names.
- **Nomisma links added to Qalawun, Kayqubad I and Qaytbay.** Their Nomisma concept pages fail for names with an apostrophe, so each concept was read through Nomisma's query service instead and confirmed to name the same ruler.
- **Biblissima identifiers added to eighteen more scholars.** al-Busiri, Ibn Ajurrum, Qadi Iyad, Ibn Abi al-Hadid, al-Firuzabadi, Zakariyya al-Ansari, Ibn al-Salah, al-Sha'rani, Fakhr al-Din Iraqi, Sultan Walad, Juwayriyya bint al-Harith and seven more now carry their Biblissima record number, each accepted only because Biblissima's Wikidata link matches ours. Two further matches with year gaps join the founder's list in the progress note.
- **al-Thurayya links added to 25 further places.** Palmyra, Sidon, Sinjar, Siraf, Tabuk, Taif, Qus, Rashid (Rosetta), Shibam, Kandahar, Qinnasrin and fourteen more now point to their record in the al-Thurayya gazetteer, matched by exact Arabic name and by position within 7 km. Only the link and the source were added.
- **iDAI.gazetteer links added to 19 more places.** Sivas, Erzurum, Bitlis, Sinop, Izmir, Iskenderun, Aksum, Asilah, Qina, Mallawi, Kastamonu, Gebze and seven more now carry their German Archaeological Institute gazetteer number, each accepted only when exactly one populated place within 1.5 km matched our GeoNames number or Arabic name.
- **1,033 hadith reports on medicine** from the two Sahihs, the four Sunan and the Muwatta (the hadith-api Arabic editions), each a short excerpt with its collection and number: the Book of Medicine and the Book of the Sick, cupping, cautery, ruqya, honey, black seed, fever, plague, contagion, visiting the sick, the treatment of the wounded.
- **650 short excerpts from books already scanned and read by machine**: Zad al-Ma'ad, the two Dala'il al-Nubuwwa, Hilyat al-Awliya', al-Isaba, Usd al-Ghaba, al-Isti'ab, Hayat al-Sahaba, Sifat al-Safwa, Ibn Sina's Canon, Ibn al-Nafis's Commentary on the Anatomy of the Canon and al-Razi's al-Hawi. Each is forty words at most, cited to its book and scan page; the machine-read text is not corrected, and every record is a draft until a human reads it.
- **230 existing records now belong to the browser**: physicians from al-Harith ibn Kalada and Rufayda al-Aslamiyya to al-Razi, Ibn Sina, al-Zahrawi and Ibn al-Nafis, the hospitals, the medical books, the plagues, the medical inventions and the fatwas on treatment.
- **New records with full prose in three languages**: prophetic medicine and its remedies (black seed, cautery, talbina, costus, senna, truffles, ithmid, fever, ladud and sa'ut), surgery, venesection, bone-setting, the care of the wounded in the Prophet's time, simple and compound drugs, and theriac and poisons, written from Zad al-Ma'ad, the Canon and the hadith collections with page and number.
### Tests
- The detector's rules are tested one by one (`scripts/tibb.test.ts`), and the founder's original request is kept with a production check-list in `docs/engineering/47-tibb-browser-requirements.md`.
## v1.29.1 — 2026-11-14
### Added
- **Du'a by occasion: comprehensive supplications.** The division of al-Adhkar on supplications for all times is open with one record: what al-Nawawi gathers on the merit of supplication and the short, all-embracing wordings from Sahih Muslim and the two Sahihs, each with its page.

### Changed
- **The museum's block on terrorist-organisation content now covers the full official designation lists.** The screening patterns behind the build's extremism check were compared, name by name, with the terrorist-organisation lists published by the European Union, the United States (State Department and Treasury), Canada, the United Nations Security Council, the United Kingdom, Australia and New Zealand, and every Islam-linked organisation on those lists that the check did not already catch is now caught — among them JNIM, the Abdallah Azzam Brigades, Al-Murabitoun, the Caucasus Emirate, Egyptian Islamic Jihad, the Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, Lashkar-e-Jhangvi and Hizbul Mujahideen, together with spelling variants that previously slipped through (GIA and the Gama'a al-Islamiyya, long named in the rule, are now actually matched). Nothing already in the museum was removed or changed: the collection is the golden reference, and the handful of designated names whose patterns would also catch records the founder has kept are documented in the content-safety rule for his decision.
### Data
- **Ten more persons read from al-Zirikli's al-A'lam.** Taha Surur, Muhammad Amin al-Shirwani (Sadreddinzade), Nuh ibn Mustafa, Ibn Abd al-Qawi al-Mardawi, Muhammad Abu Zahra, Sultan ibn Saif al-Ya'ribi (labelled Ibadi), Tawba al-Anbari, Abd al-Salam ibn Mashish, Ali ibn Ahmad al-Mahaimi and Ahmad ibn Kayghalagh now carry short cited biographies in Arabic, English and Urdu (draft), each from the entry itself with its volume and page. Four cards corrected to the entry: Ibn Abd al-Qawi died 1299 (not 1300), Sultan ibn Saif 1680 (not 1679), Ibn Mashish 1225 (not 1227), and Ibn Kayghalagh was born about 872 (not about 904); Abu Zahra is no longer described as a Maliki.

## v1.29.0 — 2026-11-13
### Added
- **Du'a by occasion: miscellaneous remembrances.** The division of al-Adhkar that gathers scattered chapters is open: the record on the manners of a gathering gains what al-Nawawi reports on the words said when rising from one, the supplication for those present, and the dislike of leaving without remembering God, each with its page.
- **Du'a by occasion: guarding the tongue.** The division of al-Adhkar on speech is open: the record on guarding the tongue gains al-Nawawi's rule that one speaks only where the benefit is plain, and the reports he gathers for it from the two Sahihs and al-Tirmidhi, each with its page.
- **Du'a by occasion: names.** The division of al-Adhkar on names is open: the record on naming gains al-Nawawi's chapters on the call to prayer in a newborn's ear, the prayer for blessing at the tahnik, the day of naming and the names he reports as dearest, each with its page.
- **Du'a by occasion: marriage.** The division of al-Adhkar on marriage is open: the record on the marriage contract gains what al-Nawawi gathers on the address before the contract, the words said to the groom, and the supplication on the wedding night, each with its page.
- **Du'a by occasion: greeting.** The division of al-Adhkar on greeting, asking leave and sneezing is open: the record on the greeting of peace gains al-Nawawi's reports on its merit, the best wording and reply, and his ruling on beginning and returning it, each with its page.
- **Du'a by occasion: travel.** The division of al-Adhkar on the traveller is open with one record: what al-Nawawi gathers for setting out and for farewell, from consulting and istikhara to the words «أستودع الله دينك وأمانتك وخواتيم عملك» and the supplication for the traveller's piety, each with its page.
- **Du'a by occasion: the campaign.** The division of al-Adhkar on the campaign is open with one record: what al-Nawawi gathers on asking sincerely for martyrdom, the supplication at the digging of the Trench and the pleading before battle, from the two Sahihs and the Sunan, each with its page.
- **Du'a by occasion: breaking the fast.** The fasting division gains a third record: the record on iftar now carries the supplications al-Nawawi gathers for breaking the fast, with the books he assigns them to and their page.
- **Du'a by occasion: particular prayers.** The division of al-Adhkar on Friday and the two Eids is open: the records on the Friday prayer and on Eid al-Fitr gain what al-Nawawi says of the remembrances of Friday and its hour, and of the takbir of the two Eids, its times and its wordings, each with its page.
- **Du'a by occasion: illness and death.** The division of al-Adhkar on illness is open: the record on visiting the sick gains what al-Nawawi gathers on what the sick person says and what is said to him, from the two Sahihs and the Sunan, each with its page.
- **Du'a by occasion: matters that arise.** The division of al-Adhkar that opens with istikhara is open: the record on istikhara gains al-Nawawi's account of the supplication from Sahih al-Bukhari, the rulings he attaches to it, and his judgement on two weaker reports. One attribution in the section on asking blessing on the Prophet, added earlier today, is corrected to what the page gives (Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayra).
- **Du'a by occasion: asking blessing on the Prophet.** The division of al-Adhkar on this is open: the existing record gains the reports al-Nawawi gathers on its merit and on doing so when he is mentioned, and his rejection of one added phrase, each with its page.
- **Du'a by occasion: praising God.** The division of al-Adhkar on praise is open: the record on «الحمد لله» gains al-Nawawi's account of when praise is recommended, the report that a matter not begun with it is cut short, and the wording of the most complete praise, each with its page.
- **Du'a by occasion: reciting the Qur'an.** The division of al-Nawawi's al-Adhkar on recitation is open: the record on completing the Qur'an gains what he says of how often the early generations completed it, his own view that it depends on the person, and the times he prefers, each with its page.
- **The Du'a Browser can be read by occasion.** It was arranged only by where a supplication is found (the Qur'an, the Sunnah, the seerah, other books). It now also has "By occasion", following the divisions of al-Nawawi's al-Adhkar in the book's own order, with a page for each division that holds a record. The first sixteen records are written from the book itself, chapter by chapter: on waking, dressing, leaving and entering the house, the toilet, ablution, going to and entering the mosque, hearing the call to prayer, distress, fright, the new moon, the Night of Power, the talbiya, food, and the chief supplication for forgiveness. Each gives the reports al-Nawawi cites, the books he assigns them to and his own gradings, with the supplication in his wording and its page in the edition read (al-Arna'ut, Dar al-Fikr, 1994, on al-Maktaba al-Shamila). Six of the twenty divisions are open; the page says so. Arabic, English and Urdu; AI-written drafts, marked as such. In the API each du'a record carries its `occasion`.
- **Two verses the audit named now have their commentary.** 36:58 and 112:1 showed "no commentary filed yet", because the museum's digests of al-Tabari stop at the sixteenth volume of the Shakir edition. Their Tafsir sections now carry a digest written from the al-Turki edition (vol. 19, pp. 466-469; vol. 24, pp. 727-730), read on al-Maktaba al-Shamila: the grammarians' readings al-Tabari reports, the reports he cites and the reading he prefers, each sentence cited to its page. Two volume records and two source records for that edition are added, and the Tafsir Browser's volume list is headed "read by the museum" now that it spans two editions. Arabic, English and Urdu; AI text, labelled as such on the page.
- **The Tafsir Browser starts from the verse.** The page used to open with two lists, "Commentaries, 23 entries" and "Volumes, 16 entries", and the sixteen volumes were one work in one edition. It now opens with "Read by verse": the surahs that carry commentary, each with its count (al-Baqara: 284 of 286 verses), then the verses of the surah, then the commentary on the verse. From the landing to al-Tabari on 2:255 is two clicks. The surahs the digests have not reached are named as such. New pages: `/{lang}/tafsir/surah/<n>/` for the 14 surahs covered today.
- **Every verse page has a Tafsir section.** The 1,715 verses with a digest of al-Tabari had it inside "Place in the museum", unlabelled. The same paragraphs, unchanged, now stand under the heading Tafsir, with the commentator, the work and the volume cited, each a link. A verse with no digest says so in one sentence: how many commentaries the catalogue holds, which one is read verse by verse so far, and that it has not reached this verse. Nothing is borrowed from another verse.
- **Surah pages lead to their commentary.** The surah's record page and its surah map both carry "Tafsir on this surah" with the count of verses covered and a link to them.
- **`/{lang}/quran/` opens.** It answered "page not found". It is now a short door to the Mushaf, the Surah maps, the Tafsir Browser and the order of revelation. The Mushaf and the Surah maps each say in one sentence what the other is for.
- **The Signs of the Hour Browser is about the signs of the Hour.** It held all 2,621 eschatology records, most of what the Resurrection, Paradise and Fire browsers hold. Its landing now holds the 114 records about the signs and reads them in order: the signs in general, the Mahdi, the Dajjal, Yajuj and Majuj, the Hour itself, the museum's own records before the passages at each step. The page says the order is the customary one of the creed books and that no text fixes it. Nothing is deleted: the full index by source is at `/{lang}/signs/all/`, and all four landings carry the same short block saying what each browser holds.
- **Journeys have a front door.** The Explore menu opened one journey, the Hijra, and the other forty-nine could only be found in the class listing. `/{lang}/journeys/` lists all fifty by kind, each with its stations in order, and every journey page links back to the list and on to journeys of its kind.
- **Every Hijri month has an address.** `/{lang}/calendar/1447/9/` opens Ramadan 1447 as a plain page: its days with their Gregorian twins, its observances, and links to the month before and after; `/{lang}/calendar/1447/` lists the year's months. They exist for the ten years either side of the present Hijri year (1438 to 1458 AH today) and need no JavaScript. The calendar and the converter stay where they were, with links to the months under them.
- **A fatwa can be found from the question.** The Fatwa Explorer was the only browser of its family with no search box, and it was arranged by issuing institution alone. It now has a find box over all 345 fatwas and a "By subject" list: the 183 subjects the fatwas are about, taken from each fatwa's own record, each with its page. The list by source stays, one source to a page. Every one of these pages carries the same sentence: the museum records these fatwas as history and issues no ruling.
- **The Graph Explorer finds an entry by name.** Its box asked for an internal id such as `person/salah-al-din-yusuf-ibn-ayyub`. Typing "Saladin" now offers the entry and makes it the centre. The centres you have visited are listed above the chart with a way back; a filter that is still on is shown beside the box with one button to clear it; and when a name cannot be drawn the box says so itself, instead of a line under the chart.
- **The Time wing and the map take a typed year.** On the Time wing, a year in either calendar opens the century that holds it. On the map, a typed year moves the year bar, and the panel now says what the bar does: it lights the places with dated records in that year and names each region's era; it does not filter a place's own list.
- **Battles can be searched by name where you land.** The Battles landing has a find box over every battle record.
- **The Messengers and Prophets Browser draws the Prophets' Tree.** `/{lang}/messengers/` listed its twenty-five prophets as cards in a grid. It now opens with a drawn tree, Adam at the root and Muhammad at the crown, that can be read at a glance and explored: choosing a prophet lights his way down to the root and opens a card with the basis of his place, his recorded parents and ties, his summary, his mention counts and the link to his page. The tree states only what the graph holds. A solid branch is drawn only where a father-and-son edge is recorded (Ibrahim to Ismail and Ishaq, Ishaq to Ya'qub, Ya'qub to Yusuf, Dawud to Sulayman, Zakariyya to Yahya); the vine from Ismail to Muhammad is the Genealogies Browser's chain, dashed where the genealogists dispute it and solid where they agree; a prophet counted among the progeny in al-An'am 84 to 86 hangs on a dashed twig with the ayah linked; every other place is dotted and labelled as order of mention, not lineage. Every prophet on the tree is an ordinary link, so it works without JavaScript, and "Read the tree as text" gives the same content as a list. In Arabic, English and Urdu, light and dark, phone and desktop. The build fails if a drawn branch has no edge behind it.
- **Twelve browsers open with a view of their own.** Each of these pages used to open with the same grid of cards. Each now opens with a drawing made from its own records, in Arabic, English and Urdu, that can be read at a glance and explored by touch, mouse or keyboard, and that still works as plain links without JavaScript (`docs/site/signature-views.md`):
  - **Asma ul Husna**: the ninety-nine names as beads on one string of three turns, in al-Tirmidhi's order; a bead's core grows with the Qur'an passages linked to the name.
  - **Centuries, Years and Months**: the Hijri year as a wheel, a bar per month for the passages that mention it.
  - **Caliphs**: a lane per caliphate and a segment per reign on one axis in both calendars, so who reigned at the same time can be seen; rival claims are drawn as claims.
  - **Khutab and Durus**: the dated sermons on a Hijri timeline (undated ones in a tray, not placed), and a ring per lecturer for the series the museum holds.
  - **Battles**: the dated records per Hijri century, stacked by kind, and the Prophet's campaigns numbered in order of date on a map of Arabia.
  - **Journeys**: every route on one map, coloured and dashed by kind; choosing a journey brings its stations forward in order.
  - **Sacred Places**: a map of every located place, with magnified lenses on the surroundings of Mecca and Medina.
  - **Companions**: one dot per Companion by the Hijri decade of death; buttons light the Muhajirun, the Ansar, the Household, the Mothers of the Believers, the women or the Ten.
  - **Four Madhhabs**: the four schools as four columns on one time axis, each scholar a lifespan, each book a mark at its author's death, and teacher-to-student lines only where the graph records them.
  - **Fatwa**: the subjects people ask about as circles sized by the number of fatwas, each ringed by the sources that issued them.
  - **Tafsir**: the whole Mushaf as 114 blocks sized by verse count, filled where commentary exists, and re-orderable by order of revelation.
  - **Hadith Qudsi**: themes against the seven collections as a matrix of discs; choosing a disc lists its hadiths.
  Every view states only what the records hold: undated, unlocated and unlinked records are counted in the caption and never placed, and the build fails when a view's fixed layout no longer matches the data.
- **Every browser now opens with a view of its own.** Twenty-seven more browsers join the twelve above; each drawing is made from that browser's records, in Arabic, English and Urdu (`docs/site/signature-views.md`):
  - **Inventions**: a lane per field and a mark per invention at its first attestation, shaped by what became of it. **Jobs**: a market street of tiles sized by the people recorded in each occupation. **Screening Room**: a film strip of decades.
  - **Hisab**: the reward figures the cited texts give, on a ladder where each rung is ten times the one below; a reward stated without a number ends in an open arrow, never a figure. **Hasanat**: shelves of surahs and hadith collections where good deeds are named. **Sayyi'at**: the same question as a stream along the order of revelation.
  - **Paradise and the Fire**: one chart for both, surah by surah, each page lit on its own side. **Resurrection**: the three themes along the order of revelation. **Signs of the Hour**: a road of five stations in the customary order, said to be customary. **Ghayb**: eight doorways for its sections, with the Night Journey's stops as an ascent. **Angels**: a ring of offices drawn with plain discs.
  - **Nature**: six strata from the heavens to the sea. **Jinn & Devils**: which sections its records share. **Magic**: the terms the sources use and where two meet in one record.
  - **Akhlaq**: virtues and vices on two sides of one spine, dealings apart. **Ibadat**: a rosette of the acts of worship with the practice records as beads. **Du'a**: 114 lamps, lit for each surah in which a supplication is recorded.
  - **Miracles**: a loom joining each prophet to the themes of his signs. **Nubuwat**: seven themes as a seven-pointed chart. **Dreams**: constellations by source.
  - **Household of the Prophet**: a family chart drawn only from recorded kinship. **Family and Marriages**: the marriages on record as knots. **Genealogies**: the tribes as trees, only where the records link them.
  - **Mukatabat**: a flow from who sent a letter to where the museum found it. **Islamic Economy**: coin, deed and endowment on three dated ledgers. **Hudud**: a plain index of terms and references, with no ruling and no ranking.
  The same rule holds for all: what the records do not date, locate or link is counted in the caption and left off the drawing.

A lesson page can now carry a depth layer after its cards and before "Try this": **Go deeper** (one scene or source excerpt seen closely), **Why they did it** (the scientist's stated purpose where a source preserves it, and a plain statement where none does), **Two views** and **Often misunderstood** (from Grade 6), **How do we know?** (from Grade 9), **Think about it** (one question that needs a reason, never recall) and **Into the museum** (doors into the people, places, objects and texts behind the lesson). Every factual sentence restates a museum record and carries that record's citation; every interpretive or religious statement names who holds it. ### Changed
- **Gallica and the Walters Art Museum checked, neither registered.** Gallica's terms page is behind a bot challenge and the only archived copy is from 2019, so its present terms cannot be stated. The Walters publishes its images and data under CC0, but its site is behind a bot challenge and its robots file signals that content should not be used as AI input, so there is no machine route to use. The three judgements flagged earlier (the al-Thurayya anchor, the Baptistere date and the Suaire date) are confirmed in the founder's decision record dec-20261114-277.
- **Dates of doubtful origin are checked, and the unchecked ones no longer place anyone in time.** An automated pass of 9 November wrote birth and death years onto 5,835 person records, and where a record's own text could test them it was wrong a quarter of the time. By the founder's decision the rest were compared with Wikidata wherever the record carries an id (2,597 records, 3,904 dates, read on 13 November 2026): 1,407 dates agree with a Wikidata statement that carries a reference and are kept, now cited with the item's revision; 461 that Wikidata contradicts are removed (each is listed and can be restored); the remainder stay untested. A date that is still untested, and that the record's own summary does not state either, no longer puts its person on a timeline, in a sorted list or in the page's machine-readable data: it is shown on the person's own page, marked "Unverified", and nowhere else. That is 4,830 dates on 3,723 people today. The ledger of every comparison is `docs/audit/data/dates-wikidata-ledger.json`; in the API these dates travel as `unverified_dates`.
- **AI-written text that no editor has read now says so where it stands.** By the founder's decision of 13 November 2026: the Tafsir section of the 1,715 verse pages that carry a digest of al-Tabari prints one sentence saying the summaries were written with AI help and not yet read by a human editor; every room of the Grand Tour prints the same under its narrative; and a published record whose opening was rewritten for the Tour (or, for the Kiswa, whose sentences were rewritten this week) prints it at the head of its page. No record's review state changes, no count changes, and a record already marked Draft keeps its one badge. Arabic, English and Urdu.
- **Jibril and Mika'il stand with the angels.** The Jinn & Devils Browser listed them among "Named figures" because they are filed as persons. A person record can now say what kind of being it is, with a source; the two are typed as angels from al-Tabari on 2:98. Iblis, Harut, Marut and Bidukh stay untyped, because the sources themselves differ on what they are.
- **The Companions roll has a page of its own.** The Companions Browser's home ended with the A-to-Z list of every Companion. With the new chart of the generation above it, the home weighed 530 KB, over its 400 KB limit, and the build stopped every pull request on it. The home now shows the first names of the roll and a link to the whole of it at `/{lang}/companions/all/`, where the find-by-name box now lives. The chart is unchanged and the home is 347 KB.
- **A volume page explains itself.** It names the commentary and the commentator it belongs to, with links, lists its coverage surah by surah in words ("Sura 2: Al-Baqara — verses 1–2, 4–43") and states a gap inside its range as a gap ("2:3 — not yet covered") instead of leaving the number out.
- **The catalogue is labelled for what it is.** The volume list is headed "The volumes of Jami' al-Bayan in this edition — 16", each commentary is marked "read verse by verse" or "catalogue entry", and `/api/v1/tafsir.json` gives every row a `role` (commentary or volume), the commentary a volume belongs to (`volume_of`) and its `verses_covered`.
- **The Jinn & Devils Browser lists its records by what they are.** Its Devils section listed Ibn Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud, Adam, Musa and Umm Salama; its Angels section listed Isa and Maryam. Each topic is now divided by the record's own class and kind: the beings themselves, teachings and terms, events, named figures, questions, books. A Companion who narrates a report about devils stands under "Named figures in these accounts", with a sentence saying the museum classes no human as an angel, a jinn or a devil. No record left the browser. The Arabic title reads «متصفح الجن والشياطين», in the order of the English. The feed gives each row its `sections` and `group`.
- **A record no editor has read yet says so the same way everywhere.** 11,771 records had a summary that began "Draft card for …" and ended "… not yet checked on the page", and 2,905 cards in the People hall printed it; pages without an article said "The long-form text for this entry has not been written yet". Those phrases were notes from the build pipeline to itself. They are no longer printed anywhere: the summary shows the description alone, and a draft record carries one badge, "Draft", with one sentence, "Written with AI help from the sources it cites, and not yet read by a human editor", on its own page and at the head of every listing that holds drafts. No record's review state is changed. Verses and hadith reports do not carry the badge: their text is the source's own. The build fails if either phrase is printed again.
- **Every hall has one shape.** A hall opens with what its wing promises (in Living: practices, festivals, food, dress and music; in Made: bookshops, publishers, apps, brands and charities), then the wing's cornerstones, then the full index by first letter, or by century in the Time wing, with a find-by-name box and the count of entries beside it.
- **A record is listed once in the Four Madhhabs Browser.** 168 records filled 331 places because a record stood in every section it touched. Each now stands in its first section and names the others it belongs to.
- **Each browser opens with its own records, then the passages.** Paradise opened with 201 passages before its 22 records, Resurrection with 507 before 36. In twenty-one browsers the museum's records about the subject now come first and the passages that mention it follow.
- **One name for each explorer.** The Explore menu said "Asma ul Husna Browser" where the page said "The Most Beautiful Names Browser", "Quran explorer" where the page said "The Mushaf", and so on for eight entries in English, seven in Arabic and six in Urdu. Each menu label is now the page's own title. The two timelines are told apart in the menu ("The whole axis: every dated entry" and "Guided walks: one person's, era's or city's story") and each page points to the other in one sentence. The Arabic title of the Ghayb Browser is «متصفح عالم الغيب», matching its own introduction.
- **The Explore menu is grouped**: texts, people, places and time, the unseen, worship and conduct, tools. No destination was removed or renamed away; the build fails if one is left out of a group.
- **"In the making" is no longer printed on finished browsers.** The Jobs, Khulafa, Battles, Inventions and Modern browsers carry their own name as an eyebrow, like their siblings.
- **The Jobs Browser says what it holds.** Its introduction promised "each job with the people who held it"; many jobs have no one recorded. It now says so, counts the jobs with no person recorded, and each such job says it in the list.
- **The Modern Islam Browser's headline reconciles on its page**: the section counts, their sum, and why the sum exceeds the number of distinct records.
- **Searching says it is searching.** The search page shows "Searching…" from the first keystroke until an answer arrives.
- The Place hall's index is headed as the index of the places on the map, which is what it lists.
- **The judgement calls behind the browsers' new views are on the decision ledger.** Five records (dec-20261113-272 to 276) state what was chosen and why: the Prophets' Tree draws only lineage the graph holds; a record a view cannot place is counted, not placed; no map of letters is drawn until the records carry both places; only an order a record states is numbered on the Ghayb ascent; and a practice's worship family is a tag on its record. Each names the engine's own answer and why it was overridden.
- **A measured count of harvested books.** `docs/reports/harvest-count-2026-11-14.md` counts the 299 canon books and the 1,754 book-like works by whether they are harvested as text and how many graph records cite them: 227 of the 299 canon books are harvested, 1,404 of 1,754 works are cited by nothing, and only four books are stated to be complete (the Qur'an, Jami' al-Ulum wal-Hikam, Tarikh al-Khulafa, one scan of al-Kamil). A second pass read the OCR output on the founder's drive: 285 of the 299 canon books are there (the ledger lists 227), and about 8% of their OCR'd pages are touched by a graph record, a lower bound. No record or page changed.

### Fixed
- **The 3D tour's Eid al-Fitr and Iftar stops list their records' sources again.** Each record gained a source (al-Nawawi's al-Adhkar) and the tour's own lists were not updated, which failed the tour's test on `main`. The lists now match the records.
- **Ten lesson cards in the Education Explorer now say only what their records say.** In Grade 6 Science: Ibn Firnas's landing is told in the two accounts the sources give, not one; a saying put in Ibn al-Haytham's mouth is replaced by one of his repeatable tests; an unsourced length of the year is replaced by al-Battani's years of observation at al-Raqqa; "the model Copernicus borrowed" becomes what Ibn al-Shatir did for the Moon's model, with the two scholars who differ on whether it reached Copernicus; the cards on Maragha, al-Jahiz, his Book of Animals and Ibn al-Baytar are rewritten from their records; the astrolabe card links a real record; and a card that paraphrased a verse of the Qur'an now only invites the student to read the verse shown on the page. In Grade 3 Science, the Dome of the Rock card drops a description its record does not hold. Arabic, English and Urdu.
- **Urdu caught up with yesterday's corrections.** Ten records' Urdu now matches the corrected Arabic, including the epidemic and plague summaries, which no longer speak in the museum's voice in any language.
- **Thirteen records corrected where the English had drifted from its Arabic, and two that spoke in the museum's own voice.** Found while deepening the lessons of the Education Explorer. Among them: Ibn al-Nafis made fair copies of eighty volumes of his great medical book (the English said he left them unfinished); in the Damascus coffee ban it was the coffee-house in Mecca that was torn down, not a scholar's home; the oud's pegs, not its frets, were likened to fingers; the Banu Musa paid translators, not copyists; and the rate on machine-watered crops is half of the tenth. The records on epidemic and plague no longer describe a hadith in the museum's voice ("a divinely-wise quarantine"): they now say what al-Bukhari and Muslim report. A cross-reference from the record on the divine decree to an unrelated record is removed. The Urdu versions are unchanged for now.
- **Run-together words repaired in 81 invention records and eight biographies.** English text such as "in416 AH", "astronomy,surveying" and "81.3by33.7centimetres" now reads with its spaces; eleven Arabic invention records gained the missing space after a comma. Citations and links are untouched. The faults that could not be fixed without the printed source, the founder or an Urdu edit are listed in `docs/courses/depth-rollout.md`.
- **The Hadith Library no longer holds chapters of other books.** A page under `/{lang}/words/hadith/<work>/<chapter>/` was built for every chapter record in the museum, and only 107 of the 2,218 belong to hadith collections. The other 2,111 are chapter digests of 203 other books (commentaries, histories, law), and each had a breadcrumb to a collection page that does not exist. Those pages are no longer built; every one of those chapters keeps its own record page, and nothing else on the site linked to them. The chapters of the hadith collections are unchanged.
- **The parents' weekly sheet opens the Objects hall.** One activity's "Open" link pointed to `/{lang}/object/`, a page that does not exist; it now opens `/{lang}/objects/`.
- **Two more people filed twice are one record each.** The two pairs left undecided were settled from the sources: Umayr ibn Wahb al-Jumahi of the Tabuk report and of the reinforcement sent to Egypt is one Companion in the biographical compilations, and the repentant highwayman filed as "al-Harith ibn Badr" is Haritha ibn Badr al-Ghudani, the name al-Tabari's commentary on 5:34 uses. Everything both records held is kept, and the old addresses still open the page. The merge tool now carries every field the removed record alone held, not only sources, relations and names.
- **The Khutab timeline no longer starts at a year 0.** The axis under the minbar timeline on `/{lang}/khutab/` began with a tick labelled "0 AH"; the Hijri calendar has no year 0, and the build's own check stopped every pull request on it. The first tick is now labelled year 1. Nothing else on the page moves.
- **The language switch on a letter page no longer leads to a missing page.** The full indexes of the halls and the class listings are cut by first letter (`/{lang}/people/all/<letter>/`, `/{lang}/browse/<class>/all/<letter>/`), and the letters are those of each language's own alphabet. From an Arabic letter page, the EN link in the header (and the page's `hreflang` alternates) pointed to the same letter in English, a page that does not exist; the same happened between Arabic and Urdu for a letter only one of them has, and where a letter runs to fewer pages in the other language. The switch now keeps the twin page where one is built (a shared letter, "other", a century of the Time wing) and otherwise opens the same listing's front page in the other language. This removes the 2,054 broken internal links that the first sampled link check found (run 43443214491), so pull requests can pass that step. Only the letter pages change; no layout file is touched.
- **The sample card on the home page is announced with the words it shows.** The card that shows one real discovery from a lesson, in the home page's section on courses, carried a hidden label ("See a lesson" and the lesson's name) that replaced everything written on the card. A person using voice control who spoke the card's title could not open it, and a screen reader read something other than what was on screen. The hidden label is removed, so the link's name is the card's own text, in Arabic, English and Urdu. This was the one serious finding that made the accessibility step fail on every pull request since 13 November.
- **Two clauses on the Kiswa page tightened to what their sources say.** A second check of the new sentences against the two pages found that the workshop was given its present name in 2017, not at its opening in 1977, and that the Arab News report of July 2022 announces the move of the yearly replacement to the eve of 1 Muharram without saying it has been kept since. Both sentences now say exactly that, in Arabic, English and Urdu.
- **Fifty-one people filed twice are one record each.** Of the 77 candidate pairs the audit left for a decision, the founder approved merging those that are the same person; reading both records of every pair showed 51 are (Abdülmecid II, Dawud al-Zahiri, Abu Ya'la al-Farra', Washmakir, Abu Thawr and others), 24 are different people who share a name, and 2 cannot be told from the records. The richer record of each pair keeps everything: the other's sources, relations, names and prose are carried over word for word, every link to the old id is repointed, and the old address still opens the page. No fact was written by the merge.
- **The Kiswa page no longer says more than its sources.** One sentence said the covering "is made today at the Kiswa Factory in Umm al-Jud by two hundred craftsmen" and cited Wikidata, which carries none of that. It now gives what two read pages say: the workshop's years and places (Ajyad 1927, Jarwal 1962, Umm al-Jud ordered 1972 and opened 1977) from Saudipedia, and from Arab News the materials of the 1444 cover and the move of the yearly replacement from 9 Dhu al-Hijja to the eve of 1 Muharram in 2022. Arabic, English and Urdu; two source records added; the text is AI-written and awaits a human read, and the record's review state is unchanged.
- **The Ten promised Paradise are ten.** The Companions Browser listed nine; Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas was missing because the section copied a trail that left him out. The section now reads the ten names the doctrine's own record lists from al-Tahawi's creed, and the build fails if the section and that list ever disagree.
- **A merged record's old address leads to the record again.** When two records were merged, links written with the old id were dropped from the graph without any warning, and a link to it inside a text became plain words. The build now resolves a former id to the surviving record: 80 links inside texts are links again, and the relations that named a former id are back in the graph (42 more edges on this tree, counting both directions).
- **Search shows the record you mean first.** On the live site "Muhammad" put a tughra above the Prophet's page, "Ibn Sina" an event above the person, and only 2 of the museum's 50 test queries returned their record first. When a query names one of the 918 canon records (by its name, a known spelling, or the words its name opens with), that record is now the first result, marked "Museum cornerstone", and the search engine's own results follow unchanged. The 50 queries are the frozen set in `scripts/fable/search-queries.json`; all 50 pass in the build's own test, among them Muhammad, Saladin, Baghdad, Quran and Kaaba. Which records are canon is not changed. New file: `/api/v1/meta/search-canon.<lang>.json`.
- **Counts are counted from what the page lists.** The Miracles Browser said 1,035 and listed 1,064; Messengers said 1,521 and listed 1,546: the subject cards on the page were left out of the number. Every browser's headline is now the count of distinct records its own sections render, and the build fails when a record is counted that no section lists.
- **The numbers the museum prints about itself are computed, not typed.** The Developers page said "52,576 records" beside a homepage that said 58,128 and described the graph files as 49,570 and 38,862 lines when they held 59,999 and 73,856; Backstage gave 17,314 commits and 4,388 pull requests, frozen weeks earlier; the homepage, Backstage and Support gave three page counts (116,000, 179,997, 99,000). All of these now come from one place at build time. "Pages" has one meaning, said on the homepage where it first appears: a record page is one entry in one language, so the count is the entries (stubs included) times three languages.
- **The API has a front door.** `/api/v1/` answered "not found" although the Developers page gave it as the base address. `/api/v1/index.json` now lists what the API holds, written from the files the build produced; the page says the base address is a prefix and names the index. `/api/v1/chains.json` (every succession relation of the graph, 307 today, and the 123 runs they form) and `/api/v1/openapi.json` exist. No API file carries an editor's `needs_source` marker any more (595 did); the build fails if one would.
- **Wing counts say what they count.** `counts.json` gave "words: 13,538", which is the number of passages, while the Words hall lists 1,056 entries. The file now carries both populations under their own names (`wings`: records of the wing's own class, what the menu's "{n} passages" counts; `halls`: records tagged with the wing, what the hall lists) with a sentence defining each, and the Coverage table says in words that it counts tagged entries, drafts included.
- **An English page no longer shows an Arabic-script name in the middle of an English list** when a record has no English label: it shows a Latin name the record carries, or the name spelled by the record's id. 786 records lack an English label, 246 of them published people; they are listed in `/api/v1/meta/label-gaps.json`.
- **Events with the same title are told apart by their year.** Four records were titled "Battle of Marash" (694, 953, 1164, 1920); 73 English and 33 Arabic event titles were shared by more than one record. A shared title now carries the year in brackets.
- **An event that starts and ends on the same date shows one date**, not "694 CE – 694 CE" with a stray dagger.
- **A record connected to nothing is not passed off as an ordinary feed entry.** Its row is marked `unconnected` and the feed lists such records under that name.
- **The prophet cards read cleanly.** The cards on the Messengers Browser's home printed the pipeline's citation markers (`{cite:sahih-al-bukhari 3326}`) inside their summaries. The markers are no longer printed; the citations stay where they belong, in the footnotes of each prophet's page.
- **Dawud's ayahs are found.** The Messengers Browser looked for «داود» with one waw; the Qur'an text writes «داوود» with two, so his Qur'an mentions were missed. Both spellings are now read, and the collector Abu Dawud is still left out in either spelling. The tree's own build check caught it: it refused to hang Dawud on the ayah that names him until the detector could see the name there.
- **The Abbasid caliphs are in order.** The Caliphs Browser sorted reign years as text, so a reign beginning in 750 came after one beginning in 1031 and the Abbasid chain was shuffled. Reign years are now sorted as numbers.
- **Browser cards read cleanly everywhere.** The cards on twenty-five browser landings printed citation markers such as `{cite:tanzil-quran}` inside their summaries, as the Messengers Browser's did. They are no longer printed on any landing; the subject pages, which turn the markers into footnotes, are unchanged.
- **The Ghayb Browser shows its Night Journey and its ten signs.** Both sections were written but never appeared, because they waited for two labels filed under another browser's name. They now show on the browser's home.
- **The Hisab page no longer scrolls sideways on phones.** A hidden label of the calculator stretched the page beyond the screen.
- **The build passes again: Jibril and Mika'il may stand among the beings.** Since 13 November the Jinn & Devils Browser lists the two angels, typed `being: angel` in their person records, in its "beings" group, while the build check written the same day failed on any person-class record there. Every build on `main` that reached the site check (about an hour in) failed on those three pages (`ar`, `en`, `ur`). The check now allows a person-class record in that group only when its data types it as a being, so a human with no such type there still fails the build. No record, page or rule about who counts as a being changed.

On 550 of them the record's own text gives a year the new date contradicts: Abaza Muhammad Pasha fought in 1769 and was dated 1576–1634; Abbas ibn Muhammad died in 271 AH and was dated 738–802. Those dates are removed from 544 records (six were kept after a hand read) and no date is put in their place; Abbas ibn Muhammad's year, era and region now follow his own summary. Every removed value is kept in `docs/audit/data/s8-removed-dates.json`. The other 5,285 dates of that pass stay; 3,790 of them sit on records whose text gives no year to test them against.
- **Seven cornerstone records are no longer dead ends.** Fourteen cornerstones had one link or none, so a visitor who reached them could go nowhere. Ten relations are added, each from a cited sentence already in the record's own text: Cairo as the Ayyubid capital and Saladin as its ruler (al-Maqrizi), Timur as founder of the Timurid house, the Seljuks at Dandanqan, the sound and the good hadith as kinds of hadith, al-Biruni and al-Khalili on the qibla, al-Baqillani on the sharia, Eid al-Adha at Mina (Encyclopaedia of Islam). Seven remain: five period records (the era a record belongs to is a field, not a relation), the Ardabil carpet (its record has nothing to link from) and Eid al-Fitr. The share of published records within three links of a cornerstone is unchanged at 38.3%; the target of 60% was not met and no edge was added to reach it.
- **Two father-and-mother edges the Qur'an states.** Yahya is recorded as the son of Zakariyya and Isa as the son of Maryam, each citing the Qur'an record, so the Prophets' Tree can draw the first as a branch and name the second on Isa's card.

- **143 lessons deepened across all Science and Social Studies courses of the Education Explorer.** Every Science and Technology course (Grades 1 to 8 and the eleven secondary courses from SNC1W to SPH4U) and every Social Studies and Geography course (Grades 1 to 4 and 6, Geography 7 and 8): 26 courses, 147 lessons, of which 143 now carry the depth layer in Arabic and English, about 87,000 words in 1,294 sections, each claim traced to its record in `docs/courses/evidence/`. Four Grade 6 Science lessons (static electricity, circuits, saving energy, the costs of flight) have none, because no record honestly serves them. Grade bands are kept apart: Grades 1 to 5 get one concrete scene and one question; Grades 6 to 8 meet sources, motives and disagreements; Grades 9 to 12 get source criticism and a counter-argument to answer. Everything stays a draft until a person reads it. The Urdu lesson pages are unchanged and do not yet show the layer. The order proposed for the remaining 39 courses, the lessons left out, and the record faults found on the way are in `docs/courses/depth-rollout.md`.
- **Seventeen senior social-science lessons deepened in the Education Explorer.** The depth layer now reaches Equity and Social Justice (HSE4M), Challenge and Change in Society (HSB4U), World Cultures (HSC4M) and Introduction to Anthropology, Psychology and Sociology (HSP3U): 17 lessons, Arabic and English, in the Grades 9 to 12 band. Here justice is treated as a concept to reason with: the ideal as a named source states it, the institution that carried it, where practice fell short, and what the sources cannot tell us, with a question that asks the student to take a position and answer the strongest objection. Rulings are reported as the jurists' or the issuing body's, never in the museum's voice. Still drafts; Urdu pages unchanged. 160 of the Explorer's 360 lessons now carry the layer (`docs/courses/depth-rollout.md`).
- **The two Philosophy courses of the Education Explorer go deeper.** Philosophy: The Big Questions (HZB3M) and Philosophy: Questions and Theories (HZT4U), 11 lessons, Arabic and English. Each lesson now lets a student rebuild one argument from the museum's records: what a thinker claimed, the reasons the record reports, and a named critic's objection, among them Ibn Rushd's case for philosophy beside Ibn Khaldun's refutation, two Sunni formulations of human action under the decree, and Ibn al-Haytham on what the eye senses and what the mind infers. Every position is given as its holder's, with no verdict. Still drafts; Urdu pages unchanged. 171 of the Explorer's 360 lessons now carry the depth layer.
- **The practice records say which act of worship they belong to.** Forty-one practice records (wudu, tayammum, the Friday prayer, tarawih, zakat al-fitr, tawaf, tajwid and the rest) now carry their worship family as a tag on the record itself. The rosette on the Worship and Adhkar Browser reads the grouping from the records; the table that held it inside the page's code is gone. One practice, the vow, moves from the supplication petal to the row beneath the rosette, because its record names no family.

- **The two World Religions courses of the Education Explorer go deeper, under a new rule of description.** World Religions and Belief Traditions (HRT3M) and World Religions in Daily Life (HRF3O), 22 lessons, Arabic and English. The founder approved a fourth lens for the depth rubric (section 2.4): a belief or practice is described as its adherents hold it, on the word of a named source, with the Sunni position first, then the academic view, then any other view, and no verdict. The page teaches about a religion and never teaches it: no sentence instructs or judges, the Qur'an is linked and never explained, and each lesson says what kind of source it is reading (a creed text, a jurists' encyclopaedia, a hadith collection, an academic encyclopaedia) and where the museum's own record is still incomplete. Still drafts; Urdu pages unchanged. 193 of the Explorer's 360 lessons now carry the depth layer.
- **Every Mathematics lesson of the Education Explorer goes deeper.** Grades 1 to 8 and Grade 9 (MTH1W): 53 lessons, Arabic and English. The question a teacher asked of the science lessons, why did they do it, is answered here from the mathematicians' own prefaces where the museum's records preserve them: al-Khwarizmi wrote his algebra for what people need in inheritance, trade, land measurement and digging canals; al-Uqlidisi and al-Kindi say what their books are for; and where the records preserve no motive the lesson says so. Older grades also meet the corrections the records carry (decimal fractions before al-Kashi, a rule about debts that is not yet negative numbers, a triangle of numbers older than its usual name) and how a lost Arabic book is known from a Latin copy. Money lessons report the jurists' rules on saving, debt and interest as theirs and give no advice. The lessons teach no mathematics the records do not state. Still drafts; Urdu pages unchanged. 246 of the Explorer's 360 lessons now carry the depth layer.
- **Classical Civilization (LVV4U) goes deeper in the Education Explorer.** Seven lessons, Arabic and English. Each now asks how we know what we say about the Greek and Roman world when it reaches us through Arabic hands: what Ibn al-Nadim's catalogue reports of Socrates, Plato, Aristotle, Euclid and Archimedes, which books it says were translated and by whom, where two records name a translator differently, how al-Biruni and the astronomers count the era of Alexander, and where a lesson rests on one author alone. Still drafts; Urdu pages unchanged. 253 of the Explorer's 360 lessons now carry the depth layer.
- **Every Arts, Visual Arts and Music lesson of the Education Explorer goes deeper, under a rule against reading meanings into forms.** The Arts for Grades 1 to 8, six Visual Arts courses (AVI1O to AVI4M) and two Music courses (AMU3M, AMU4M): 73 lessons, Arabic and English. The founder approved a fifth lens for the depth rubric (section 2.5): a work is described through who made it, who paid for it, what it was for, how it was made and what its inscription says, on the word of a named source. The museum never says what a pattern or a dome "means": where scholars read a meaning, the lesson names them, and where they disagree it gives both (does ornament carry symbols at all; why was the Dome of the Rock built). For music, the jurists' disagreement appears only as named views beside the documented practice, and a lesson never says music is permitted or forbidden. Young grades get a hand, a tool, a material; senior grades ask how a signed piece differs from a late report. Still drafts; Urdu pages unchanged. 326 of the Explorer's 360 lessons now carry the depth layer.
- **The depth layer now covers the whole Education Explorer: 356 of its 360 lessons.** The last thirty are Nutrition and Health (HFA4U), The World of Fashion (HNB4M) and International Languages, Levels 1 to 3, in Arabic and English. The food and health lessons were written under the strictest rule of the programme: nothing reads as dietary, medical or religious advice. Each says who ruled what, by name and school, and that such texts show what was ruled or reported, not what a food or a fast does in a body. With this, every course a student can open carries the layer the reviewing educator asked for; the four lessons without it are Grade 6 Science lessons for which the museum holds no honest record. All of it stays a draft until a person reads it, and the Urdu pages are unchanged. What remains (the human reading, Urdu, the Grade 6 pilot, and the record faults found on the way) is listed in `docs/courses/depth-rollout.md`.
- **Grade 6 Science and Technology in the Education Explorer is rebuilt from the Ministry's own text.** It was the hand-made pilot of the courses surface and followed an older curriculum: its expectations were not Ontario's wording, its Arabic and Urdu expectation texts were copies of the English, and half its cards linked no museum record. Every expectation is now the Ministry's 2022 wording with a real Arabic and Urdu translation; electricity sits in strand C and flight in strand D, where the curriculum puts them; a strand A lesson on who has contributed to science and technology is added; and each of the 21 cards restates a museum record with that record's sources. Every lesson address still works. Eight lessons for which the museum holds no honest record (the four on electricity, three on biodiversity, one on aviation's impacts) are kept and say so plainly, with no cards. Fourteen expectations are listed in the course's gap register with the searches that found nothing. Still a draft.
### Tests
- **Connectedness is measured over the records it can apply to.** The target of 60% of all published records within three steps of a cornerstone could never be met, because nearly half of the published records are sources, which other records cite but are not related to. By the founder's decision the museum now reports the share of published subject records within three steps (72.6% today), beside the number of sources nothing cites (107) and of subject records with no relation at all (1,654). The older measure and its baseline are kept unchanged for comparison. `scripts/audit/subject-reach.py` prints all three.
- **The Companions roll has a page-weight limit.** `/{lang}/companions/all/`, the A-to-Z roll moved off the Companions home, is now checked at every build against 350 KB. It weighs 291 KB today for 604 Companions, so the limit leaves room for about 180 more; past that, the roll is to be cut into letter pages, as the halls are.
- **A test for the letter pages' language links.** `scripts/paged-alternates.test.ts` checks that a letter page names its twin in another language only when that letter and page number exist there, and the listing's front page otherwise.
- **A pull request gets its answer in minutes.** Its check run built all 202,000 pages (54 to 89 minutes, and three hours before that), so the result arrived after the merge and faults reached the live branch. It now validates the content first (about two minutes) and builds a sample: every listing, browser and landing page, the records the pull request changed in the three languages, and a spread of each class, with the same page checks, link check, accessibility audit and Lighthouse budget run on it. The full build after the merge still renders and checks every page, and a new check there follows every link of the whole site.
- **A corrupted letter is caught before any build.** Validation now fails on the replacement character (U+FFFD) anywhere in a data, prose, interface-string, education or tour file. The old check skipped a passage's text, which is where the letter that stopped the build of 12 November was.
- `scripts/tafsir.test.ts` checks, over every verse and language, that lifting the commentary out of the prose loses no text and leaves no tafsir citation behind; `scripts/check-site.ts` checks the verse-first landing, the Tafsir section on 2:255, the fallback on a verse without commentary, and `/quran/`.
- Validation now reports a person whose summary states a death year that the structured date contradicts by more than two years (ten for an approximate date); 19 records are reported today. New tests cover that check, the Ten, and the rendered pages of this part.
- `scripts/audit/e2e-graph.mjs` drives the Graph Explorer in a real browser (name search, star click, the centre button, the trail, the filter badge, the error at the box): 11 checks, all passing on this build. `scripts/audit/s34-names.ts` compares every menu label with its page's heading and title.
- **The Prophets' Tree is checked against the data.** A new test file asserts that every solid branch is a `child_of` edge, every tie an edge, every browser subject is drawn once, the vine splits as the Genealogies chain does, no two leaves overlap in any of the three languages, and the detector reads both spellings of Dawud.

### Performance
- **Builds of the live branch no longer queue for hours.** Every merge queued a full build, so after many merges the newest one was built hours later and hundreds were cancelled by hand. One build runs and only the newest merge waits; a build the founder starts by hand still always runs to its end.
- **No listing page ships its whole corpus any more.** The browsers and halls rendered every record into one page and filtered it in the browser. Each is now a landing that shows the first rows of every section, with the full list on linked sub-pages, every one a real address that works without JavaScript; the filter box searches the whole list through a small index fetched on the first keystroke. Arabic pages, HTML before images: Worship 4,985 KB → 326 KB; People 4,021 → 116; Mukatabat 3,615 → 274; Signs 3,527 → 276; Akhlaq 3,504 → 349; Messengers 2,241 → 266; Objects 2,202 → 366; Time 2,046 → 159; Ansab 1,744 → 303; Hisab 1,547 → 337; Islamic Economy 1,512 → 302; Miracles 1,268 → 305; the person listing 1,974 → 105; Wander 8,281 → 98. The battle listing was 1,483 cards on one page and is 200 a page. No sub-page exceeds 500 KB, and the weight check enforces that ceiling on 25 routes. Still over 500 KB and not changed here: the changelog, three theme pages, the art gallery, two Modern Islam listings, two subject pages (Muhammad in Ansab and in Messengers), the poetry and timeline-events listings, the Fatwa Explorer, the Place hall and the references page.

## v1.28.0 — 2026-11-12
### Added
- **The engineering record of the Fable 5.2 run and the build and deploy speed work is written down.** A new engineering document (`docs/engineering/45-fable-5-2-improvements.md`) gathers in one place, with the source of every number, what the Fable 5.2 run changed in the museum — the Grand Tour, the canon repairs, the contradiction sweep, and the two statements its own ledger marks NOT GREEN — the independent production tests taken before and after it, and the measured speed work that was tried on UAT and brought to `main` on 13 November (page rendering 3 h 6 min to 43 min, a build run of about 3 h 34 min to 1 h 22 min, a deploy of 3 h 13 min to 47 min). Documentation only; the site itself is unchanged, and the speed changes go live at the founder's next deploy, as the entry above records.
- **GitHub now greets contributors with templates.** The repository gains markdown issue templates for a bug report, a content correction (record, the wrong fact, the right fact, and the citable source this museum runs on) and a feature request, alongside its existing forms; a pull-request template that carries the museum's own gates as checkboxes — validate finishing at 0 errors and cite-check at 0 fail, the canary entry in the same commit, Arabic–English parity with the Urdu edition left to the founder's lane, and no layout breakage on any screen; and an issue configuration that allows blank issues and points newcomers at the standing help-wanted call for prose and harvesting help (issue #6513). Developer-funnel plumbing only; the site itself is unchanged.

### Performance
- **The build takes about an hour and twenty minutes instead of three and a half hours, and a full deploy about forty-seven minutes instead of three hours and a quarter.** Tried on UAT first (build run 43300358009, deploy run 43334841849, 13 November) against the production build and deploy of the same content the day before. Four changes. (1) Each entity page looked up its connections by scanning every edge of the graph about eight times and re-read the whole list of related entities from disk; both are now prepared once per build. Rendering the 202,253 pages fell from 3 h 6 min to 43 min, and 400 pages sampled across the sitemap are byte for byte the same on UAT and production. (2) The publisher uploaded its archives with a call that blocked everything else, so they went up one at a time whatever the parallel setting said; it no longer blocks. A full publish went from 99 minutes for 307,693 operations with 678 retries to 42 minutes for 441,087 operations with 13. (3) The sync Workers no longer write one shared progress file that up to 42 of them wrote at once, against R2's limit of one write a second to a key. (4) The build is stored as one compressed file of 1.15 GB instead of 456,000 separate files (the upload took 24 minutes, now under three), and the deploy copies only the 95 files the Worker serves itself instead of the whole build (six minutes, now sixteen seconds). Builds made before this change stay deployable: the deploy accepts both forms.

### Fixed
- **The unit tests pass on `main` again, so builds are no longer cancelled.** Three stops of the 3D tour (Ibn Sina, al-Khwarizmi, Ibn Khaldun) list the sources of their records, and the records gained the Biblissima source on 12 November without the tour file being updated; the test that keeps the two in step failed, and a failed test cancels the build. The three lists now match their records.
- **`/ar`, `/en` and `/ur` without the final slash open the language's home page.** They answered "page not found" on production and UAT: the Worker was written to redirect them, but the routing list only sent addresses below `/ar/` to it.

### Changed
- **The workflows use the current versions of the GitHub and Cloudflare actions** (checkout, setup-node and upload-artifact v7, download-artifact v8, wrangler-action v4). GitHub had begun warning that the old ones target a retired Node version. Not yet exercised by a deploy: the first build and UAT deploy after this change are the test.

### Docs
- **The build and deploy review is written up in the engineering documentation** (`docs/engineering/45-build-deploy-review.md`): the timings before and after, each change and the evidence for it, how it was checked on UAT, the Cloudflare and GitHub limits the plan was read against (with sources and the date), and the open items that were found and not changed. The deployment and performance documents now describe the pipeline as it runs today, and no longer name a GitHub Pages fallback mirror, which was not being published and could not hold the site.
- **The fallback for a Cloudflare outage is decided and written down (founder, 13 November 2026).** There is no live copy of the site outside Cloudflare, and that risk is accepted: everything is in the public repository and the site can be rebuilt from it in about an hour and a half. `docs/engineering/06-deployment.md` section 5a records the decision, the three options (accept the risk, a reduced mirror on GitHub Pages, a full copy with a second provider) with what each gives and costs, and the events that should reopen the question. The UNESCO dossier and the DPGA evidence map, which named the mirror, are corrected in the same change (a submission-impacting change, signed off by the founder).

### Changed
- **Page-weight budgets raised for three education routes (founder's decision, 12 November 2026).** The 12 November build (run 43257201121) passed every earlier step and failed at the page-weight check: `/ar/event/hijra/` measured 169.2 KB against 160 KB, and `/ar/learn/daily/` and `/ar/shabab/daily/` measured 120.7 KB against 120 KB. The Hijra page grew when its prose gained the Encyclopaedia of Islam sections; the two daily-challenge pages are unchanged and grew with the shared layout, the same cause as the classroom quiz budget the founder raised to 150 KB the same day. `scripts/check-weight.ts` now allows 200 KB for the leveled-reading page and 150 KB for the daily challenge. The alternative is to remove weight: cut prose from the Hijra page or slim the shared menu on every page.

### Added
- **al-Thurayya Gazetteer registered as a citable source (Tier 2).** The museum can now cite the Leipzig-run gazetteer of more than two thousand places of the Islamic world in the ninth and tenth centuries, with Arabic names, regions and types, as `{cite:althurayya-gazetteer <file name>}`. The project publishes its original data under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; material it took from other works is left out of that grant, so the museum takes only place identity, name, region and type, and treats coordinates as approximate. The place's file name in the project's public repository is the anchor, recorded with the Arabic name and the date read. This is the last of four pilot sources approved on 12 November 2026.
- **Louvre object records registered as a citable source (Tier 2).** The museum can now cite the Musée du Louvre's collections website, including the Islamic Arts department, for an object's inventory number, date, material, inscriptions, provenance and bibliography, as `{cite:louvre-collections <ARK id>}`. The museum's Terms of Use put the text of the records under the French Etalab Open Licence, which requires crediting the Louvre and the date of the last update. Photographs are not open and are never fetched; the site's export route, which its robots.txt forbids, is never used. This is the third of four pilot sources approved on 12 November 2026.
- **vHMML manuscript metadata registered as a citable source (Tier 2).** The museum can now cite the Hill Museum & Manuscript Library's Reading Room and Data Portal for a manuscript's shelfmark, repository, language, script, colophon information, provenance and date, as `{cite:vhmml <HMML project number>}`. The library publishes this metadata under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0. Its images are not open and the museum fetches none. No dataset was downloaded; that needs the founder's separate permission. This is a separate entry from the existing HMML catalogue source, and the second of four pilot sources approved on 12 November 2026.
- **Biblissima authority records registered as a citable source (Tier 2, facts-only).** The museum can now cite Biblissima's open authority database of persons, works and institutions of the manuscript world, including Arab and Islamic authors with Arabic-script names and life dates, as `{cite:biblissima Q499}`. Its data is published under the French Open Licence 2.0 (Etalab), which allows reuse with attribution. It is read only through the project's public JSON interface, one record at a time; the SPARQL service needs a login and is not used. Facts are restated in the museum's own words. This is the first of four pilot sources the founder approved on 12 November 2026; the ten-person pilot itself follows.
- **A new courses experience: the Education Explorer (`/{lang}/learn/courses/`).** The courses page is rebuilt in Arabic, English and Urdu as three steps: a finder (school system, grade, course), a course map that shows every lesson and where you stopped, and a lesson page built as a small loop — the goal, something to see before, the lesson with the museum's connections woven into it, something to follow after, and a short self-check. Each lesson shows the official expectations it serves with the authority's own codes; a classroom view and a print layout are included; every page reads without JavaScript, and progress is kept only in the reader's own browser. Design record: `docs/courses-mission/DESIGN.md`.
- **The homepage presents it.** A section on the homepage in all three languages says what the Education Explorer is and whom it serves, and it joins the homepage's list of explorers. The header menu is not changed: that would rewrite every page of the site, and is left to the founder's weekly batch.
- **A repeatable way to bring a curriculum in.** `docs/courses-mission/PIPELINE.md` is the runbook: the official source only, the authority's wording quoted within the 40-word limit, a link to the museum only where an honest one exists, everything else written to a gap register with the searches that were tried, and a gate (`scripts/courses/check_course.py`) that must print GREEN. A fresh agent proved it on Ontario Grade 4 Social Studies using the runbook alone.
- **Missing-record batch 5: eighteen new records in English, Arabic and Urdu.** Napoleon Bonaparte, Ibrahim Bey, Muhammad Abu al-Dhahab, Umar Makram and Mariette Pasha (Egypt around 1798 and after); Said Pasha, Ferdinand de Lesseps, the Suez Canal Company, Port Said and Hasan al-Banna; the Latin translators Petrus Alfonsi, John of Seville, Hermann of Carinthia and Savasorda (Robert of Chester already existed as Robert of Ketton and gained a name variant); and Dimitrie Cantemir, Edward Codrington, Tudor Vladimirescu and Gregory Palamas. Drafted from the Encyclopaedia of Islam (2nd ed.) with conflicting dates recorded side by side. Four Mamluk emir records (Baybugha Urus, Manjak, Taybugha, Minkali) were started but not finished and are not included. Draft translations by Claude Sonnet 5.5.

- **A public evidence package for the Fable 5.2 build (`docs/verification/`).** The independent production tests taken before the run (10 November, v1.10.0) and after deployment (12 November, this version) are published in the repository alongside the mission prompt and the run's own records, with an index that states the result defect by defect — seven of nine baseline defects fixed, one partial, one not fixed — so any reader can check the museum's claims about the build against the same evidence the founder used.

### Changed
- **Five candidate families assessed, none registered.** Al-Thurayya Gazetteer (open project data, pilot proposed), EpiHub's Historic Cairo inscriptions (no terms page, deferred), vHMML (metadata open under CC BY 4.0; images excluded, pilot proposed), Biblissima authority referentials (Etalab 2.0; SPARQL needs a login, so the wiki API is the route, pilot proposed) and the Louvre collections (text notices open under Etalab, photographs excluded, pilot proposed). Each has a score sheet in `docs/delegation/web-sources-progress.md`.

### Data
- **al-Thurayya links added to ten places.** Aleppo, Hama, Homs, Mosul, Qumm, Samarqand, Samarra, Tustar, Wasit and Balkh now point to their record in the al-Thurayya gazetteer of ninth and tenth century places. Each was matched by Arabic name and by position, within 7 km. Only the link and the source were added; no coordinate or description changed. All ten records had an Arabic name that matched ours exactly. The anchor is the place's file name in the project's repository, a choice the founder can overturn.
- **Louvre catalogue facts for three Islamic objects.** The Suaire de Saint-Josse, the Pyxis of al-Mughira and the Baptistere de Saint Louis now carry their Louvre record number, inventory number, measurements and inscription translations, and each page has a short Collection record section in Arabic, English and Urdu citing the Louvre. The Louvre dates the basin to 1325-1340, later than the museum's earlier c.1300; the page says so and the data date is left for review. Only three Louvre objects exist in the graph, so the pilot is three, not ten. No images were fetched.
- **Biblissima identifiers added to ten scholars.** Ibn Sina, al-Farabi, Ibn Rushd, al-Khwarizmi, Thabit ibn Qurra, Ibn al-Haytham, al-Kindi, al-Tabari, Ibn Khaldun and Ibn al-Nafis now carry their Biblissima record number (for example Q2018 for Ibn Sina), each confirmed because Biblissima's Wikidata link matches ours. The records cite the new source; no dates or prose changed. Biblissima's labels are French, so the Arabic share of the fifteen records tested is zero. Small year differences from Biblissima are listed in the progress note for review.

One course (Grade 5 Social Studies) ended with no lesson and is recorded as a gap only. Every lesson was read by a fresh reviewer after it was written and corrected or removed where the link was stretched; the reviews are in `docs/courses-mission/verifier/`.
