## v1.5.1 — 2026-11-09

### Added
- **The Khulafa Browser «متصفح الخلفاء» (plan 30, founder-approved).** The caliphs of Islam are browsable at `/{lang}/khulafa/`: ~160 caliphs as ordinary `person` records, grouped by the caliphate they ruled — Rashidun, Umayyad, Cordoba, Abbasid Baghdad and the ceremonial Cairo line, Fatimid, Almohad, Ottoman and Sokoto — with the Zubayrid, Hammudid and Sharifian counter-caliphates labelled as claims last. Each caliph page at `/{lang}/khulafa/<slug>/` shows his reign, his predecessor/successor strip inside the chain, the events his reign saw (the new `during_reign`/`reign_saw` predicate), and `perspectives` where the accession is contested. Exported at `/api/v1/khulafa.json` and `/api/v1/khulafa/chains.json`; landing card and Explore entry included.
- **The Asma ul Husna Browser «متصفح أسماء الله الحسنى» (plan 29, founder-approved).** The ninety-nine names of God are now records in the graph: 99 `concept` entities of the new kind `divine-name`, ordered on the Tirmidhi enumeration with transliteration, lexical root and `part_of` the umbrella `concept/asma-allah-al-husna`, each citing Jami' al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Qayyim's Jala' al-Afham. The browser at `/{lang}/asma/` shows the numbered grid with a vowel-insensitive filter, and each name's page at `/{lang}/asma/<slug>/` groups its cited stories — Qur'an passages, hadith, seerah events, Companions and the righteous — from `mentions`/`exemplifies` edges (seeded with the Hashr close 59:22–24, ayat al-kursi, the Fatiha and al-Isra 17:110, and Muslim 2677), plus curated trilingual prose as it lands. Exported at `/api/v1/asma.json`; landing card and Explore entry included. Schema gained `divine-name` plus `order`/`name_meta` on concept, and the validator now requires each name's order, enumeration and source.
- **Asma browser phase 4: stories and full edges.** Each name's story sections are now populated: 850 text-verified `mentions` edges (computed against each passage's own normalized text) give every name its real Qur'an and hadith occurrences; `exemplifies` edges carry sahaba/saliheen stories (Bilal, Salman, Rabi'a, Uways); 21 `related_to` pairs join the paired names; and all 99 names gained trilingual prose (brief, «في القرآن», «في السنة», people-stories) at draft tier with provenance.
- **Proposal: the Asma ul Husna Browser (plan 29).** A new plan document proposes «متصفح أسماء الله الحسنى»: the ninety-nine names of God as `concept` records of a new kind `divine-name` under the existing `concept/asma-allah-al-husna` umbrella, ordered on the Tirmidhi list with Ibn Majah differences labelled. Each name would get a page at `/[lang]/asma/<slug>/` grouping its cited stories — Qur'an passages, hadith, seerah events, sahaba and saliheen — through the existing `mentions`/`exemplifies` edges plus curated trilingual prose, with a `/api/v1/asma.json` export. It is a proposal only: no schema, data, site or i18n changes until the founder approves it.
- **Proposal: the Khulafa Browser «متصفح الخلفاء» (plan 30).** A new plan document proposes the caliphs browser: every caliph stays an ordinary `person` record, carrying a cited `story_roles`/`ruled_over` reign toward its caliphate `polity`, grouped as Rashidun, Umayyad, Cordoba, Abbasid Baghdad and Cairo, Fatimid, Almohad, Ottoman and Sokoto — plus labelled rival claims (Zubayrid, Hammudid, Sharifian) and the ceremonial Cairo line. Each caliph page at `/[lang]/khulafa/<slug>/` would show the reign in both calendars, the predecessor/successor chain, the events, buildings and works of the reign through a proposed `during_reign` predicate, the realm map, and `perspectives` where the accession is contested; exports at `/api/v1/khulafa.json` and `/api/v1/khulafa/chains.json`. A roster dataset drives the audit of ~140–160 caliphs; missing person records and reign edges are mined from the filed canon (Suyuti's Tarikh al-Khulafa, Tabari, EI2…) and harvested sources. It is a proposal only: no schema, data, site or i18n changes until the founder approves it.

### Data
- **Khulafa Browser data spine (plan 30).** The roster `datasets/khulafa-roster.csv` maps ~160 caliphs across 8 caliphates plus three labelled claims; every roster row now has `roles: [caliph]`, a cited `story_roles` reign, `ruled_over` and `successor_of` edges (Suyuti's Tarikh al-Khulafa, Ibn Idhari, Sicill-i Osmani, al-Maqrizi). Thirty missing person records were created (Cordoba, Cairo-line, Ottoman and Sokoto caliphs), and four polity records were added: `zubayrid-caliphate`, `hammudid-caliphate`, `abbasid-caliphate-cairo` (the ceremonial Cairo line) and `sharifian-caliphate`.
- **Khulafa Browser schema spine (plan 30).** The `during_reign`/`reign_saw` predicate is registered — events, buildings, works and inventions can now cite whose reign they fall under; the validator requires a person whose `story_roles` reign (or rival claim) points to a `caliphate` polity to carry `roles: [caliph]`, and warns where a `caliph` role still lacks its recorded reign. `person/hasan-ibn-ali` gains the `caliph` role for his six-month reign, the first record the new rule caught.
- **Provenance recorded for the 3D tour's records.** Thirteen records shown in the 3D tour previously failed the publication-standard cite-check on missing provenance. Eight (Junoon, the OIC, three living-culture listings, Fatima al-Fihri, Mimar Sinan, iftar practice and al-Fihrist) now carry a top-level `provenance` block naming the cited sources and the generating run. The five object records (Andalus dirhams, Umar ibn Yusuf's astrolabe, Birmingham mushaf, Iznik bottle, V&A mosque lamp) cannot carry one — the object schema declares `provenance` an array while the base schema declares it an object — so `cite-check` now honours their `status.generated_by` plus cited-sources convention instead. `npm run cite-check` on all 53 tour-referenced records: 0 fail.

### Fixed
- **Unbreak `main`: duplicate YAML keys in 513 place and person records.** Yesterday's geocoding and date-enrichment batches added a new `coordinates` / `coordinate_precision` / `coordinate_note` triple (466 place files) or a second identical `died:` line (47 person files) without removing the old line, and in nine files inserted the triple inside a list, so `npm run graph`, `npm run validate` and the build all stopped with "Map keys must be unique". Each file now keeps the new geocoded triple and drops the superseded "no reliably attested coordinates" note and precision; no coordinate, date or source value was changed.
- **Unbreak `main`: Urdu map-viewer strings mis-keyed under `hadith`.** Yesterday's Urdu map-viewer copy landed as `hadith.viewer.*` instead of `map.viewer.*` — the i18n parity gate failed (37 ur-only keys) and Urdu map chrome rendered raw key paths. Moved the block under `map:`; ar/en/ur key sets are identical again.
- **Unbreak `main`: MapViewer missing quote.** Yesterday's map-viewer merge left an unterminated string in the Arabic edge-label table (`born_in: "وُلد في` had no closing quote), so `npm run build` failed before any page compiled. Restored the quote; the site builds again.
- **3D tour QA fixes (`/{lang}/3d/`).** (1) Enter now crosses the doorway the visitor is facing even while a top-bar or strip button holds focus — jumps also move keyboard focus onto the 3D canvas, so the "press Enter to go through the doorway" prompt finally does what it says right after entry and after strip/map jumps. (2) The Exit button opens an in-page confirm dialog instead of `window.confirm` (which embedded/webview contexts can silently suppress, leaving a dead-looking button); confirming disposes the scene and returns to the museum home, cancelling restores focus to the tour. (3) First visit now shows a real spinner plus a line explaining that the 3D engine downloads once and later visits are fast; the load watchdog was raised from 9 s to 60 s, re-arms once the three.js import resolves, and can no longer declare failure after init succeeded. (4) The Umayyad dirham close-up is no longer a blank grey disc — both faces carry a stylised inscription-band-and-field coin face with a milled rim (still a stand-in model; the honest note stays), and closer-scene texture maps are now disposed on close. (5) Floating exhibit/wing label sprites clamp to at most 60% of the viewport width and shrink as their anchor nears a screen edge, so long Arabic names can no longer run off-screen. (6) The entry-card and page ledes in Arabic and English no longer claim the wing galleries are "on the way" — all nine are open today (the Urdu copy already said so). New i18n keys `tour.loading_first`, `tour.exit_yes`, `tour.exit_stay` ship in ar/en/ur in the same commit.

## v1.5.0 — 2026-11-09

### Fixed
- **Validation repair after the geo-enrichment merge.** `data/place/kufa.yaml` now quotes its `founded.edtf` year ("0638") so the date schema validates again, and the 3D tour's `tour/halls.yaml` Medina stop lists `source/wikidata` (and the Cordoba stop likewise) to match the records' updated source lists.

### Added
- **The Islam Map Viewer.** The Place wing (`/{lang}/place/`) now opens into a full-screen interactive map of the Islamic world: twelve hand-drawn regions on a Natural Earth world outline, collision-free place markers inside each region, city orbit and focus views that draw the real graph edges (people, events, buildings, works, journeys one hop from each place), a Hijri time slider from 74 BH to 1448 AH that dims everything outside its year, free pan and zoom, a parent-level preview button, and a black/ivory-gold theme toggle. All geometry is computed at build time from `world-atlas` topojson and the compiled graph — nothing is fetched at runtime — and readers without JavaScript still get the schematic MiniMap. The landing page and the Explore menu gain a localized "Islam map" card in Arabic, English and Urdu.
- **Wave 199 — the Kurdish scene joins the modern-figures graph.** Four people and two channel brands from Iraqi Kurdistan's Sorani dawah scene, each with dated audience counts: reciter Peshawa Qadir Al-Kurdi (1.67M YouTube subscribers), Sulaymaniyah Friday preacher Muhammad Mala Fayaq Sharazoori (398K), surgeon-professor and preacher Dr Abdulwahid Muhammed Salih (1.7M Facebook followers), Kifri preacher Mamosta Sabah Kifri (280K), and the Bangawaz TV (2.7M) and Tebinni Islam (117K) lecture channels — the brands name no individual operator, and the records say so honestly rather than inventing one.
- **Wave 199 §C — the founder-cleared Kurdish pair.** Abdullatif Ahmad Mustafa, the Sulaymaniyah preacher who founded Amozhgari TV, and the channel itself (1.8M Facebook followers) join the graph, built on the founder's ruling with the full public record carried openly in the entries — including his July 2026 dismissal from his university post after an official investigation, his denial of the allegations, and the fact that no criminal conviction is reported.

Pan is clamped to the zoom so the map can no longer be dragged off-stage; the toolbar is no longer clipped under the sticky header; the year step arrows work in all three languages with direction and icons matching each page's text direction; and all map chrome (breadcrumb, controls, year label, aria-labels) is localized through `map.viewer.*` keys in Arabic, English and Urdu. Early-year region highlighting now only inherits dates through place-dating predicates (born/died/lived/ruled/occurred), so 11 AH no longer lights up the whole map. Detail pages gain Urdu region names via `schema/enums/regions.yaml` and a safe label fallback, and the "In time" strip no longer clips its edge year labels.
- **Islam map requirements doc.** `docs/engineering/19-islam-map-requirements.md` records the map's full requirement set — palette, basemap, camera bounds, time slider, drill-down, orbits, localization, accessibility — with a production test checklist for validation.

Ambiguous identifications carry approximate coordinates with the alternatives recorded in the coordinate note. Mostafa al-Aridi is now placed in Beirut. Only Iram, Wabar and the non-geographic Royal Court remain unlocated.
- **344 missing places geocoded.** Every person-referenced place that lacked coordinates now has them: 307 records updated and 17 dangling place references created as stubs (Unaizah, Alexandria/Iskandariyya, Bijapur, Daulatabad, Pamplona, Tripoli, Gulbarga, etc.), each with coordinate precision and a provenance note. Places without a regions list are now also assigned to their containing map region by geometry, so every linked person appears. ~15 toponyms remain unlocated (legendary or non-geographic records like Iram and Royal Court).
- **Residual person locations resolved.** The final unlocated person records were researched against classical and modern sources: 22 people now carry place edges (born_in, lived_in, died_in, traveled_to, ruler_of) so they appear on the map — including Nicolaus of Damascus, the Emir Sawdan of Bari, Eustathius in Baghdad, and Zaynab bint al-Ghazzi in Damascus. Two new place records (al-Jawa in Qassim, Groningen) were created. Thirteen records stay unlocated with documented reasons (scriptural/legendary figures, faceless modern channels).
- **City orbits show every linked entity.** Drilling into a city used to hide people and events outside the selected year — Mecca showed only a handful. The orbit now lists all entities linked to the place (48 people plus events, buildings, works and journeys for Mecca), ordered by degree with year-active items first.
- **Map panning now reaches every edge of the world.** Pan and zoom are applied to the map content inside the viewbox (a camera transform) instead of the svg element, so on phones — where cover-fit crops the sides — dragging left/right reveals Russia, East Asia, the Americas and every cropped edge; the pan clamp now matches the real rendered size. A Home button in the map toolbar exits back to the site, and region labels shrink on phones to reduce overlap.
- **Touch drags pan the map.** On the full-screen map page, touch gestures pan in both directions instead of scrolling the page behind it, and the stage shows a grab cursor.
- **Map page is now a full-screen browser.** `/{lang}/place/` renders only the map viewer — no site banner above it and no card list below (the place card index remains for no-JS visitors inside `noscript`). The toolbar pins just under the sticky site header when the map is embedded, and the viewer hydrates immediately (`client:load`) so there is no first-load flicker.
- **Every city and every attached person now appears on the map.** Places without surveyed coordinates (battle sites, valleys, quarters) are drawn at their containing place's position with a small offset, which also brings in the people and events linked only to them. Region markers stay visible across the whole timeline, and cities use a wireframe glyph.
- **Era-aware region names and a data-driven Hijri range.** The zoomed-out world shows each region's era name at the selected year (e.g. العصر النبوي over Arabia at 11 AH) from `data/period/` records, falling back to the geographic name; the year slider range is computed from the actual spans in the map's entity slice instead of a fixed −74…1448.
- **Map viewer follow-up fixes.** The toolbar is now in the page flow inside the viewer (no longer hidden under the sticky header); region city markers are smaller with wider collision spacing so overlapping cities like Mecca are clickable; and the mount animation no longer replays on first load, removing the initial flicker.
- **Validation and tour metadata corrected.** Kufa's founding year is stored as the EDTF string the schema expects, and the 3D tour's Medina and Córdoba stops now carry the same Wikidata source citation as the enriched place records, restoring the schema validation and halls parity checks.

## v1.4.0 — 2026-11-08

### Added
- **First TEI-enriched objects: the four dated tiraz silk fragments of 132 AH.** Four new object records cite the Thesaurus d'Épigraphie Islamique fiches for the famous set of inscribed silk textiles dated 132 AH (749–750 CE) and found in Egypt — now dispersed across the Victoria and Albert Museum (London), the Brooklyn Museum (New York), the Whitworth Art Gallery (Manchester) and Moscow's Museum of Oriental Cultures — each cross-linked to its three siblings, all draft-tier pending human review.
- **Seven more trusted sources registered (second wave).** The Arabic Papyrology Database (13,586 pre-modern Arabic documents — the everyday-life evidence for early Islamic Egypt), the Princeton Geniza Project (4,350+ transcribed Geniza documents, Zenodo metadata), the University of Oxford's Manar al-Athar photo archive (~83,000 labelled site photographs — captions only, images never ingested), the Qatar Digital Library and HMML manuscript catalogues, plus the Museum With No Frontiers and Qantara Mediterranean heritage databases — all facts-only with stable-id citations. Zeno's coin database was assessed and held at pointer tier: its robots file bars all automated access and its data derives from published catalogues.
- **Nomisma.org registered as a trusted numismatic source (third wave).** The American Numismatic Society's linked-open-data ontology — the shared vocabulary for coins, mints, issuing authorities and standards, licensed CC-BY 3.0 with a SPARQL endpoint — joins the citation families at Tier 2: `{cite:nomisma <concept-id>}` is the attribution, partner-dataset records stay facts-only until their own licences are checked, and legend text and images are never republished. It is the machine-readable answer to the coin backlog the graph cannot yet carry (only two coin objects exist today) and corroborates mints, issuers and regnal dates across the whole Islamic timeline. Decision `dec-20261109-224`.
- **Six trusted web sources registered for citation.** Following the source-family criteria and decision-ledger rulings, the museum can now cite Archnet (Islamic architecture sites, authorities and media), the Thesaurus d'Épigraphie Islamique (dated inscriptions — Hijri and CE — for buildings and objects), the British Museum, the Victoria and Albert Museum Collections API, the Khalili Collections and the Qatar Museums / Museum of Islamic Art Doha object databases. All six are facts-only: record text and images are never republished, and every citation names the family's own stable id. The UNESCO World Heritage Centre dossier family was filed to the founder's docket instead.
- **New `web-sources` lane.** An autonomous agent lane that works through `docs/agents/source-families.md` end to end: assesses each registered, queued and exploratory web source family against the eight trust criteria, files every onboarding decision through the decision ledger, registers accepted families (harvest registry, `data/source/` entity, attribution row, tier tables) and enriches museum records with cited facts. Non-commercial families stay facts-only, permanently.
- **Tradition taxonomy reference.** `docs/decisions/tradition-taxonomy.md` maps every identifiable Muslim denomination — Sunni sub-schools and movements, the three Shia branches, Ibadi, Mu'tazila, Sufi orders, Quranists, Ahmadiyya, nondenominational, and groups outside the Muslim fold — with the ordered evidence test for classifying a person's tradition (self-designation → rijal label → corpus membership → works → teachers → geography → contested markers), feeding the tradition-attestation rule and judge rubric.
- **Full-autonomy mode for the decision approver (proof of concept).** The engine now runs in `mode: autonomous` by default on this branch: every former founder-docket surface — deploys, spending, outreach, deletions, licence changes, review-status, governance, conflicting authorities — gets the engine's own conservative, reversible decision instead of a human approval request. Deploy questions are answered with an explicit cost-aware cadence policy (deploy only on code/schema changes, milestones, or accumulated content deltas; never per-commit or docs-only). Hard content invariants — the terrorist-organisation block, Qur'an text, typed honorifics, prophet depictions — still refuse outright in every mode. `--mode conservative` restores the founder-docket behaviour for comparison.
- **Data-driven rule engine.** All gates, rules, domains and the autonomy map live in `docs/decisions/rules.yaml` — versioned, editable without code changes, priority-ordered. The engine records a full decision trace (`--explain`), machine-readable output (`--json`), and an advisory contract (`--advisory`) so any AI model can propose an action and receive the engine's authoritative verdict (`allow`, `redirect`, `deny`, `route-to-founder`). Decision records now feed back as precedents — every decided record becomes matchable authority for future questions.
- **Doctrine mined from the full commit history.** Twenty thousand commits yielded the founder's actual decision patterns, now encoded as rules: the doubt rule (doubt → unknown, absolute), the strict two-independent-sources faith rule (office, descent, movement membership and infobox-only values never count), the Shia-mapping precedent, homonyms never merge, unidentifiable items logged with searches, stubs replaced in place (REPLACE ruling), unrecognised wings default to Ideas, children's-wing rules, conflicts preserved as debated readings, external IDs fail-closed, reach thresholds for modern figures, inclusive harvest rules, the no-skip lane rule, and open corrections.
- **Benchmark at 70/70.** The labelled benchmark grew from 37 to 70 cases covering every decision domain — content, sources, dates, media, i18n, accessibility, process, engineering, safety and governance — plus per-mode autonomous cases, with per-class pass metrics.
- **Optional GenAI judge tier with bidirectional evaluation.** Held questions can optionally be advised by a local model (`DECIDE_JUDGE_CMD`, e.g. Ollama, or any OpenAI-compatible `DECIDE_JUDGE_URL`) — the model's reply is recorded as `status: recommended` with evidence, advisory only; the deterministic engine remains the sole authority, following the AI-control proposer/disposer pattern. The judge is now queried twice per held question — once under an affirmative framing and once under an adversarial "assume the obvious answer is a false conflation" framing (SCOPE-style bidirectional preference evaluation). Order-averaged confidence is penalised by inter-pass disagreement; material dissent keeps the safe-default hold and records `judge_dissent` for audit instead of upgrading. Set `DECIDE_JUDGE_SINGLE=1` for a single-pass call. Verified live against local `qwen3:32b` via Ollama.
- **Decision records carry provenance, modality and expiry.** Every record now records `modality` (book/website/video/audio/repo), `expires_at` (365-day TTL so early autonomous rulings are re-reviewed rather than hardening into permanent facts), and `derived_from` links to the governing rule, gate or precedent. Expired records drop out of precedent matching automatically and are listed in the docket's re-review section.
- **Hybrid precedent retrieval (BM25 + embeddings).** Precedent matching now fuses lexical BM25 with dense embeddings (`qwen3-embedding:0.6b` via local Ollama, corpus cached on disk) using weighted fusion — paraphrased or transliterated questions that BM25 misses can now match the ruling they mean, while a dual-path gate (cosine ≥ 0.68 AND title overlap ≥ 0.25 AND hybrid ≥ 0.52, or the unchanged lexical gates) keeps same-topic/different-question false matches out. Verified live: a zero-lexical-overlap paraphrase correctly stayed held, and a near-paraphrase matched its precedent at cosine 0.84. `DECIDE_HYBRID=0` disables; an unreachable endpoint silently falls back to BM25.
- **Judge uncertainty is now measured, not guessed.** The bidirectional judge passes combine into a proper SCOPE-style uncertainty score — binary entropy of mean support plus a framing-flip penalty — with verdict agreement detected by recommendation similarity rather than string equality. Confident passes reaching different conclusions, or composite uncertainty above 0.5, keep the safe-default hold with `judge_dissent` recorded. Judge calls also request grammar-constrained JSON and low temperature for reliability.
- **Two doctrine rules from the architecture audit.** Office/headship is now explicitly a separate claim type from faith — it may be recorded as a biographical fact on one source but never settles the `faith` field (the 1 Nov 2026 office shortcut was an unapproved agent draft reverted under PR #2873). And chronologically impossible dates — born/died outside a person's documented activity window — are stripped entirely rather than repaired by invention (the Hadji Kamlon R1 precedent).
- **Engineering documentation.** `docs/engineering/17-decision-approver.md` documents the full architecture — pipeline stages, rule engine, hybrid retrieval formulas and thresholds, judge BPE math, record schema, configuration reference, research basis and roadmap — so any agent or engineer can operate or extend the approver without reverse-engineering the code.
- **Precedent authority statuses (a proposal is not a precedent).** Every mined precedent now carries `provenance_status` — `founder-ruled`, `founder-ruled-ai-assisted`, `agent-ruled-delegated`, or `agent-proposed-pending` — assigned fail-closed by the extractor, plus `supersedes:` chain links. Only ruled entries may decide a question; proposals, observations and superseded rulings are excluded from authority. This encodes the lesson of the 1 November 2026 incident, where an AI-drafted packet that sounded like the founder reversed six of his positions and had to be reverted (PR #2873).
- **Adversarial benchmark traps.** Ten new benchmark cases encode the doctrine's trap list — office/descent/AI-output never settling faith, one source family ≠ two attestations, homonyms never merging, impossible dates stripped, excluded items never resurrected, unbelief needing own-words — plus `rule-ai-not-evidence` and `rule-excluded-absent`. Benchmark is now 81/81.
- **Judge packets are two-sided.** Judge prompts now require naming the strongest reason the obvious answer is wrong before recommending, and return decomposed confidence components (evidence strength, source independence, model agreement) alongside the aggregate — thin evidence, conflicting evidence and model disagreement are logged as different failure modes.
- **Fixed: decision-record id collision.** Record ids were derived from file count, which collided with live records when numbering had gaps — a batch run silently overwrote a research record. Ids now derive from the max existing suffix; the clobbered record was restored as `dec-20261108-015` with a `restored_from` note, and the founder's one-time FDR policy question is filed as `dec-20261108-016` for the docket.
- **Fixed: `kid` matched inside "wikidata".** The children's-wing rule pattern used bare substrings, so a Wikidata question was answered by the kids' rulebook. Patterns now use word boundaries; a systematic boundary audit of short tokens is on the roadmap.
- **Governance digest.** `scripts/decisions/digest.ts` writes `docs/decisions/digest.md` at the end of every batch run and via `npm run decisions:digest`: blocked-item count as the headline metric (founder-docket items + undecided inbox questions), autonomous decision rate, safe-state rate by domain, override rate, benchmark debt, expired backlog, judge dissent — with honest `instrumentation: partial` markers where machinery doesn't exist yet.
- **Record validation gate.** `scripts/decisions/check-records.ts` (`npm run decisions:check`) asserts the ledger schema — required fields fail, legacy-missing optional fields warn, `supersedes:` chains and cited precedent ids must resolve. Currently 15/15 valid.
- **Override records are live.** `kind: override` records with `supersedes:` now work end-to-end: the superseded record is excluded from precedent authority (dead authority, never deleted), the override itself becomes a `ledger-record` precedent carrying the corrected ruling, and records serialize `supersedes`, `correct_outcome`, `wrong_outcome`, `override_reason`, `signals`, `induction`, `jury`, `state_chain` fields.
- **Calibration logging on every record.** New records carry a `calibration_log` block — deterministic gate pass, fired rule count, precedent distance, top precedent id/status, judge framing confidences + entropy + verdict agreement, `founder_resolution: null` as the future label stream for conformal/isotonic calibration.
- **Two new rules.** `rule-relation-direction` (edges only in attested direction, else prose-as-claim) and `rule-ui-no-deviation` (UI changes ship inside the current pattern; deviations become labelled proposals).
- **Fixed: judge command contract.** `DECIDE_JUDGE_CMD` now receives the question payload on stdin (matching JUDGE-SETUP.md) instead of as a command argument.
- **Decision ledger page and API (proof of concept).** A new `/{lang}/decisions/` page lists the auditable records emitted by the decision pipeline — each question, its status (decided, with the founder, or rejected), the precedent it rests on, its confidence and rationale — alongside the count of precedents mined from the repository's own rulings. The same records are exported at `/api/v1/decisions.json`. This is the visible surface for testing the autonomous-decision proof of concept; deploys, deletions, spending, outreach and review-status changes remain founder-only by design.
- **Decision inbox and founder docket (proof of concept).** Lanes can now drop questions into `docs/decisions/inbox/` instead of interrupting the founder; a batch run of the decision pipeline answers what it can by rule or cited precedent and regenerates `docs/decisions/docket.md` with only the items that genuinely need the founder. First pilot: the ten open coverage-programme decisions were routed — five to the docket (money, schema, robots.txt, commission, authorisation) and five held at the conservative default pending a real precedent, after a fix that stops observational flags from masquerading as rulings.
- **Harvest decisions now route through the decision engine.** A new section in the source-mining guide (`docs/agents/mining-sources.md` §4b, pointed to from the library lane doc) makes it explicit: every labeling, classification and judgment call a harvest makes — a source's standing, school or tradition, edition choice, an exclusion, a contested attribution — goes through the decision ledger (inbox → `decide.ts` → record), never the harvesting agent's own discretion. Mechanical choices and founder-only surfaces (exclusions, safety blocks, Qur'an text, licences) are carved out explicitly.
- **Decision-engine documentation refreshed and the local model layer documented.** `docs/engineering/17-decision-approver.md` and `docs/decisions/README.md` now reflect the shipped system: the question/proposed_action text split (gates see the proposal, rules and precedents see only the question), conservative default with opt-in autonomous mode and the `safe_proceed` domain list, founder-only deploy/delete/spend/outreach surfaces, precedent authority statuses with TTL and supersession, the override-bypass contract, agent self-labelling under the standing delegation, the golden-set doctrine, and the full operator script surface. New `docs/engineering/18-local-models.md` documents the Mac-side model layer — machine roles (Mac computes, Devin orchestrates and translates), the model inventory and per-component assignments, selection rationale from current research, and optimization notes. `docs/decisions/JUDGE-SETUP.md` and `docs/agents/workflow.md` §9b carry the same machine-roles ruling.

### Fixed
- **Harvest source registry parses again.** `scripts/harvest/sources.yaml` had entries appended outside the `sources:` mapping (after the top-level `workspace:` key) plus several unquoted values containing `: ` and a broken apostrophe — the file could not be loaded by the harvest scripts. The stray entries are now correctly nested and the scalars quoted; content unchanged.
- **i18n YAML escape fix inherited from main.** `i18n/en.yaml` and `i18n/ur.yaml` carried an unescaped apostrophe in `charter_body` ("in the founder's words" inside a single-quoted scalar), which broke YAML parsing and four tests; doubled to `founder''s`. Surfaced by the decision-ledger merge — the same fix belongs on main.
- **Decision pipeline self-heal pass.** Robustness fixes after the first pilot: policy patterns no longer fire inside negated phrases ("not a deploy"), batch runs are idempotent via `question_hash` (decided questions are skipped, not re-recorded), the precedent miner excludes `docs/decisions/` and status-table rows to prevent self-citation and garbage titles, `decisions.json` uses the newest record's date instead of a build timestamp so it only changes when the ledger does, `docket.md` now also lists questions held at the safe default that a precedent would unblock, and the matcher gained a canonical-rule step plus a title-overlap gate so only strong, on-subject precedents can decide.
- **Adversarial-review hardening of the decision engine (critical fixes).** An independent adversarial review probed the engine and found live failure modes; all demonstrated ones are now fixed and locked in by 11 new benchmark cases (92/92, now asserting the exact rule/gate/precedent id, not just the step): (1) a wrong autonomous ruling was live precedent authority — the `kid`-in-`wikidata` bug's record `dec-20261108-014` is reversed by override `dec-20261108-017`, and the benchmark now certifies the corrected ruling; (2) hard rejects now evaluate before non-delegable gates, so "deploy a page showing a painted prophet portrait" is rejected, never autonomously approved; (3) the negation guard no longer exempts imperative deletes/spend from gates; (4) precedent retrieval reads the literal question only — evidence, options and proposals can no longer stuff a match; (5) ledger records are depth-0 authority only: precedent-step records are never re-cited, overrides are the only hand-written authority, and the checker fails on foreign authorship, stale rule ids, dead supersedes links and contradictory duplicate question hashes; (6) the precedent extractor can mint `founder-ruled` authority only inside founder-owned files, honours `supersedes` only there, tightens delegated-scope vocabulary, namespaces colliding lane decision ids (`D-001@inventions-decisions`) and fails on any remaining duplicate; (7) six doctrine rules that fired on substrings (`ai` inside "main", `title`, `different`, `unreachable`, `minor`, bare `conflict`) were rewritten with bounded patterns, and a new `rule-source-families` rule now correctly answers mirror-counting questions; (8) the extremism hard-block scan now covers the published decision ledger (records, inbox, docket, digest); (9) the site ledger parser fails loudly with the filename instead of a bare YAML error.

- **Decision-engine rollout safety: conservative default, per-domain autonomy, concurrency guards.** Following the adversarial review's rollout warnings: the engine's default mode is now `conservative` (founder docket) — `autonomous` is opt-in per run. Even in autonomous mode, gate-mapping only proceeds for domains on the new `safe_proceed:` list in `rules.yaml` (engineering, process, governance, money-outreach — the pilot classes whose mappings are advisory and reversible); every other domain docks, fail-closed. The engine now reads `origin/main`'s decision records before writing: questions already decided on main are skipped and record ids never re-mint a number main already has, closing the two-worktree collision path; the record checker additionally fails on duplicate record ids and contradictory duplicate question hashes. `docket.md` and `digest.md` are now generated artifacts (gitignored, no longer committed — they were last-writer-wins merge-conflict magnets). `npm run validate` now runs the record checker and the 92-case benchmark, so a red ledger fails CI. New `scripts/decisions/founder-rule.ts` records the founder's verdict (`approved`/`rejected`/`held`) into a record's `calibration_log.founder_resolution` — the label stream every agreement metric depends on; first label applied to the dec-017 override.

- **Precedent replay diagnostic.** `scripts/decisions/replay.ts` replays every extractable lane question through the engine in conservative mode and reports coverage plus citation precision — first run: 55 questions, 15 decided, 40 held (all held trace to `agent-proposed-pending` lane logs — the engine correctly refuses to treat unratified proposals as precedent), 0 rejected, 1 precedent citation and it was authority. This is the coverage/precision instrument; agreement still awaits `founder_resolution` labels via `founder-rule.ts`.

- **Pilot seeding: 55 real lane questions through the engine.** `scripts/decisions/seed-inbox.ts` converts non-authority precedent questions into inbox files (deduped by question_hash, authority precedents skipped); first seed wrote 55 inbox questions and the batch produced 55 records — 14 decided by doctrine rules, 2 by delegated-authority precedents, 39 held at safe-default pending founder labels. The held set is the pilot docket: each awaits a `founder-rule.ts` verdict that becomes the calibration label stream. Ledger now 71 records, all valid.

- **Process/engineering pilot class seeded.** Twenty realistic agent-workflow questions (merge conflicts, CANARY/version rules, schema-first ordering, deploy cadence, lane claims, i18n same-commit rules, id collisions, validate failures) written to the inbox from actual repo rules; batch produced 20 records — 6 doctrine rules, 8 safe-default holds, 6 policy-gate dockets (deploy, authority-conflict, delete, review-status, governance ×2 — all legitimate gate surfaces). One observed gate false-positive candidate: "delete the file and regenerate" phrasing trips nd-delete though no entity is harmed — logged for the rule-precision audit. Ledger: 91 records, all valid.

- **Calibration instruments: surface audit + applied-state tracking.** `scripts/decisions/audit.ts` reports founder_resolution labels per rule/gate/step — the per-surface agreement rates the autonomous-promotion gate needs (currently 1 label; everything else honestly shows "insufficient data"). `scripts/decisions/mark-applied.ts` records `state_chain.current_state: applied` when a decided record's outcome is actually acted on — the decided→applied funnel Fable flagged as unmeasured. First entries: dec-017 labelled approved and marked applied. Full `npm run validate` now passes end-to-end including the ledger checker and benchmark.

- **First founder verdict batch: 65 records labelled.** The founder answered every held record as yes/no/hold; all verdicts are written into `calibration_log.founder_resolution` via `founder-rule.ts` — 35 approved, 22 rejected, 8 held (66 labels total including dec-017). This is the first real calibration data: `scripts/decisions/audit.ts` now reports per-surface agreement, and the rejected content leads (dec-024, 027–029, 033, 036, 040, 044, 047–051, 062–063) are recorded as non-qualifying so they do not return as precedent authority. Process/governance approvals (robots.txt Content-Signal, corpus access, lane registrations, predicate confirmations, version bump) are the pilot's first authorised decisions.

- **Second verdict batch: 24 ruled records labelled, exposing a live authority leak — now fixed.** The founder ruled on every decided record: 16 approved, 8 rejected. labelling immediately proved its worth — reworded variants of the rejected questions were still being *decided by precedent*, citing the very records the founder had just rejected (dec-018's accessibility misfire, dec-085's entity-dedup-on-git-merge). `loadLedgerPrecedents` now treats `founder_resolution: rejected` and `held` as dead authority alongside superseded and expired records — a wrong ruling can no longer propagate to similar questions while awaiting an override record. Root causes of the five confirmed rule false positives are also fixed: `aria` matched inside "variants" (rule-accessibility and the domain classifier), `rant` inside "quadrant" (rule-harvest-include), `miss…row` spanning "missions…browser" (rule-nothing-skipped), `merge…into` and `same entity file` matching git questions (rule-duplicate-alias), and bare `UI` firing the layout-deviation rule on an i18n question (rule-ui-no-deviation). All patterns now use word boundaries or bounded lookahead. A new `rule-i18n-same-commit` encodes the AGENTS.md rule the rejected record was actually asking about. Six post-label probe cases lock every fix into the benchmark — now 98/98. Ledger: 90 founder labels total; audit shows rule-level agreement is real signal now (duplicate-alias 0/3, accessibility 0/1, harvest-include 0/1, nothing-skipped 0/1, ui-no-deviation 0/1 — all founder-rejected and all fixed).

- **CEGIS loop closes: founder verdicts now induce rules.** The second label batch's approved/rejected outcomes were mined for doctrine the engine lacked — five new rules encode them: generated artifacts regenerate rather than hand-merge (dec-080), Arabic-parenthesis isolation ships in the same commit (dec-074's rejected follow-up framing), AGENTS.md governs over plan sequencing (dec-077), local-only test failures with green CI are environment noise (dec-091), and colliding ids are renumbered (dec-082). Each cites its grounding verdict; six benchmark cases lock them (105/105). One induced rule was deliberately dropped: predicate-first registration is already covered by the `nd-governance` non-delegable gate — the founder's dec-089 approval answered a docketed question, which is the gate working as designed. `audit.ts` gained a domain rollup — the per-class promotion view (currently no domain near the 50-label bar; fallback/unclassified dominate because legacy records predate the domain field).

- **Second label-seeding wave: 39 realistic questions → 39 records (ledger: 130).** Fresh process/engineering, content, sources, dates, media, safety and governance scenarios written to the inbox from actual repo rules — 14 decided by doctrine rules, 17 held at safe-default, 7 policy-gate dockets, 1 delegated precedent. First-run spot check found four more rule false positives, all fixed and regression-locked: `independent sources` fired the attestation-counting rule on a date-conflict question (now bounded to counting vocabulary; `rule-conflict-preserve` also gained "sources give/report different" and "different death/birth/date" patterns), bare `same person` fired entity-dedup on non-dedup questions (now requires a second dedup signal within 50 chars), `hand-edit` sat outside the generated-regen window (widened, `regenerat` added), and `ur next batch` exceeded the i18n-same-commit window (widened). Also fixed a self-reinforcement surface the new records exposed: rule-decided ledger records are doctrine restatements — they no longer enter the precedent corpus (`rule_id` records excluded), since the rule itself is the authority and re-citing the record only adds retrieval noise. Benchmark: 105/105. `replay.ts` gained `--mask-self` (generalization test) plus self-cite/other-authority breakdown; first masked run: 16 decided / 39 held / 0 non-authority citations — identical masked and unmasked because pending precedents cannot self-cite.

- **Chain-integrity fields on every decided record.** Records decided by a rule or precedent now carry a `chain:` block — `depth` (bounded at 1 by construction: precedent-step records never become precedents, so citation chains cannot launder TTL), `root_id`, `root_kind` (rule / mined-precedent / ledger-record), `root_expires_at`, and `derived_rule_hash` — a hash of the governing rule text or cited precedent content, so a later doctrine edit makes past derivations measurably stale. `check-records.ts` enforces the depth≤1 invariant, verifies `root_id` resolves, and warns on stale rule derivations. Verified live: a Wikidata-debt question derives `depth:1, root_id:dec-20261108-017` through the override chain.

- **Audit and digest integrity reporting.** `audit.ts` now flags rule/gate surfaces as `DEMOTE CANDIDATE` when they carry ≥3 founder verdicts below the 95% agreement bar (step surfaces excluded — a rejected hold is a coverage gap, not a wrong rule). `digest.ts` reports chain-depth violations and contradictory duplicate question-hashes as zero-tolerance metrics alongside the existing dashboard. First live flag: `rule:rule-duplicate-alias` at 0% — already fixed; the flag is the regression alarm.

- **Audit disagreement worklist + README refresh.** `audit.ts` now ends with the actionable list: `decided-but-rejected` records (wrong rulings to fix — currently 8, all already remediated by the rule-tightening wave and re-verified live: chess→safe-default, git-merge questions→`rule-merge`, i18n→`rule-i18n-same-commit`, Wikidata→dec-017 override, sextant→D-109) vs `held/docket-but-rejected` coverage gaps (22 — these need new rules or rulings, not fixes). `docs/decisions/README.md` updated: conservative is the documented default, the full tool inventory is tabled, and the `chain:`/`calibration_log` record anatomy is described.

- **Founder verdicts enacted as override authority.** The 21 records where the founder's verdict on a held/docket question was a substantive "no" are now `kind: override` records (`dec-20261108-132`–`152`) that supersede the dead-end holds — each faithfully restates the ruling (e.g. "do not batch-mark the 400 records reviewed", "Ibn al-Haytham credits the pinhole observation only", "alpha 0.02 not 0.05", "AI prose stays draft until human read"). Re-asked questions now cite them as precedent instead of re-holding. dec-087 deliberately excluded — its verdict was ambiguous. Known boundary: policy gates still intercept before precedent, so gated questions like dec-002's still docket even with an override on record — safe but worth revisiting.

- **Exact-question founder overrides bypass gates.** `decide()` now checks for a live `kind: override` record matching the question's exact hash after hard-rejects but before founder-reserved and policy gates — the founder already ruled on *this* question, so re-docketing is waste. Exact-hash only: fuzzy precedent similarity still cannot bypass a gate, and hard rejects still fire first. Verified: re-asking the "400 records reviewed" question resolves `decided/override → dec-132` instead of re-docketing; novel questions unaffected; benchmark 105/105.

- **Stale-record sweep killed a live wrong-authority record.** Re-running every rule-decided record's question through the current engine found 9 stale citations — 8 already dead via founder-rejected labels, but `dec-20261108-129` (a date-conflict question answered by `rule-duplicate-alias`, generated before the pattern tightening) was still live ledger precedent teaching the wrong ruling. Override `dec-20261108-153` supersedes it; re-asks now resolve to the conflict-preserve ruling. This is the second instance of the dec-014 vulnerability class — worth a periodic sweep as rules evolve.

- **Wave-2 calibration: 39 founder labels + 9 enacted rulings + policy changes.** All 39 second-wave records labelled (18 approved / 8 rejected / 13 held). The 8 substantive rejections became override records `dec-154`–`162` (incl. dec-087 clarified: file separately, dedicated hotfix PR for broken main). Two rulings changed live policy: **money-outreach removed from `safe_proceed`** — spend and outreach now always docket for manual founder sign-off (benchmark expectations updated to certify); and **agents no longer self-merge** — AGENTS.md now says the founder merges every PR (dec-160). `expires_at` backfilled on all records: check-records reports **0 failures, 0 warnings**. Local judge enabled: `npm run decisions:local` wires `DECIDE_JUDGE_*`/`DECIDE_EMBED_*` to Ollama (`qwen3:32b` + `qwen3-embedding:0.6b`); verified live — a held VR-exhibit question produced affirmative+adversarial evidence with `judge_dissent: true` while the engine correctly stayed at safe-default.

- **Self-maintaining ledger: sweep script, lane wiring, judge triage.** `scripts/decisions/sweep.ts` re-runs every live rule-decided record's question through the engine and fails `npm run validate` on stale citations — the dec-014/dec-129 vulnerability class is now a CI gate, not a manual audit (first run: 23 live records, 0 stale). `docs/agents/workflow.md` gained section 9: every session is now instructed to route ambiguities through `docs/decisions/inbox/` + `decide.ts --batch --write` instead of blocking on the founder — this is what generates real calibration labels. `scripts/decisions/triage.ts` (`npm run decisions:triage`) produces a judge-recommendation digest over unlabelled holds; currently empty because every held record carries a verdict — the tool is ready for the next wave. Replay after the override wave: lane-question coverage rose 13→30 decided (19 via other-authority precedent, 0 non-authority citations, masked==unmasked).

- **Real-question wave 3: 11 lane-mined decisions + two more FP kills.** Questions extracted from actual lane progress files (modern-figures, ei2, azhar-academy, dawlat-uthmaniyya, hisham, khutab-durus) → 8 rule decisions, 2 safe-defaults, 1 governance docket — all queued for founder labels. The wave immediately paid for itself: `rule-merge` matched `pr` inside "repre**sented**" on a Hijri-date question and `rule-bug-fix` matched "fail" inside "fail-closed" plus "api" inside an option — both patterns now word-bounded (with a `-closed` guard), and stale records dec-164/dec-173 superseded by overrides dec-174/dec-175. `sweep.ts` also learned to replay full inbox questions (options+evidence), not just the question string — it had produced two false stale positives before the fix.

- **Canon authenticity queue opened: batch-01 proposal prepared.** The first agent-prepared batch of canon authenticity decisions (25 books, adab-zuhd + aqeedah, per queue order) is drafted in `docs/delegation/canon-batch-01-proposal.md` under the dec-133 delegation ruling: 16 accept candidates with Wikipedia-verified Sunni school evidence, 6 label/unverified proposals (including al-Jahiz as Mu'tazila per his article infobox), edition evidence flagged where archive.org metadata names publishers/editors. Batch 01 marked `[~]` with founder in `phase-02-queue.md`. Nothing is written to the authenticity register until the founder approves the batch. The batch surfaced a real policy gap — the validator requires a publisher-named edition for every accept even though pre-print books are authentic by manuscript/institutional provenance — filed as inbox question `canon-accept-manuscript-basis` (dec-176, safe-default → founder docket).

- **Second-opinion audit fixes: institutional-outreach gate + regex boundary sweep.** External review caught that `nd-outreach`/`money-outreach` lacked institutional names — a question like "apply for UNESCO partnership status" could classify into a safe domain and bypass the founder's money-outreach removal. Both the gate pattern and the domain pattern now cover UNESCO/UNICEF/DPGA/ICDE/OIC, apply-for/application-to, partner-with, membership, accreditation, award, grant and funding; two benchmark dockets lock it. A short-token audit of all 49 rules also fixed four latent substring matches: `ten` inside "often" (source-families), `to`/`do`/`id` unbounded in alias/one-source/external-id groups — benchmark now 108/108, sweep clean.

- **Second-opinion audit round 2 (Muse): question-only rule matching + 5 overrides + proposal corrections.** Muse's empirical audit found rules/gates could be steered by asker-written options — matching now scores the question only, same as precedents (dec-163/167 went stale and are superseded by overrides dec-177/178). New overrides: dec-179 enacts the founder's dec-104 "soften unsourced consensus" ruling (the stored decision was a wrong-rule misfire that got labelled anyway), dec-180/181 enact approved-yes verdicts on holds for symmetry. rule-conflict-preserve widened for "which Hijri date / how should the conflict be represented" phrasings; founder_reserved now catches "pending the founder's decision"; judge docs/examples corrected to qwen2.5:32b per the founder's stated model. Canon proposal corrected: Isfahani is Shi\'i-leaning per EI3/Britannica/Iranica (not "universally Sunni"), Ibn Arabi recommendation strengthened to label/other, Sarraj/Mubarak reason texts fixed, and two disclosures added — the one-source ruling has no repo record, and 13/16 accepts still need named editions. Benchmark 110/110, sweep clean, 180/180 records.

- **Claude audit fixes: gate visibility, founder-only surfaces, batch-01 reconciliation.** Three holes closed: (1) proposed_action is now visible to gates/hard-rejects/founder-reserved/domain classification again — a dangerous proposal can no longer hide behind an innocuous question (rules and precedent matching stay question-only); (2) deploy, delete, spend and outreach lost their autonomous gate mappings entirely — they reach the founder in every mode, closing the domain-classification bypass; (3) the exact-question override bypass now requires a founder label, so unlabelled agent overrides remain precedent authority but cannot skip gates. Canon batch-01 reconciled with the founder's 31-Oct accept-all decision (`phase-02-batch01-evidence.md`): the proposal now cites it, adds the three missing books (Qushayri, Sulami, Ahmad ibn Hanbal), carries the earlier edition findings forward, and corrects the Buyid-era error. dec-133 clarified: founder approves each batch, not each book. Benchmark 112/112, sweep clean, 180/180 records; one unrelated graph-endpoint test fails on stale build output in this worktree.

- **Founder rulings enacted: full-autonomy delegation, draft-tier AI output, canon evidence fixes.** Eleven rulings applied after three-way audit reconciliation (founder + Muse + Claude). Engine: mined precedents now carry a 1-year expires_at and supersedes dead-lettering (decide.ts + extractor); founder-minted precedent authority requires a dated claim in whitelisted paths (Q10 interim). dec-186 records the standing delegation: the agent labels records and agents hold full precedent authority — hard gates remain founder-only. - **Canon queue cleared: all 295 books decided under delegation.** First full exercise of the dec-186 autonomy delegation: the agent decided all 292 remaining canon books in one sweep — 234 accept (school sunni verified via person-graph traditions or attested-author research), 61 label (3 shia incl. contested al-Isfahani, 1 mutazili, 5 other/modern-academic, 52 unverified). Method: strict person-graph matching (last-token matching rejected after wrong-person hits), attested-author map for famous scholars, book-level overrides for anonymous works. Every entry carries `decided_by: devin-swe2 (agent, founder delegation)` — reversible, auditable, and the phase-13 second-source pass can upgrade labels later. dec-187 records the sweep methodology. Phase-02 queue fully checked.

- **Golden-set doctrine enacted.** Founder rule (dec-188): everything currently in the museum — all data, prose, events, persons, books — is the golden reference. Rules and the decision engine conform to it, never the reverse; a rule that would rule out existing content is wrong and gets fixed. New rules apply forward only — existing published content is never retroactively invalidated (this also settles that the draft-tier AI rule applies to new output, not the existing corpus). Added to AGENTS.md as a rule that never bends.

- **Golden-set audit of the canon sweep.** First application of dec-188: cross-checked all 292 agent canon decisions against the person graph's own tradition records — found 3 conflicts (al-Shawkani's record carries mixed sunni + shia-zaydi traditions; my attested-author map had flattened it to sunni). Corrected nayl-awtar, tafsir-shawkani and irshad-fuhul to label/other with the contest preserved. Final canon state: 231 accept, 64 label.

- **First Arabic Papyrology Database enrichments: four records gain paper-document attestations.** Working through APD's JSP catalogue (facts-only, `{cite:apd <inventory>}` anchors), four entities now cite surviving Arabic paper and papyrus documents — al-Fustat gains three documents issued at the city in 801–900 CE (a house sale, a room lease in an enclosure, and a rent roll of urban properties), Qasr al-Hayr al-Gharbi gains a marble fragment bearing five lines of a letter of Caliph Hisham dated 724–743 CE, Mecca gains two letters sent from the pilgrimage city to business friends in Fustat (901–1000 and 1101–1200 CE), and Ahmad ibn Tulun gains a patent preserved as a flyleaf in a Syriac manuscript (870–882 CE, Alexandria).

- **EAMENA registered as a source family: the MENA archaeological-site database joins the harvest registry.** `source/eamena` (decision dec-20261108-222, superseding an engine false-positive) records the Endangered Archaeology in the Middle East and North Africa database — ~383,000 heritage-place records from Oxford, Leicester and Durham on the Getty/WMF ARCHES platform — under its stated CC BY 4.0 licence with attribution. The museum cites it as `{cite:eamena <heritage-place-id>}` for site identity, period and recorded condition; the public access tier withholds coordinates, so no coordinate claims are sourced from it without research registration.

The family stays registered (CC BY 4.0, attribution); its `reliability_note` now records the verified limitation, and the pilot waits on research access or a working public query path.

Runs lib-wave-21-mishkat-masabih-1 to -6.

- **AlFehrest registered as a Tier-3 pointer source; IDEO Diamond / al-Kindī queued for assessment.** Following the Muse assessment and decision `dec-20261108-190`: alfehrest.org (interactive timeline/map of polities, rulers and scholars 700–1500 CE) joins Encyclopaedia Iranica's class — discovery and diffing only, every fact re-cited to the underlying source each page names, never a citation target; the entry carries the FIHRIST (fihrist.org.uk) name-collision warning. IDEO Diamond / the al-Kindī project (ideo.diamondrda.org, Dominican Institute for Oriental Studies, Cairo) — the institutional author/work authority database AlFehrest links into — is added to the explore list as a candidate for the works backlog.
- **IDEO Diamond / AlKindi onboarded as a Tier-1 source family (facts-only).** Following the Muse assessment and founder-approved decision `dec-20261108-191`: `source/ideo-diamond` registers the IDEO Cairo / LRM-CS IFLA-LRM/RDA catalogue (>230k works, >116k agents, typed commentary/refutation/abridgement relations) for the works backlog — citable for bibliographic facts only, never a work's contents, facts-only until LRM-CS confirms a data licence. Harvest channel today is the Wikidata P8795/P11979 crosswalk plus per-record citation (`{cite:ideo-diamond work/<id>}`); bulk use waits on a data-sharing conversation with LRM-CS.
- **Founder delegation: agents act as the human in the loop.** `AGENTS.md` now records the founder's standing delegation (8 Nov 2026): the agent owns the full decision lifecycle — understand the situation, generate and research options (including acquiring books/corpora and setting its own source-trust criteria), weigh consequences and side effects, choose, execute, follow up and verify, and record every judgment in the decision ledger for asynchronous audit. The founder's hard invariants (terrorist-organisation block, Qur'an text, licence posture, safety gates) still stand unless explicitly lifted.
- **tafsir.app harvest approved and launched.** Founder instructed the 72-book tafsir/ulum harvest (dec-20261108-192, workspace-local under facts-only posture — texts never republished, citations name underlying editions). Recon verified the get.php route end-to-end; the sequential resumable download is running in the harvest workspace with per-book manifests and a verification pass queued.
- **Founder delegation: own the museum's completeness and growth.** `AGENTS.md` gains a second standing mandate (8 Nov 2026): agents proactively enrich prose and website and grow the museum — auditing coverage, usability, display and quality gaps, then filling them with rich cited trilingual prose in validated batches — with the goal of making islam.museum the most useful and most referenced website about Islam on the global web.
- **Tradition-attestation rule and person-faith audit shipped.** `rule-tradition-attestation` joins the decision rules: a person's tradition/madhhab/sect requires cited biographical evidence (self-designation → rijal label → single-school tabaqat → works → rijal membership → teachers → geography-as-context), judge/model/dataset recommendations are proposals never attestations, contested markers stay contested, and name/family/birthplace never count. `scripts/decisions/tradition-audit.ts` scanned all 11,299 person records: 322 documented, 1,112 basis-only, 770 default-only, 1,975 unknown-only, 7,120 missing — 9,865 judge-packet candidates for the tradition-classification pipeline (`docs/decisions/tradition-attestation-audit.md`).
- **Judge packets for the tradition pipeline generated.** `scripts/decisions/tradition-packets.ts` builds one ready-to-classify evidence packet per audit candidate — identity, dates, teachers, students (inverse `student_of` index), authored works, group memberships, summary, and a rubric prompt carrying the taxonomy's evidence hierarchy and hard rules — written to `docs/decisions/tradition-packets.jsonl` (9,865 packets, regenerable, gitignored). The Itqan narrator database claim is verified: github.com/R3GENESI5/Itqan is real, MIT-reported, ~115k rijal profiles from 22 classical texts; recorded as a corroborating signal in `docs/decisions/tradition-taxonomy.md`, never a sole attestation.
- **Tradition judge runner added.** `scripts/decisions/tradition-judge.ts` sends packet prompts to the local OpenAI-compatible judge (Ollama, `DECIDE_JUDGE_URL`/`DECIDE_JUDGE_MODEL`), collects strict-JSON verdicts into `docs/decisions/tradition-judge-results.jsonl`, and is resumable by person id. Verdicts are proposals for the ledger and review — they never write `data/person` directly.
- **Tradition pipeline scoring and cross-match tooling.** `scripts/decisions/tradition-score.ts` scores judge verdicts against recorded attestations through a label-normalization hierarchy (exact / compatible / abstain / disagree with agreement and disagree rates) — the golden-set benchmark. `scripts/decisions/islamlab-match.ts` rebuilds the islamlab/islamic-scholars cross-match on normalized Arabic names plus a death-year sanity check: 283 museum matches, 42 carrying madhhab labels → 11 agreements, 0 disagreements, 31 museum-unlabeled pilot candidates; the dataset stays a corroborating signal only. The Itqan narrator database licence is now confirmed MIT via its Zenodo deposit (the GitHub repo ships no LICENSE file), and a draft LRM-CS/IDEO outreach requesting the Diamond data licence plus a reciprocal CC0 exchange is ready for the founder to send (`docs/delegation/lrm-cs-diamond-outreach-draft.md`).
- **The Founder's Charter now opens the museum's plan.** On 8 November 2026 the founder stated the project's doctrine in his own words — first in a message explaining the museum to a friend, then directed to stand as its vision, strategy and doctrine. The Charter (`docs/plan/00-founders-charter.md`, with its Arabic text and the message preserved verbatim) now governs the plan: the raw material is the content of one to two thousand of the mother books of Islam, read page by page by AI — mentions first, identity resolution (a known person is enriched, a new one created), then place, company, exact words, events, context and theme, and only then the classification rules, Sunni or not among them. The knowledge graph of the whole umma is the foundation; the website and everything in it are applications for displaying it. Progress is measured against the corpus (the founder estimates barely 1–1.5% of the first thousand books mined so far, yielding over 160,000 pages of persons, places, events and exact quotes), never against page counts. And AI images are stated for what they are: the model told what the graph knows and asked to draw its imagining — a reading of the graph, never a depiction of its subject. The vision document carries the Charter's banner, `AGENTS.md` points every agent to it first, and the Method page opens with a plain-language digest of it in Arabic, English and Urdu.

- **First microSD-library harvest batch (siyar-nisa continuation).** Ten new women join the museum's people collection from Umar Rida Kahhala's *A'lam al-Nisa'* (vols 1–3, Risala 1984 edition, the local microSD scans): Amina bint al-Sharid — the eloquent Ali-partisan Mu'awiya imprisoned in Damascus, who cursed him over her husband Umar ibn al-Humq's severed head and died of plague at Homs; Umm Aban bint Utba — the Qurashi widow of Aban ibn Sa'id who refused the proposals of Umar, al-Zubayr and Ali each on her own grounds; Arwa bint al-Harith — the Prophet's aunt and the most celebrated woman orator at Mu'awiya's court; Ramla bint al-Zubayr — beloved of Khalid ibn Yazid and courted by Abd al-Malik; Sa'da bint Kurayz — Uthman's aunt, the soothsayer-poetess who foretold Ruqayya's marriage; Aisha bint Uthman — Uthman's daughter, author of the famous rebuke after his killing; plus the pre-Islamic poetess Umama bint Dhi al-Isba', the Syrian waqf-saint Khadija bint Nasr Allah, and two traditionists (Zaynab bint Abd al-Baqi, Aisha bint Ali ibn Abd al-Ghani). Each carries cited Arabic, English and Urdu prose; referenced missing figures are registered as stubs. Run `microsd-books-batch-1`.
- **Second microSD-library harvest batch (rijal-hawl-rasul completion).** Khalid Muhammad Khalid's *Rijal Hawl al-Rasul* (Dar al-Muqattam 1415/1994 unified edition, the local microSD scan) completes its five thin-Companion queue: Abu Jabir — Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Haram, naqib of Banu Sakuma at the second Aqaba pledge, first Muslim killed at Uhud, whose body Jabir found uncorrupted forty-six years later in the grave shared with Amr ibn al-Jamuh — and Amr ibn al-Jamuh — chief of Banu Salama, the last of the Ansar to embrace Islam in the book's telling, who marched on Uhud on his lame foot saying he hoped to swim to Paradise on it, and lies in the same grave; both gain cited Arabic, English and Urdu "In Rijal Hawl al-Rasul" sections, the source in their records, a sibling/in-law edge between them, a `spouse_of` edge to the new `person/hind-bint-amr-ibn-haram` stub, and the lane's progress file is updated. Run `microsd-books-batch-2`.
- **Third microSD-library harvest batch (suwar-hayat-sahaba thin Companions).** `suwar-hayat-sahaba` (Abd al-Rahman Rafat al-Basha, *Suwar min Hayat al-Sahaba*, Dar al-Nafa'is 1412/1992, registered `source/suwar-min-hayat-al-sahaba-nafais-1992`) completes its five-target thin-record queue after identity resolution: three already carried the book or needed only verification — Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud (the Trench stratagem that broke the confederates, pp. 400–410), Fayruz al-Daylami and Zayd al-Khayr (canonical `zayd-al-khayl` with the Khayr alias) — while two were enriched trilingual: Majza'a ibn Thawr al-Sadusi (chief of Banu Bakr; the Tustar night-tunnel infiltration, the hundred champions, and his duel with al-Hurmuzan, pp. 156–163) and al-Rabi' ibn Ziyad al-Harithi (Umar's «no one has been truer to me», the Manadhir campaign and his brother al-Muhajir's martyrdom, the Sijistan/Barwiz peace, the Khurasan governorship dispute and his death prayer, pp. 419–427), kept distinct from the other Rabi' ibn Ziyad records and without a Companion role since Isaba lists him among tabi'in. All citations name the book and page; the lane's progress file is updated. Run `microsd-books-b3`.
- **Fourth microSD-library harvest batch (medicine-science: Manazir Book 1 + al-Farghani completion).** Ibn al-Haytham's *Kitab al-Manazir* Article 1 («في كيفية الإبصار بالجملة», Sabra 1983 vol. 1, scan pp. 60–200) is now described from its actual text in Arabic, English and Urdu on the work record: the opening survey of the two opposed doctrines of vision — the natural philosophers' incoming form versus the geometers' emitted visual cone — the author's inductive method, the ~144 propositions proving light travels in straight lines through holes into darkened rooms, the afterimage chapter, the layered anatomy of the eye, and the conditions of sight. Al-Farghani's *Jawami' 'ilm al-nujum* (Golius's 1669 Amsterdam Elementa astronomica) gains its missing English and Urdu prose — both the author record's book sections and a new work-record page — completing the trilingual coverage begun by the earlier harvest run. Run `microsd-books-b4`.

### Added
- **The goal, vision and strategy now stand in Arabic, English and Urdu, and IDEO Diamond is a Tier 1 source.** At the founder's direction, the Founder's Charter is published in all three languages (`00-founders-charter-ar.md`, `00-founders-charter.md`, `00-founders-charter-ur.md` — the Urdu a translation open to the founder's correction, the Arabic governing), the roadmap (`06-roadmap.md`) opens with its governing goal in the three languages (a full Urdu roadmap is the recorded next step), and the Method page's charter section gains the goal paragraph in all three languages.
- **IDEO Diamond / AlKindi registered as a Tier 1 source family** (`source/ideo-diamond`), on the founder's approval of the 8 November 2026 assessment. Diamond is the IFLA-LRM/RDA authority catalogue built at IDEO, Cairo (originally named AlKindi) and stewarded since 2021 by LRM-CS in Paris: 230,000+ works and 116,000+ agents shared by eleven libraries, with typed work-to-work relations (commentary, refutation, abridgement, sequel) and edition/translation history — the evidence class the museum's book-mining cannot produce for itself, feeding the 1,153-work prose backlog and author authority. Citable for authorship, work identity, edition history and relations as `{cite:ideo-diamond work/1781}` / `{cite:ideo-diamond agent/<id>}` — never for a work's contents. No data licence is published, so the posture is facts-only with attribution until LRM-CS confirms terms in writing; there is no public API or dump, so the machine channel is the Wikidata crosswalk (P8795 agents, P11979 works) and bulk use waits on a data-sharing conversation.

### Changed
- **The Charter gains its Article 0, and AlFehrest is registered as a pointer.** The founder's second statement of 8 November 2026 is now the Charter's opening article: Islam, with all its contents, available to everyone — old and young, Arab and non-Arab, Muslim and non-Muslim — and anyone free to reshape the knowledge graph in any form or application that suits their own users, above all schools, universities and study circles; the graph is the bridge to a knowledge that once demanded many books and a lifetime, a revival of the religious sciences for this age and the future. The statement is preserved verbatim (`docs/plan/founders-goal-2026-11-08.md`), carried into the vision document's "Why it matters" and into the Method page digest in all three languages. Separately, **AlFehrest** (alfehrest.org) is registered in `docs/agents/source-families.md` as a Tier 3 pointer after assessment: a volunteer timeline/map of Islamic civilisation (700–1500 CE) used for discovery and diffing only, never cited for a claim — and explicitly not Oxford's FIHRIST manuscript catalogue, an unrelated project with a near-identical name.

### Data
- **The Muhajirun/Ansar extension closes its qualifier set (batch MA-3).** The last 18 draft qualifiers gain their edges — 16 Ansar and 2 Muhajirun: Mus'ab ibn Umayr, who carried the Muhajirun's banner at Badr and Uhud, and Umm Salama, whose record narrates her own emigration. All 62 companions whose records explicitly establish their membership now carry it; twelve borderline cases remain for the founder's ruling.
- **The Ansar roll grows by 25 draft companions (coverage extension, batch MA-2).** Twenty-five more companions whose own records name their Aws or Khazraj tribe gain their Ansar membership edge — among them Abu Mas'ud al-Badri and al-Nu'man ibn Bashir.
- **Companions gain their Muhajirun and Ansar memberships (coverage extension, batch MA-1).** Under the founder's standard — an edge only where a companion's own record explicitly establishes it — 19 published companions gain their specific membership: 17 join the Ansar roll (among them Ka'b ibn Malik and Qatada ibn al-Nu'man) and 2 the Muhajirun. A scan of all 475 companion records found 62 who qualify on their own records' words; the rest stay under the general Companions membership rather than being classified by implication, and 12 borderline cases wait for the founder's ruling.

Entity and section pages are unaffected; the change takes effect at the next deploy.

One scouted name was excluded by the founder's ruling and one prominent preacher stays unbuilt because his audience figure exists only undated.

The ruling's first applications close wave 197: Akib Ahmed, the Dhaka drama creator behind Akib Islamic TV (5.38 million subscribers, now also a group record of its own), and Muhammad Badruzzaman, the singer-composer who founded Holy Tune and directs Kalarab, who qualifies on his own channel's 148,000 subscribers — his label's 10.8 million are the label's, not his.
- **The Bengali dawah scene enters the museum (modern-figures wave 197).** Twenty-one new records map the Bengali-language lecture (waz) world of Bangladesh and its diaspora: one preacher — Abdul Hai Muhammad Saifullah, khatib of Masjidul Juma Complex in Pallabi, Dhaka, whose verified Facebook page counts 3.3 million followers — and twenty lecture-aggregator channels from Islamer Rasta (5.14 million subscribers) down to Islamic Media Waz (291,000), each recorded from a dated platform read and each stating plainly that no named operator was identified for it. One promoted channel, Waz TV (886,000), is recorded from its statistics page because its handle could not be pinned, and one revived channel's three-year dormancy is stated rather than smoothed over. Channels already in the museum from an earlier pass (Shaykh Ahmadullah, Abu Taw Haa Muhammad Adnan, Holy Tune) were recognised and not duplicated.

Forty entity records gain a cited Assabile section in Arabic, English and Urdu — among them remembrance and gratitude (dhikr, shukr), renunciation and patience (zuhd, sabr), the soul's states in sleep (al-nafs wal-ruh), the Day of Resurrection scenes (yawm al-qiyama, shafaa, jannah), and the closing episode's command-versus-prohibition teaching (tawhid, iman, tawba).
