- **Ibn Sina's Canon gains its first organ-doctrine section; four harvest books are registered.** `concept/anatomy` now cites the three-volume Beirut 1999 print of the Canon (Book I, first part, fifth teaching, scan pp.36–41): Ibn Sina's definition of the organ, the simple/composite division, the ordered list of similar-part organs, the accepting and giving organs, and the principal and serving powers — described in Arabic, English and Urdu. The harvest queue (`scripts/harvest/library/books.yaml`) registers the three Canon print volumes and al-Farghani's Elements of Astronomy (Golius 1669) under medicine-science. Run `microsd-books-b8`.
- **Ibn al-Haytham's *Kitab al-Manazir* Article 2 is opened in the record.** The work page gains a trilingual "Article 2" section read from the Sabra 1983 scan: the four-chapter plan, the ray-line geometry of Chapter 2 — the ray from the centre of sight through the eye's humours, the vitreous humour's refracting surface, images ordered then refracted, the central ray's point clearest — and the opening of Chapters 3–4 on the meanings sight perceives beyond light and colour. Cited scan pages 198–309; draft-tier like the rest of the mined text. Run `microsd-books-b9`.
- **Five Hilyat al-Awliya notices mined into person records.** Abu Nu'aym's notices on Ibrahim ibn Adham (vol. 7, no. 394, PDF pp.367–395), Malik ibn Dinar (vol. 2, no. 200, pp.357–389), Ka'b al-Ahbar (vol. 5, no. 325, pp.364–391), Abu Sulayman al-Darani (vol. 9, no. 448, pp.254–280) and Sahl al-Tustari (vol. 10, no. 546, pp.190–226) gain trilingual "In Hilyat al-Awliya" sections with vol/page citations — Ibn Adham's leaving of the hunt, his lawful-earning years in Syria and his famous anecdotes; Malik ibn Dinar confirmed as the same person as the mushaf copyist of the Fihrist (Abu Yahya, d. 130 AH); Ka'b al-Ahbar's Torah-and-eschatology reports flagged as transmitted from the Books of the People of the Book; al-Darani's supplication heard by Dhu al-Nun al-Misri; and al-Tustari's six roots and marks of certainty. All draft-tier OCR-derived prose; ~600 notices remain. Run `microsd-books-b10`.
- **The friends of God get their introduction section: Hilyat's "neat" list mined into two concepts.** `concept/wali` and `concept/karamat-al-awliya` each gain a trilingual section from Abu Nu'aym's introduction (vol. 1, pp. 4–17): the sacred hadith on harming a friend of God, the groups he enumerates — the envied-by-prophets-and-martyrs, those sheltered in safety, the certainty that splits rocks, the century's forerunners, the hidden God-fearing, the just judges, the hasteners to rights — and Dhu al-Nun al-Misri's portrait of creation's elite. Reports are attributed to Abu Nu'aym's chains; draft-tier like the rest. Run `microsd-books-b11`.
- **Sufyan al-Thawri's enormous Hilyat notice mined across two volumes.** His record gains a trilingual "In Hilyat al-Awliya" section drawn from notice 387 — vol. 6 pp.356-393 and its continuation "بقية ترجة" in vol. 7 pp.3-144: the opening portrait and the testimonies of Ibn al-Mubarak, Shu'ba and Sufyan ibn Uyayna; his covenant-letter to Ubbad ibn Abbad; the Basra flight and the lineage adjuration before Ma'n ibn Za'ida; the Umm Hassan al-Asadiyya exchange; his definitions of zuhd, his grief at Abu Hanifa's death, his fainting at the Kaaba and tears at al-Fatiha; his explicit ordering of the imamate and his caution about al-Mahdi; and the deathbed purse and the unseen visitor at his grave. The hilyat source joins his record; draft-tier OCR-derived prose. Run `microsd-books-b13`.
- **Ahmad ibn Abi al-Hawari's Hilyat notice mined: the ascetic who threw his books into the sea.** His record gains a trilingual "In Hilyat al-Awliya" section from vol. 10, notice 457 (PDF pp.5–41): the two accounts of scattering his books — "you were a good guide; occupation with the guide after arrival is impossible" — the Jurayj exchange on denying oneself desires, the thirty years of seeking knowledge, the marks of love and contentment, and the traveller's stations from repentance to fear. The hilyat source is added to his record; draft-tier OCR-derived prose. Run `microsd-books-b12`.
- **Tradition-judge outputs stay out of git.** `.gitignore` now also covers `tradition-golden-results.jsonl` and `islamlab-match.jsonl`, matching the existing regenerable-artifact policy for packets and audit output; the files remain in the working tree for the calibration runs.
- **Omar Abdelkafy's Qissa wa Ibra gains episodes 9–12 — Solomon's ants, the mother of Moses, the sacrifice and the People of the Trench.** The Assabile lecture-series record `work/silsilat-qissa-wa-ebra` gains its episode 9–12 index sections in Arabic, English and Urdu: Solomon as the grateful wealthy king whose blessing is bound by gratitude, the ants' warning, the four birds' lament for the purpose of creation, an Umar anecdote on testing a would-be governor; the mother of Moses commanded to cast him and the bond placed on her heart; Ibrahim's dream and Ismail's obedience with Satan at the third stone-throwing; and Surat al-Buruj's sorcerer-boy, the crucifixion, the trench fire and the infant who spoke the testimony before the flames. Three entity records gain cited sections in all three languages — Solomon, the mother of Moses and Ibrahim — and the series gains three new `about` relations (Umar ibn al-Khattab, Uthman ibn Affan and Surat al-Buruj). Fragile transcript windows keep `needs_source` annotations rather than silent claims.
- **Omar Abdelkafy's Qissa wa Ibra gains episodes 13–15 — Ibrahim's four birds, the tongue, and the owners of the garden.** The Assabile lecture-series record `work/silsilat-qissa-wa-ebra` gains its episode 13–15 index sections in Arabic, English and Urdu: Ibrahim's question about giving life to the dead answered with four birds — the peacock, vulture, rooster and crow read as blameworthy traits to be slaughtered in the soul; the tongue's grave sins and the slander story told as a warning that the spoken word cannot be taken back, with the question "what have I presented to Islam?"; and the three brothers who inherited a garden in Sanaa, swore to withhold it from the poor, and watched it become like al-sarim while the poor came whispering. All claims carry episode-timestamp citations; entity enrichment for these episodes is queued for the next batch.
- **Omar Abdelkafy's Qissa wa Ibra gains episodes 16–19 — Moses in Midian, Jabir's trench, "every moist liver", and Pharaoh's drowning.** The Assabile lecture-series record `work/silsilat-qissa-wa-ebra` gains its episode 16–19 index sections in Arabic, English and Urdu: Moses' flight to Midian, the two women at the well and his marriage to Shu'ayb's daughter for service; Jabir's barley-and-sheep meal blessed by the Prophet's hand at the Trench, Abu Hanifa's counsel to a worker asking for less pay, and Ibn Mas'ud's prayer over the thief of his coins; the "every moist liver has a reward" hadith with the camel's complaint, stray-animal waqfs of early Islamic Egypt, the cat story and "no injustice today"; and Moses at the Red Sea — "my Lord is with me, He will guide me", the twelve bridges, Pharaoh's drowning, certainty in provision, the shepherdess and the wolf's cub, and Ali asleep under God's protection during the hijra. Seven new `about` relations link Jabir, Abu Hanifa, Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Hurayra, charity, and Surat al-Shu'ara. Fragile transcript windows keep `needs_source` annotations.
- **Omar Abdelkafy's Qissatuna wa-Ibrahimiya gains episodes 20–22 — completing the series.** The Assabile lecture-series record `work/silsilat-qissa-wa-ebra` gains its final three index sections in Arabic and English (Urdu translation still owed): the two brothers' khawatim, the companions of the cave and their five conditions, and Musa's question to al-Khidr on who is most learned, the three "I" statements, the kinds of knowledge, adab and tafakkur versus tadabbur. Six new `about` relations link the series to khawatim, the companions of the cave, Surat al-Kahf, al-Shafi'i, Abu Talib and knowledge.
- **TEI sweep continues through fiche 32800: fifteen more records link dated-inscription fiches.** The 28801–32800 range — dominated by Ottoman Balkans, Turkey and the eastern Mediterranean — yields verified links for the Alhambra's six remaining palace fiches (Mirador del Lindaraja, Sala de las Dos Hermanas and related Nasrid halls, fiches 28883–28963), Edirne's Üç Şerefeli (29368–29369) and Selimiye (29394) mosques' portal texts, and Kubadabad Palace's three Seljuk records (30597–30607). Damascus's Hanabila Mosque gains a 1202–1203 portal inscription (30213), Topkapı's Çinili Köşk a 1472–73 text (30497), Kırşehir's Ahi Evran zaviye-türbe its 1481–82 record (31694), Harput's Arap Baba mescidi its 1279–80 inscription (31306), Develi's Dev Ali türbe its 1203–04 tomb text (32258), Aleppo's al-Firdaws Madrasa its 1236–37 record (32783 — the entity is the Aleppo madrasa, not a namesake) and Antalya's Yivli Minare complex its two 1227–28 medrese texts (32401–32402). Hamza Bey's türbe in Bolu gains fiche 30437 for its 1462–63 türbe inscription. Dozens of namesakes were checked and rejected: Cairo's Bab al-Nasr is not the Aleppo or Damascus gates of the same name, the Meccan Maqam Ibrahim is not Aleppo's citadel shrine, Tunis's Sidi al-Ansari mosque is not the Aleppo-region mashhad of Sa'd al-Ansari, Tanta's Ahmad al-Badawi mosque is not the Damascus zawiya, Jerusalem's Tankiziyya is not Damascus's dar al-hadith, and the many "Mahmud", "Mehmed" and "Selçuk Hatun" tomb and mosque hits across Turkey and the Balkans were verified as different monuments.
- **TEI sweep continues through fiche 36800: twelve more records link dated-inscription fiches.** The 32801–36800 range — Turkish türbe country plus Afghanistan, Iran and the Syrian north — yields verified links for Istanbul's Süleymaniye Mosque (fiche 32831, 1558–59), three more texts for Antalya's Yivli Minare Seljuk medrese (33135, 35575, 35961 — the same complex as the 1227–28 pair), another Alhambra palace text from the Peinador de la Vega (33808, 1397–98), Erzurum's Çifte Minareli (Hâtuniye) Madrasa two records (33302–33304), and Amasya's Torumtay Tomb (32844). Five more Ottoman türbe drafts gain their dated inscriptions — Şeyh Bedreddin's tomb at Ilgın (32808), Şeyh Tennuri's at Kayseri (32928), Seyyid-i Şerif's at Develi (32836) and Seyyid Battal Gazi's mausoleum at Eskişehir (33444) — while Mashhad's Parizad Madrasa gains the Do Dar inscription of the Imam Reza complex (36001), Maragha's Diri Baba Mausoleum its 1402–03 text (36162) and Sari's Imamzadeh Abbas two records (36297–36301). Rejected namesakes include the Aleppo mashhads around Sa'd al-Ansari and the Sulṭāniyya (not the Tunis mosque or the Cairo mausoleum), the Harawi "Maqam Ibrahim" of Aleppo, the Gawhar Shad mosque of Herat (not the Jam Ghurid mausoleum), the Murad III kiosk of Topkapı (not a türbe), the Gaza "Hammam al-Samara" (not Samarra's Great Mosque), and the Imamzadeh Ismail shrines of Isfahan and Qumm.
- **TEI sweep continues through fiche 40800: three more records link dated-inscription fiches.** The 36801–40800 range — Ghazni, Herat, the Balkans, Fez and Cairo — yields Cairo's Bab Zuwayla gate its own construction text (fiche 38857, 1092–93), the Sayyida Nafisa shrine its two medieval mausoleum revetment inscriptions (39651, 39653, 1227–28 — correctly routed to the Cairo shrine, not the Baghdad bimaristan namesake) and the Alhambra's Patio del Mexuar a Nasrid palace text (40515, 1397–98). Rejected namesakes: inscriptions found in Masud III's Ghazni palace do not attest his minaret, Herat's Gawhar Shad congregational mosque is not the Jam Ghurid mausoleum, the Turkmenistan mausoleum of the mystic Luqman is not the Levantine fort of the same name, the Siberian "Tobolsk" finds are not the Tobolsk mosque, and Skopje's Mehmed Bey mosque and Fatih bridge are not Ottoman tombs.
- **Qissatuna wa-Ibrahimiya's closing episodes gain their Urdu sections.** The Assabile lecture-series record `work/silsilat-qissa-wa-ebra` now carries episodes 20–22 in all three languages — the two brothers' khawatim, the companions of the cave, and Musa's question to al-Khidr — completing the trilingual set for the whole 22-episode series.
- **TEI sweep continues through fiche 44800: the Alhambra's Nasrid palace inscriptions land in bulk, plus six new draft monuments.** The 40801–44800 range — dominated by an Istanbul roll-call of person-named mosques, fountains and baths — adds forty-nine palace fiches to the Alhambra (the Partal oratory, the Mexuar suite, the Comares façade and courtyards, the whole Lions-palace set from the Mocarabes room to the Lindaraja mirador, the Infantas tower and the former San Francisco convent site, 1348–1418 CE), a Meccan Maqam Ibrahim restoration text (43022), Toledo's Bab al-Mardum mosque-turned-Cristo de la Luz (42962) and Tunis's Zaytuna a 1583–84 record (41806). Six harvest leads become draft entities: Edirne's Gülbahar Hatun and Selçuk Hatun mescidi (1451–52, 1455–56), Bursa's Şehzade Mahmud Türbesi in the Muradiye complex (1506–08), the Mashhad of Sa'd al-Anṣārī in Aleppo's countryside (six Mamluk-era fiches, 1347–1513), Damascus's Zawiya of Ahmad al-Badawi (1493–94) and Yambol's Sofular Mosque (1481–82); Stara Zagora's Old Mosque — already identified as Hamza Bey's — gains its 1408–09 portal text. Dozens of Istanbul namesakes were rejected: "Mahmud", "Mehmed", "Yahya Efendi" and "Ali Efendi" mosques, fountains, hamams and mescidi matched to unrelated tomb entities, plus palace-versus-minaret and mosque-versus-türbe kind mismatches across the Balkans.
- **TEI sweep continues through fiche 48800: seven more Qarawiyyin architectural texts and a Hayrabolu mosque record.** The 44801–48800 range — Fez's Qarawiyyin cluster plus the last Istanbul namesakes — adds seven dated inscriptions to the Qarawiyyin Mosque itself (the west pavilion of the courtyard, the mosque pavilion, the dome before Bab al-Ward, the khatib's prayer hall and the great Bab al-Shammā'īn lustres, 1205–1437 CE), while Güzelce Hasan Bey Mosque at Hayrabolu gains a 1499–1500 text on the mosque built for a son-in-law of Bayezid I in 1406. Rejected: the Edirne Selim II mosque object, the Crimea Abdurrahman Bey mosque, Sokullu Mehmed Paşa's medrese and mosque, the Bosnia church-turned-mosque and another Masud III palace-versus-minaret case.
- **TEI sweep passes fiche 52,800 — the halfway milestone of the epigraphy catalogue.** The final 48,801–52,800 range closes this thread's sweep: Istanbul's Şehzade Mosque gains its külliye inscription (49226, 1548–49), Cairo's Madrasa of al-Nāṣir Muḥammad a wooden entrance-door text (50259, 1303–04) and the al-Ghawri madrasa-mausoleum complex two more texts from its Ghawriyya wing between the Moski and Bab Zuwayla (50914–50915, 1511–12). Namesakes rejected include Yashbak's mausoleum versus his palace, the Konya Eşrefoğlu Mosque versus the Beyşehir entity, caravanserais misread as the Aksaray mausoleum, and a Meccan imaret misread as Murad III's türbe.
- **Qissa wa Ibra's remaining entities gain their Omar Abdelkafy sections.** With the series' twenty-two episodes complete, the five Assabile records that episodes 2–20 touch but had never cited the series now carry cited sections in all three languages: Jabir ibn Abdullah (the Trench meal blessed in his house), charity (the seventy-devils obstacle, secret giving, lawful hidden wealth, and the hadith of the raised charity), khawatim (the two brothers whose word decided Paradise and Fire, and the sorcerers' last prostration), Maryam (the palm-trunk miracle and the Lord of causes preparing causes), and Uthman ibn Affan (named among the righteous who stood firm until death). Every claim carries an episode-timestamp citation to `source/assabile-omar-abdelkafy`.
- **A new Omar Abdelkafy lecture series opens: excerpts from the Prophet's life.** `work/muktatafat-mena-al-seera` — twenty-four recorded lessons in the Assabile archive — now has its record in Arabic, English and Urdu, opening with episode one's introduction: the return to Monday lessons after years away, the series outline (pre-Islamic Arabia, the mission, the hijra and the founding of the state, the conquests), the question of why Arabia was chosen, the pre-Islamic Arab character of generosity and honour, and an allusion to the episode of Ta'if. Six `about` relations link the Prophet, Abu Talib, Khadija, Salah al-Din, the sira and generosity. The opening episode's transcript is heavily garbled in places, so fragile windows carry `needs_source` annotations rather than silent claims; episodes 2–24 follow in later batches.
- **Muktatafat min al-Sira gains episode two — the world into which the Prophet was born.** The new Assabile series record gains its second episode in all three languages: Quraysh, Mecca and the Kaaba, Abd al-Muttalib's raising of the Prophet's father Abdullah, the year of the elephant and Abraha's failed attack, the father's death before the birth and Amina's vows, the monk Bahira's recognition of the sign of prophethood, Salman al-Farisi's search for the true religion, the pre-Islamic Arab month names, and the return to why the Arabs were chosen. Four new `about` relations link Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, Amina bint Wahb, Salman al-Farisi and Bahira; the heavily garbled transcript keeps `needs_source` annotations throughout.
- **Muktatafat min al-Sira gains episode three — the Prophet's qualities and the series plan.** The Assabile lecture-series record gains its third episode in Arabic, English and Urdu: a talk on the three kinds of inheritance — background, character and general or particular — then the Prophet's physical description as the sira books record it (stature, black hair, the straight nose, fair complexion, smooth cheeks, long fingers, soft feet), his honours as a mercy to the worlds, and the announced plan of the series from his birth through the Meccan period — his grandfather's care, his mother Amina's death, his uncle Abu Talib's guardianship, his marriage to Khadija, Zayd ibn Haritha's marriage and parting, and the return to Mecca before the hijra. One new `about` relation links Zayd ibn Haritha; the heavily garbled transcript keeps `needs_source` annotations throughout.
- **Muktatafat min al-Sira gains episode four — lessons and counsel.** The Assabile lecture-series record gains its fourth episode in all three languages: hadiths on the umma's protection ("my umma will not perish by famine"), difference among Muslims read as a law of creation rather than despair, da'wa by wisdom and goodly exhortation; conquest-era positions of the Companions — Abu Hurayra and Khalid ibn al-Walid entering Damascus — and the unity of what they agreed upon (tawhid, prayer, Ramadan, hajj, zakat); family and educational counsel (a righteous wife for one's son, parents' rights, patience with a spouse, aqeeqa and circumcision, keeping spousal secrets, screens in the home); and a closing fiqh Q&A (the manner of istikhara, making up a parent's missed prayers, divorce rulings, removing nail polish for wudu). Seven new `about` relations link Abu Hurayra, Khalid ibn al-Walid, Umar ibn al-Khattab, da'wa, keeping secrets, istikhara and brotherhood; the heavily garbled transcript keeps `needs_source` annotations throughout.
- **Muktatafat min al-Sira gains episode five — lessons from the Prophetic hadiths.** The Assabile lecture-series record gains its fifth episode in all three languages: the merit of gatherings of knowledge and the woman who dragged her child toward the Fire ("is not Allah more merciful to His servants than I am to my child?"); the man who worked the deeds of Paradise's people until an arm's length remained, and the man shown every blessing then cast down; Umar's vigil in the Prophet's mosque and the rule that whoever aids in wrong will be opposed; a qudsi hadith on who enters the Fire, the three pillars of iman, "I am the city of knowledge and Ali is its gate", and the scale on which la ilaha illa Allah outweighs the heavens and the earth; Companion stories including Abu Bakr and Umar offering Hafsa, and a closing question session on marriage and hijab. Six new `about` relations link gatherings of knowledge, Paradise, iman, hadith qudsi, Abu Bakr and Hafsa; the heavily garbled transcript keeps `needs_source` annotations throughout.
- **Muktatafat min al-Sira gains episode six — the Prophet's upbringing and his marriage.** The Assabile lecture-series record gains its sixth episode in all three languages: the mawlid night coinciding with the Muslims' suffering and a survey of Western designs, historical distortions and economic claims about the Islamic world; the Prophet's upbringing among Banu Sa'd under the foster mother Halima al-Sa'diyya — pure Arabic eloquence and the Bedouin dialect, ummi, named Muhammad the Trustworthy — and the rebuttal of claims he learned from the People of the Book; his foster household's care ("I see Muhammad as the blessing"), learning archery, swimming and riding; his return to Mecca, his mother Amina's death and his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib's guardianship; and Khadija's proposal with Abu Talib's marriage plan. Four new `about` relations link Halima al-Sa'diyya, Abd al-Muttalib, Ali ibn Abi Talib and revelation; the heavily garbled transcript keeps `needs_source` annotations throughout.
- **Muktatafat min al-Sira gains episode seven — the Kaaba, Fatima and Ali.** The Assabile lecture-series record gains its seventh episode in all three languages: the Muslim's adab of gaze and the saying "a man of action among a thousand is better than a thousand men of words"; the knight who fell before Ali and the sword of Banu Ghaifar given to Khalid ibn al-Walid; Islam's transformation of the Arabs into loving brothers and Khalid's stance toward the truce; the rebuilding of the Kaaba and the placing of the Black Stone by Muhammad the Trustworthy; Quraysh's persecution of Fatima and her sisters; Abu Talib's death; Umar's refusal and Ali's acceptance in the proposal; and the wedding feast with Ali's sermon and the urging of kinship ties. Eight new `about` relations link Fatima, Umm Kulthum, Zaynab and Ruqayya (the Prophet's daughters), al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, the Black Stone, the Kaaba's rebuilding and the Hudaybiyya truce; the heavily garbled transcript keeps `needs_source` annotations throughout.
- **Muktatafat min al-Sira gains episode eight — the life of Ibrahim.** The Assabile lecture-series record gains its eighth episode in all three languages: a recap of Fatima and Ali's four children and Khadija's role before the mission; the life of Ibrahim — "Ibrahim who fulfilled", a hanif Muslim neither Jew nor Christian, his trials the greatest of trials paralleling the Prophet's, the comparison of his message with the Prophet's in the hadith of the man who built a house, and the Kaaba's rebuilding in his time; his upbringing in Iraq, migration to Egypt and Syria in famine, death at eighty-six, and wisdom in trusting God's choice; and the beginning of the story of Hajar and Ismail. Five new `about` relations link Ibrahim, Ismail, Hajar, Hasan ibn Ali and Husayn ibn Ali; the heavily garbled transcript keeps `needs_source` annotations throughout.
- **Muktatafat min al-Sira gains episode nine — the fruit of knowledge and scenes of revelation.** The Assabile lecture-series record gains its ninth episode in all three languages: the announced move to the descent of revelation; knowledge that must bear fruit in three treatises — between spouses, parents and children, and fellow Muslims — lest it become a proof against the scholar; supplication and its fruits ("worries and debts froze in my Lord's hand"), the wronged man's complaint and the hadith on supplicating against a wrongdoer; the scholars' adab toward rulers (Sufyan al-Thawri, Ahmad ibn Hanbal); and closing narrations of dreams and Gabriel's address to the Prophet. Seven new `about` relations link knowledge, supplication, Sufyan al-Thawri, Harun al-Rashid, Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, Gabriel and Ahmad ibn Hanbal; the heavily garbled transcript keeps `needs_source` annotations throughout.
- **Muktatafat min al-Sira gains episode ten — unity and questions of married life.** The Assabile lecture-series record gains its tenth episode in all three languages: "lesson eleven" on the question of unity — a heart whose concern is unified on God rather than on provision, wife and trade; knowledge as the door to God in this world and the next ("whoever wants the world, the hereafter, or both — let him take to knowledge"), the Prophet's welcome of knowledge-seekers, and descriptions of the early generations; fiqh questions on married life — the couple's dispute before the Prophet over maintenance, "we were created from a crooked rib", the wife as the greatest blessing after faith, the wife's work and the days of menstruation; Prophetic reports narrated by Aisha (the Prophet's wish that Paradise be given to whoever asks); sira reports including Abu Sufyan and the conquest of Mecca; and a closing summary of the major signs of the Hour from the two Sahihs — the sun rising from the west, the Beast, the Smoke, Gog and Magog, and the descent of Isa. Nine new `about` relations link Aisha, Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, the hereafter, the mosque, the moon's splitting, the signs of the Hour, Isa ibn Maryam, the end of time and khums; the heavily garbled transcript keeps `needs_source` annotations throughout.
- **Muktatafat min al-Sira gains episode eleven — the umma's glad tidings and reports of the Companions.** The Assabile lecture-series record gains its eleventh episode in all three languages: the umma's glad tidings ("give this umma the good news of joy and right guidance", the hadith of the best umma as narrated by Ibn Abbas in Sahih Muslim); Abu Bakr's station — "the first to be shaken from his grave on the Day of Judgment is your Prophet, then Abu Bakr" — and Gabriel's question about the umma's condition; the man who received revelation alone on the mountain; the shepherds' parable for communal solidarity and counsel to take knowledge from different shaykhs; wealth not changing character and travelling in search of knowledge; the first migration to Abyssinia with Uthman and Ruqayya; reports of Quraysh's boycott of Banu Hashim, the Negus's words about Isa and Maryam, the Isra and Mi'raj, and the Prophet's return to Mecca and Khadija's death. Seven new `about` relations link the Negus, Uthman ibn Affan, the two Abyssinian migrations, the Isra and Mi'raj, Ibn Abbas and Mus'ab ibn Umayr; the heavily garbled transcript keeps `needs_source` annotations throughout.
- **Muktatafat min al-Sira gains episode twelve — Ta'if, the year of sorrow and the Isra and Mi'raj.** The Assabile lecture-series record gains its twelfth episode in all three languages: the announced three topics — the Prophet's journey to Ta'if and return to Mecca, the year of sorrow (the deaths of Abu Talib and Khadija), and the Isra and Mi'raj; long sermons on the struggle between truth and falsehood through history — patience, refusal to despair, bearing relief upon blessing, examples from the prophets (Noah and his wife); reports of polytheists and believers including Umm Jamil, wife of Abu Lahab; part of the story of those who worshipped falsehood then believed; an anecdote of Abu Hanifa on faith in the Qur'an; and instruction on prayer — the takbir, the opening supplication and the invocations. Six new `about` relations link the journey to Ta'if, the year of sorrow, Noah, Umm Jamil, Abu Lahab and Abu Hanifa; the heavily garbled transcript keeps `needs_source` annotations throughout.
- **Muktatafat min al-Sira gains episode thirteen — prayer and its conditions, then a sermon on the family.** The Assabile lecture-series record gains its thirteenth episode in all three languages: the session devoted to prayer as the bulwark of religion; the conditions of prayer's validity — purity of body, clothes and place, the kinds of impurity and wudu; Islam as a chain ending in divorce and the hadith distinguishing a servant from polytheism through abandoning the prayer; covering the Muslims and their private parts and looking with good opinion; long chapters of fiqh and adab — gentleness in judgement, an anecdote of al-Hasan al-Basri, counsel on the tongue and reading, the story of Abu Hurayfa in prayer; hearts — the sound and the dead — and closing with a sermon on the Muslim family, the righteous wife, recitation of the marriage contract's pillars and supplication. Seven new `about` relations link purity, wudu, impurity, prayer's conditions, al-Hasan al-Basri, marriage and the khutba; the heavily garbled transcript keeps `needs_source` annotations throughout.
- **Muktatafat min al-Sira gains episode fourteen — a minimal entry for a near-unintelligible recording.** The Assabile lecture-series record gains its fourteenth episode in all three languages, kept deliberately short: the transcript is almost entirely garbled speech-recognition noise, so the entry records only what can be said with confidence — the session continues the chapters of purity and prayer ("whoever establishes the prayer establishes the religion"), presents the attendees' fiqh and madhhab questions with an anecdote of Abu Hanifa and al-Shafi'i, returns to the kinds of purity, and closes with supplication. Every bullet carries `needs_source` annotations and no new `about` relations were added, since nothing in the recording supports a specific entity link.
- **Muktatafat min al-Sira gains episode fifteen — sincerity and following, then back to the pillars of prayer.** The Assabile lecture-series record gains its fifteenth episode in all three languages: the handhold of Islam is prayer; al-Hasan al-Basri's maid left in the market without God's remembrance and the verse on wine and gambling; a letter to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz about drinkers and the scholars' saying on one present at sin who disapproves in heart; sincerity and intentions with Musa's accepted charity; honouring the elderly — the shaykh as worship and God's mercy — and Ibn Abbas with Zayd ibn Ali; the four categories combining ikhlas and mutaba'a with the report "the best of people is good to them"; Umar ibn al-Khattab's night vigil at the Prophet's door and weeping at the hadith of Paradise by mercy; a report on that year's pilgrims with reservation; supplication adab and Umar at the Kaaba; Harun al-Rashid asking Imam Malik for private teaching and being refused; then a return to the pillars of prayer — intention, the meaning of "God is greater", the Prophet's prayer at Umm Salama's house and the vision of the gates of Paradise and Fire — patience and the food of Paradise, and fiqh answers on wudu from a vessel, ghusl reaching the scalp, and a promised handout on menstruation rulings. Thirteen new `about` relations link ikhlas, intention, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, wine, Musa, Zayd ibn Ali, Umm Salama, David, Imam Malik, ghusl from janaba, hajj, patience and prayer; the unevenly garbled transcript keeps `needs_source` annotations on its uncertain passages.
- **Muktatafat min al-Sira gains episode sixteen — signs of divine enablement, then the pillars of prayer and fiqh.** The Assabile lecture-series record gains its sixteenth episode in all three languages: whoever enters a town of Islam knows Islam only through prayer; the state of the cities — mixing, lowered voices, the fading of modesty; the signs of tawfiq in worship — the heaviness of obedience and the lightness of sin, the market anecdote of declining trust, "whoever sins while laughing", the soul's love of sin and "the truth is heavy"; good character — humility, smiling, greeting those known — and al-Hasan al-Basri's parable of the believer as a bee; visiting the sick, the sweet scent of the righteous, and an anecdote attributed to al-Shafi'i; the first cause of lacking tawfiq and reports on wealth and poverty before God; the kinds of pride as lying and the costliness of knowledge; following the righteous with Abu Bakr as model, and a digression on clerical mediation in confession; the world running after us while the hereafter comes upon us; then a return to the pillars of prayer in detail — intention in the heart, takbir, standing, bowing with palms on knees, "God hears whoever praises Him", prostration and the testimony — and fiqh answers on tayammum (striking clean earth, wiping to the wrists, janaba lifted only by ghusl or tayammum), water, menstruation and the ends of Ramadan. Seven new `about` relations link tayammum, modesty, al-Shafi'i, divine enablement and misguidance, Ramadan fasting, pride and delusion; the unevenly garbled transcript keeps `needs_source` annotations on its uncertain passages.
- **Muktatafat min al-Sira gains episode seventeen — "what would the Messenger do in my place", then the prayer in detail.** The Assabile lecture-series record gains its seventeenth episode in all three languages: the opening principle of asking in every act what the Messenger would do; digressions into anecdotes — "who will judge us? God — my Lord", tales of "in the name of God" and encounters with Ali, talk of filial piety and long life, and a mixed-society discussion with an anecdote attributed to al-Jahiz; then a return to prayer — raising the hands at the opening takbir as a confirmed sunna agreed by about fifty Companions including the ten promised Paradise; the Prophet's length in qunoot and witr (sixty to a hundred ayat, sometimes sura al-A'raf at Maghrib) and Ibn Umar's stance with Umar ibn Uthman; the bowing "subhana rabbi al-'azim" and the rising "God hears whoever praises Him"; prostration on seven limbs — forehead and nose, palms, knees, toes; and the testimony with the greetings, the two testimonies and the Ibrahimic blessing; closing with the attendees' prayer and fiqh questions including marriage schools and kin-marriage rulings. Three new `about` relations link raising the hands in prayer, Ibn Umar and the mahram rules; the unevenly garbled transcript keeps `needs_source` annotations on its uncertain passages.
- **Muktatafat min al-Sira gains episode eighteen — approaching God, then the night prayers.** The Assabile lecture-series record gains its eighteenth episode in all three languages: the fruit of knowledge is acting on it; the discourse on "approaching God" — repentance as the first word of the entrant, hearts as vessels and sincerity of intention; the Bedouin's question "who will judge us? God — my Lord" and the generous one's forgiveness; the four categories of knowledge; the five conditions of supplication; the hadith of Habib al-Najjar and the Prophet's "may God have mercy on Habib al-Najjar"; "the nearest a servant comes to his Lord is while prostrating"; the Qur'an as light — "an argument for you or against you"; and the night prayers in detail — what the Prophet did before Fajr per Aisha's hadith, the length of witr, and discussion of rak'a counts; closing with prayer and fiqh questions on marriage, the waiting period and other matters. Two new `about` relations link repentance and night prayer; the unevenly garbled transcript keeps `needs_source` annotations on its uncertain passages.
- **Muktatafat min al-Sira gains episode nineteen — prayer as a pillar, then God's love, trust, and intercession.** The Assabile lecture-series record gains its nineteenth episode in all three languages: prayer presented as the second pillar of Islam and the first thing the servant is asked on the Day of Resurrection, with a long supplication for Muslims everywhere; a hadith narrated from Ibn Abbas (Ahmad, Ibn Majah among the transmitters) on remaining upon the clear path; answers held cautiously on killing one who seizes wealth or honor, and on Abu Dharr's question about scholars and travelers increasing; the hadith that God sends destruction by removing the soul, the hadith qudsi of God's beloved servant made beloved to Ibrahim and Jibril; trust (amanah) as word, lifetime, spouse, children, neighbor, home and work; the scene of intercession on the Day of Resurrection with the prophets' plea; the presentation of deeds; and a return to the prayer sunnas — the funeral prayer, the two Eid prayers, raising the hands in takbir, and stillness in bowing and prostration. Five new `about` relations link trust, intercession, the funeral prayer and both Eid festivals; the unevenly garbled transcript keeps `needs_source` annotations on its uncertain passages.
- **Muktatafat min al-Sira gains episode twenty — stories from the Prophet's life, then prayer fiqh.** The Assabile lecture-series record gains its twentieth episode in all three languages: more sira stories — hearts that longed for the Prophet's return, the call among a few Companions with the saying about the sun and moon, the hadith of the three men who kept night vigil, the Bedouin's question and the stray she-camel, household stories touching Fatima and Umar's positions in Medina, a Palestine anecdote and the search for Umar; trial explained as trade with God; then a return to prayer details — a man seen tying a cord while praying told prayer comes first, the gaze between the feet, the Prophet's mounts, and closing fiqh on the verse of seeking forgiveness and Abu Hanifa's and Abu Yusuf's words on speech and yawning inside prayer. One new `about` relation links Abu Yusuf al-Qadi; the unevenly garbled transcript keeps `needs_source` annotations on its uncertain passages.
- **Muktatafat min al-Sira gains episode twenty-one — the Friday sermon and its rulings, then the funeral rites.** The Assabile lecture-series record gains its twenty-first episode in all three languages: hadiths on the tongue — 'speak good or keep silent', using one's time in what is required, tomorrow and provision; 'Lord of the worlds' as Lord of all worlds; 'the dearest deeds are the most constant', being in this world as the Prophet's companions were, and Islam returning as it began strange; then the Friday subject — the sermon menu, the preacher anecdote, the sermon's conditions (Qur'an recitation, enjoining good and forbidding evil, sincerity), hadiths on Friday's merit (the answered hour, its pre-Islam name, neglect of the prayer leading to Hell), angels not cursing the Friday traveller without necessity, all creation expecting the Hour on Friday, and the sale prohibition between the two adhans; digressions into walking in the mosque, funeral accompaniment, and Abu Bakr anecdotes; then death — the soul's departure, the dying person's testimonies, hope for the sick; and washing the dead, funeral accompaniment, three days of mourning, and the grave in Paradise. One new `about` relation links the Friday prayer; the unevenly garbled transcript keeps `needs_source` annotations on its uncertain passages.
- **Muktatafat min al-Sira gains episode twenty-two — knowledge circles and their etiquette, then Umar's life.** The Assabile lecture-series record gains its twenty-second episode in all three languages: circles of knowledge as the Muslim's best provision for the hereafter with their general etiquette; 'every fatwa has its context' and every ailment having its remedy — the Prophet prescribing to each questioner what suited his state; degrees of nearness and serving God; a fragment of Umar ibn al-Khattab's story — his entrance and his charge over Quraysh's delegation; Chosroes calling the Prophet 'king of the Arabs'; Umar's justice — 'our ancestors made justice secure among them, so do not say, Umar'; the closing principle that Islam spreads by noble character and example, not by lectures; dreams and their interpretation, including Abu Hanifa's youthful dream of the Prophet's grave; building mosques and mention of Abdullah ibn Auf; and the etiquette of reciting the Qur'an — completing the mushaf in three nights. The heavily garbled transcript keeps `needs_source` annotations throughout; all named figures were already linked, so no new relations were added.
- **Muktatafat min al-Sira gains episode twenty-three — Abu Dharr's hadith on the wonders of this world.** The Assabile lecture-series record gains its twenty-third episode in all three languages: the closing supplication and announcement of the series' final lessons, Abu Dharr's question about the Prophet's 'market' in Mecca before the message, and the famous hadith of the four wonders — marveling at one certain of death yet rejoicing, of the reckoning yet laughing, of decree yet shaking his hands, of Paradise and Hell yet heedless. Two new `about` relations link death and divine decree; the short opening transcript keeps `needs_source` annotations.
- **Muktatafat min al-Sira gains episode twenty-four — the closing lesson on the effect of good deeds.** The Assabile lecture-series record gains its twenty-fourth and final episode in all three languages: the closing lesson 'the third and final' on the effect of righteous deeds on their doer; faith as the greatest blessing; humility and adab anecdotes; Qur'anic and hadith fragments on believers' description and the merit of mosques; dreams and saintly marvels in the manner of these gatherings; a critical discussion of sorcery and the evil eye; and scattered modern passages — advertisements and news — noted as outside the lesson's content; closing with praise and supplication for the Muslims. The heavily garbled transcript keeps `needs_source` annotations throughout; all named figures were already linked, so no new relations were added. The series is now complete through all twenty-four episodes.
- **A new Omar Abdelkafy lecture series opens: the servants of the Most Merciful in Ramadan.** `work/silsilat-ebadu-al-rahman` — a planned twenty-eight daily lessons — now has its record in Arabic, English and Urdu, opening with episode one: supplication at the month's start, the daily program announcement, the nine attributes of 'the servants of the Most Merciful' in Surat al-Furqan, this world as an abode of trial (Qarun, the man of the two gardens), renewed intention, humility before all people, and a practical Ramadan program — taraweeh, home Qur'an recitation, reconciliation, and making up accumulated fasts. Episode two begins the attributes with humility: the one blessing never envied, pride's ruin, kindness to parents, 'you reap what you sow', clean money, humility toward kin and scholars, the Prophet serving his guests, stories of the caliphs' humility, and humility toward the weak. Five `about` relations link Surat al-Furqan, humility, Muslim brotherhood, taraweeh and Ramadan fasting; the unevenly garbled transcript keeps `needs_source` annotations.
- **Fix: geo-enrichment leftovers repaired in the tour stops.** The person-and-place geo-enrichment merge wrote `founded.edtf` as a bare number (`0638`) on the Kufa record, and added `source/wikidata`/`source/nomisma` to the Medina, Cordoba and Duranir records without updating the 3D tour stops' source lists — all of these failed the gates on every branch until now. The EDTF value is now the string `"0638"` with the same year precision and sources, and every affected stop lists the same sources as its record. No content changes.
- **TEI sweep continues through fiche 56,800: the al-Ghawri complex gains six more texts and Cairo's al-Mu'ayyad mosque three.** The 52,801–56,800 range — Cairo's mosque belt and Fez — routes nine inscriptions the matcher first tied to nearby Bab Zuwayla to their true monuments: six dated texts (1503–04) for the Madrasa Ġawriyya between the Moski and the gate now enrich the al-Ghawri madrasa-mausoleum complex, and three (1420–21) enrich Sultan al-Mu'ayyad's mosque just north-west of the gate. The Alhambra gains another palace text from the Peinador (1390–91) and the Qarawiyyin its two great gates, Bāb al-Ḫulafā' and Bāb al-Ward (1136–37). Rejected: the Hasankeyf mausoleum of Zaynal ibn Uzun Hasan (not the Tabriz türbe of his father), a Mardin pavilion, the Ramla Shaykh Mahmud mosque and an Edirne chandelier of uncertain provenance. Separately, Nomisma.org — the American Numismatic Society's linked-open-data coin ontology — passed the eight-criteria source-family score and is queued for registration.

- **The Thesaurus d'Épigraphie Islamique sweep is complete — every fiche through 61,517 has been harvested, matched and verified.** The 56,801–60,800 tail adds three more palace texts to the Alhambra (1300–01 and 1494–95), and probing past 60,800 revealed the catalogue's true end: fiches above 61,517 parse as empty placeholders, so the final 717-fiche range (60,801–61,517) closed the sweep with zero new matches. Across the whole run the lane has linked dated-inscription evidence to buildings, tombs, gates and objects from al-Andalus to Central Asia — and documented hundreds of namesake rejections so no wrong monument was ever cited.
- **Nomisma.org's first harvest lands: ten city records now carry their numismatic identity.** The newly registered numismatic ontology (CC-BY 3.0, `{cite:nomisma <id>}`) begins corroborating the place backlog — Damascus, Cairo, Baghdad, Kufa, Samarra, Isfahan, Nishapur, Merv, Qazvin and Rayy each gain their stable mint-concept id after the mint's own definition was verified as the same city. Coins are primary evidence for mint towns, issuing authorities and regnal dates; this is the first step toward the coin object class the graph has only just begun to cover.
- **The Nomisma mint map spreads across the Islamicate world: 63 more city records gain their numismatic identity.** Following the first ten, the mint↔place pass now links sixty-three further cities — from Tyre, Susa and Emesa's neighbours to Córdoba, Seville, Marrakech, Palermo and Granada in al-Andalus; Kairouan, Tunis, Ceuta and Sijilmasa's sphere; Baghdad's orbit through Wasit, Hillah and Surraq; the Iranian plateau from Istakhr to Kirman, Hamadhan and Qumm; the eastern reaches at Kabul, Ghazna, Zaranj, Balkh and Bukhara — each cited by its stable `nomisma.org/id/` mint concept after the definition was verified as the same city. City mints are among the hardest primary evidence for urban continuity across the whole Islamic millennium.
- **ANS MANTIS registered as a trusted coin-catalogue source — the missing object class gets its evidence backbone.** The American Numismatic Society's collection database (~98,000 coin objects, about 60,672 in the Islamic department) joins the citation families at Tier 1, facts-only (`source/ans-mantis`, decision `dec-20261109-226`): stable accession ids resolvable as `{cite:ans-mantis <accession-id>}` for denomination, mint, issuing authority, Hijri and CE dates and weight — the object-level counterpart of Nomisma's vocabulary. Data is openly licensed (ODbL; images Public Domain Mark), so citation carries attribution while bulk structured ingestion waits on a separate share-alike review; catalogue prose, legend text and images are never republished. The decision engine's outreach gate misfired on "denominations" containing the substring "nomination" — the fourth recorded instance of substring false-positives in rule keywords, overridden with the correct ruling.
- **Nomisma's issuer pass lands: seventy-seven records gain numismatic authority links.** The mint map's natural next step — matching Nomisma's issuing-authority concepts to the graph's own entities, each verified against the concept's own definition before linking (`source/nomisma` in `sources`, the concept id in `external_ids.nomisma`): sixteen polity records gain their dynasty authority (the Umayyad, Abbasid, Samanid, Aghlabid, Fatimid, Almoravid, Almohad, Ayyubid, Bahri, Burji, Mamluk, Ottoman, Safavid, Ghaznavid and Muhammad Ali polities, plus Umayyad Córdoba); fifty-nine person records gain their coin-issuing ruler identity — from the first Abbasid caliph's circle (al-Mansur, al-Amin, al-Mu'tazz, al-Muttaqi, al-Nasir and al-Zahir bi-Amr Allah), the Fatimid and Ubaydid line (al-Qa'im, al-Mu'izz, al-Mansur, al-Aziz, al-Hakim's successors, al-Musta'li, al-Mustansir, al-Zafir, al-Amir and al-Adid), the Ayyubid sultans (al-Adil I and II, Salamish, al-Kamil, al-Salih Isma'il, al-Malik al-Aziz and Turanshah IV), Tulunid and Ikhshidid founders, the Córdoba emirs and caliphs (Abd al-Rahman II and III, Hisham I, al-Hakam I and II, Sulayman al-Musta'in), the Ghaznavid, Seljuk and Marinid-adjacent rulers, the Jalayirid Ahmad ibn Uways, the Mamluk sultans (Qutuz, Faraj, Jaqmaq, Inal, al-Mansur Uthman, al-Mansur Ali and al-Nasir Muhammad), the Moroccan Alawids (Hassan I) and the Ottoman line from Bayezid I through Mehmed V and Abdülaziz. Two coin objects — the V&A's Andalusī dirham and the Umm Hajara hoard — gain their denomination and issuer concept ids. Namesakes were rejected by definition check throughout: Morocco's Muhammad III and IV are not the Hafsid caliph, Abd al-Rahman's Moroccan namesake is not the Córdoba emir, and Nomisma's Murad III is the Ottoman sultan, never the Tunisian Bey.
- **Source-family scouting round: three coin/art candidates assessed and deferred, none registered.** The web-sources lane probed the next explore-list families: Tübingen's Sylloge Nummorum Arabicorum online catalogue (authority excellent — the reference series for Islamic coin types — but the live site is currently broken on both its hosts and only ~444 objects are online, the real corpus being the copyrighted print volumes, so it is deferred until the catalogue is reachable); the Fitzwilliam Museum (its open collection-data API host is unreachable from the harvest network today, so its licence and structure stay unverified); and the Ashmolean (its collections-online interface loads but no licence statement is visible, so it needs a proper API and terms check before scoring). All three are recorded in the lane's delegation ledger with revisit conditions; nothing was registered or cited.
- **Person/place geo-enrichment consolidated across three parallel runs.** The consolidated output of three enrichment batches now lands on the graph: ~10,000 person records gain cited `born_in`, `died_in` and `lived_in` map-relevant edges (mostly from recorded Wikidata revisions, each flagged medium-confidence for corroboration), 1,440+ new place records join the atlas — world cities, historical regions, arrondissements and caliphate entities — and existing places gain coordinates and gazetteer ids. `event/mamun-egypt-entry` and the time-browser media index are retargeted to the canonical place ids, two sources are registered (`source/cgie-encyclopaedia`, `source/tarajm-com`), and duplicate records written by the parallel runs were semantically merged. Enrichment reports are under `docs/reports/person-place-geo-*.md`; the remaining unmatched place names are logged in `docs/reports/unresolved-person-places.txt`.
- **iDAI.gazetteer registered as a trusted place-gazetteer source — and its first twelve cities linked.** The German Archaeological Institute's ancient-world gazetteer joins the citation families at Tier 2 (`source/idai-gazetteer`, decision `dec-20261109-228`): stable `gazetteer.dainst.org/place/<gazId>` URIs, CC-BY 4.0 content licence, unauthenticated JSON endpoints (`search.json`, `doc/<gazId>.json`), multilingual names including Arabic, and owl:sameAs links to the Pleiades/GeoNames identifiers the museum already carries. Cited as `{cite:idai-gazetteer <gazId>}` for place-identity facts — types, coordinates, alternate names, hierarchy; editorial text never republished. First pilot: twelve major cities gain their gazetteer id after per-record verification — Damascus, Aleppo, Cairo, Córdoba, Fez, Istanbul, Qayrawan, Marrakesh, Mecca, Medina, Tunis and Baghdad — each record's gazetteer entry checked for name, coordinates and Arabic-name match before linking.
- **The iDAI.gazetteer link spreads to thirty-four cities.** A second verified batch adds gazetteer ids to twenty-two more place records — Antioch, Balkh, Basra, Bursa, Constantine, Edirne, Granada, Herat, Jerusalem, Khiva, Konya, Kufa, Málaga, Murcia, Nishapur, Palermo, Samarkand, Samarra, Seville, Tlemcen, Tus and Valencia — each checked against its gazetteer record before linking. Wasit was deliberately left unlinked: the gazetteer entry is typed administrative-unit and sits ~50 km from the record's own approximate coordinates, so it waits for coordinate reconciliation rather than a guessed match.

## v1.3.1 — 2026-11-07

### Tests
- **Proof of concept: an autonomous decision ledger.** New `docs/decisions/` directory, a precedent extractor that mines the repository's own rulings (`D-` records, FLAG lines, founder decisions) into `precedents.yaml`, and a pilot `decide` pipeline that routes each question through a non-delegable policy gate, a precedent match, and a conservative reversible default — emitting an auditable decision record for every outcome. Documentation and build-time scripts only; nothing changes on the site, in the data or in any policy, and deploys, deletions, spending, outreach and review-status changes remain founder-only by design.

### Fixed
- **Event locations now carry an address in structured data.** Google Search Console flagged events whose JSON-LD `location` had a name and coordinates but no `address`. Event locations — and place pages themselves — now emit a `PostalAddress` built only from what the place's own record attests: the place as locality and its registered region as region (for Mecca: locality Mecca, region Arabia). Historical places have no street address and no modern country field in their records, so none is invented.
- **Object images load again.** The Content-Security-Policy `img-src` directive allowed only same-origin images, so browsers blocked every museum-collection photograph hotlinked from Wikimedia Commons, the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the Victoria and Albert Museum and the Cleveland Museum of Art — the Objects wing rendered caption text with broken-image icons. `img-src` in `site/public/_headers` now also allows those five image hosts; no other directive changed.
- **3D tour: al-Khwarizmi's sources stay in step with his record.** The People hall stop now includes the record's MacTutor source, restoring complete source parity and allowing the tour's provenance check to pass. Tour navigation and the Arabic, English and Urdu descriptions are unchanged.
- **Intermittent 520 errors: Workers Cache no longer shared across deploys.** The production Worker config set `cross_version_cache = true`, so cache entries written during a deploy window survived every later deploy, could not be cleared by any zone-level purge (Cloudflare documents that purges do not affect Workers Caching), and were served by some edge locations as intermittent 520 errors while Worker logs stayed clean. `cross_version_cache` is now `false`, so each deploy starts from a fresh cache partition.

### Data
- **Companions as one set: 25 more companions linked to the Sahaba group.** The coverage-expansion programme's Phase 1 added `member_of` edges for the next 25 published companion records (Abu Layla Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b through al-Irbad ibn Sariya), each edge citing the source its own record rests on, so the companions can be queried as a single set. 157 published companion records remain in this move.

- **Job Browser: the potter and the weaver join the crafts wave.** Two more crafts get sourced articles in Arabic, English and Urdu: the potter, who here is the maker of glazed architectural tile from Samarra to Iznik and Kutahya, and the weaver, the Ottoman cullah with his looms, guild, merchants and decline. The weaver record covers the Ottoman period only, and says what is not yet written.
- **Job Browser: the crafts wave begins with the papermaker and the tanner.** Two hand crafts join the Job Browser with sourced articles in Arabic, English and Urdu and the first craft blocks (materials and techniques): the papermaker, from the TDV encyclopaedia's paper entry, and the tanner, from its leather entry. People tied to them include al-Fadl ibn Yahya and Ibrahim Muteferrika for paper, and Sawda bint Zam'a and Zaynab bint Jahsh for leather, each with the entry's own hedging.

The 42 lecture series are grouped by speaker in collapsible sections, with contested series labelled. The page opens with what a khutba, dars and series are and the museum's describe-never-preach notice, and links the Fatwa Explorer and the JSON data. The linear-interpolation instrument is distinct from his plate of heavens, sine and circumference work; hypothetical modern numbers explain the task without claiming original graduations, global priority or software ancestry.
- The Modern Islam Browser gets its data model (plan 26, Phase 1, approved by the founder on 6 November 2026 as D-000): a twenty-fourth class, `award`, for prizes, medals, sales certifications, rankings, titles and competition prizes; four optional sourced blocks on every record, `honours` (who gave what to whom and when, with the result), `footprint` (the Wikipedia languages, Wikidata item, catalogue ids and dated press coverage of a subject), `reach` (platform figures read on a date, never stated as facts) and `horizon` (what is announced, in production, under construction or scheduled, with its expected date); `sports` on a person, `tracks` on an album, `scope` and `countries` on a group; new kinds (album, song, protest, attack, competition, award ceremony, festival, heritage month, exhibition, tournament, launch, newspaper, television channel, radio station, newsletter, channel, record label, production company, device, product, chain, grocery, airline, hotel, manufacturer, conglomerate, team, band, think tank, online community, Islamic centre, museum, university campus) and roles (singer, composer, actor, director, producer, presenter, journalist, diplomat, banker, economist, entrepreneur, comedian, influencer, coach, astronaut, judge, lawyer, nurse, professor); nine predicates (performed, composed, produced, played for, represented, owns, organised, hosted, and the derived `awarded`). A record's browser section is derived from its class, kind and dates, never typed; `npm run modern:census` counts the existing records per section into `docs/modern-islam/coverage.md`. The static API gains `/api/v1/award/index.json`, `/api/v1/modern/index.json`, one file per section, one per year from 1976, and the reach indices `/api/v1/modern/top/<list>.json` with their printed formula. No award record, no page and no content yet; nothing is live until the founder deploys, and no Worker or workflow file changed.
- Validator rules for the new blocks: an honour needs a real award record, a year or date and a source, a position only when ranked and a level only when certified; a press item needs a defined source; a reach figure needs its date; a horizon needs a source and an expected or announced date, and a build warning names horizons whose date has passed; `awarded` cannot be hand-written; a song's or album's prose may not carry a lyric block; a modern person's school or order needs two independent sources (the modern-figures rulings), and "made by Muslims" needs a basis for records in the browser's window.

- The Modern Islam Browser opens at /ar/modern/, /en/modern/ and /ur/modern/ over the 2,010 existing records whose dated facts fall from 1976 on: a home with the year-by-year ribbon (Hijri and Gregorian), the nineteen section tiles with their counts and newest records, the upcoming and new-in-30-days strips, the reach-index links, the countries and the languages; a page per section with facets by kind, decade and country (the figures section grouped by field) and a name filter that needs no JavaScript to read the full list; a page per year since 1976, per country and per language; the new-records page; the reach-index pages with their printed formula; a strip on every entity page in the window with its sections, honours, footprint, dated reach figures and upcoming badge, and the honoured records on award pages; a landing card and an Explore menu entry. Lists say "listed is not endorsed"; nothing is ranked by taste. A section of more than 300 records (the figures section lists 1,467 people) renders compact rows in every one of its lists, so the page stays under its 700 KB budget while the full list remains plain HTML. The pilot records for the sections still empty follow; nothing is live until the founder deploys.

- A Method page (`/{lang}/method/`, Arabic «المنهج») in Arabic, English and Urdu states the museum's working rules in the open, digested from its own documents: what it holds (the twenty-four classes, the nine wings, the span from the world of 610 to the present including the modern era); the publication standard (claims cite defined sources, provenance is recorded, one defined cited source suffices, no review stands between a record that meets the bar and publication; data CC0, prose CC BY-SA 4.0); how topics, people and works are chosen (gap-driven coverage with the gaps published, lanes and waves with nobody skipped, minimal honest records where evidence is thin, the modern-figures reach thresholds and Tier-A evidence for inventions); how classification is guarded (the five claim statuses, a person's faith only on two independent sources attesting it for the person himself — never office, headship, family, descent or an infobox — with doubt recorded as `unknown` and the contested reading preserved; views named before they are stated under the stated Sunni frame; unrecognised wings default to Ideas, multi-wing entries show every wing as a tag); what the museum refuses (unsourced claims, single-source sensitive classifications, depictions of prophets, sources that fail the authenticity gate, unverifiable or aggregator modern channels, anything beyond well-sourced public facts for the living, hidden gaps and silent skips); ages and sensitivity (kid mode, the children's wing's own rulebook); and corrections made in the open, with links to the governing documents. Linked from every page's footer beside the authenticity link.

- A dispute-resolution protocol now stands in `CONTRIBUTING.md` ("Disputes and contested claims"): a dispute is a pull request against the single record, settled by two independent sources attesting the value directly, with attested minority readings preserved in the record's note rather than deleted, structured-data values treated as leads rather than proof, escalation to a recorded founder ruling where the evidence standard cannot decide, and no drive-by reversals of settled values. Alongside it, `docs/agents/orchestration.md` documents how the agent fleet actually builds the museum — git as the only shared memory, bounded waves with file-level briefs and hard limits, the literal "0 errors" / "0 fail" merge gates, the founder as router and court of appeal, and the wave-brief template with the per-wave pipeline.

### Removed
- **Extremism check in `npm run validate` (`scripts/check-extremism.ts`).** The hard block is now enforced by the build: it fails when any data or content file names a blocked organisation or media wing, in Latin, Arabic or Urdu, unless the record is a founder-approved exception; known innocent names (Marj Dabiq, Tafsir al-Manar, Ibn Hamas, the 1992 Islamic State of Afghanistan and others) are built-in non-matches, with 40 tests.
- **Agent rules: content safety (`docs/agents/content-safety.md`).** The hard block on terrorist-organisation content now has its own agent document with the blocked lists, the non-matches that must stay, and the founder's record-by-record decisions of 7 November 2026; it is linked from `AGENTS.md` and `docs/agents/README.md` so no agent misses it.
- **Extremism firewall: founder review reverses most of the clean-up.** After the founder's record-by-record yes/no review (`docs/delegation/extremism-firewall-questions.md`), 135 of the 144 changed records are restored exactly as they were and listed in `docs/delegation/extremism-firewall-exceptions.md`. Only the biographies of Ahmed Yassin and Ahmed al-Sharaa and their seven source records stay removed. Entity totals fall by 2 and source totals by 7.

- Tafsir Browser: al-Tabari vol. 10, batch 40 (pp. 262-268, reports 11844-11858): 5:33 continues (the view that the ruler is free to choose and its argument from the word 'or', al-Tabari's choice and answers, the sense of cutting on opposite sides and the first views on banishment), in Arabic, English and Urdu, cited as {cite:tafsir-tabari-shakir-v10 p. 268}; stop at the foot of p. 268.
- IndexNow hardening and documentation (`docs/indexnow.md`): IndexNow was already live for the production site — the key file at the site root, the `scripts/indexnow.mjs` helper that reports each deploy's changed pages, and the production-only `notify-indexnow` deploy job. The helper now also hard-fails for any host other than islam.museum, so the staging twin (uat) can never be announced to search engines through it however it is invoked, and a short note records how the key, the helper and the workflow fit together. cookwala.ai runs the same setup with its own key.

- The Job Browser gains the translator, in Arabic, English and Urdu, from the TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi article on the tercüman, read in full. It keeps the interpreter of speech apart from the translator of books, and follows the work from the pre-Islamic courts through the Ottoman imperial divan and the translation office. Zayd ibn Thabit, Ibn Wahshiyya and Hoca İshak Efendi, who already have records, now carry the occupation. No person was created from a name alone. With this office, every court-and-administration job in the taxonomy has a record. **العربية:** ديوان الوظائف يكتمل بمنصب المترجم، في النقل الشفهي ونقل الكتب، من القصور السابقة للإسلام إلى غرفة الترجمة العثمانية. **اردو:** ملازمتوں کے براؤزر میں مترجم کا عہدہ شامل ہوا، زبانی ترجمہ اور کتابوں کا ترجمہ، عثمانی دفترِ ترجمہ تک۔ اس سے دربار اور انتظام کے درج تمام عہدوں کا ریکارڈ مکمل ہو گیا۔

- The Job Browser gains four court offices, each in Arabic, English and Urdu, from a TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi article read in full. - Tafsir Browser: al-Tabari vol. 13, batch 21 (pp. 173-179, reports 15250-15251): 7:159 closes (the river of honey and the community beyond China, with the editor's notes), 7:160 (the twelve tribes and the grammarians' dispute on the feminine number, the twelve springs, the cloud, manna and quails), 7:161 (the town and the word 'hittah') and 7:162 (the changed word and the punishment) are filed in full, and 7:163 is begun (the town by the sea), in Arabic, English and Urdu.
- Al-Tabari's Jami' al-Bayan (Shakir edition), volume 14, pp. 77-83 filed in Arabic, English and Urdu (reports 16330-16342): 8:71 closes and 8:72 is filed to the foot of p. 83 (the Emigrants and Helpers as allies, inheritance by emigration and its abrogation by the kinship verses, aid owed to those who did not emigrate except against a treaty people, the four ranks the Prophet left), cited as {cite:tafsir-tabari-shakir-v14 p. 83}; the next stop is p. 84. Statements are given as transmitted with no museum verdict.
- Al-Tabari's Jami' al-Bayan (Shakir edition), volume 14, pp. 70-76 filed in Arabic, English and Urdu (reports 16316-16330): the rest of 8:68 (the prior writing, the view that ignorance is not held to account, al-Tabari's general reading, Umar and Sa'd ibn Mu'adh), 8:69 and 8:70 in full (the lawful booty, al-Abbas and the ransom, the Bahrain money) and 8:71 begun (the captives' possible treachery, the scribe who apostatised and the Ansari's vow), cited as {cite:tafsir-tabari-shakir-v14 p. 76}; the next stop is p. 77 in 8:71. Statements are given as transmitted, with al-Tabari's choices and the editor's notes attributed to them and no museum verdict.
- Al-Tabari's commentary on 12:36 (the two youths in prison, their dreams, grapes called khamr in Oman, Joseph's good doing) is filed in full and 12:37 is begun (the creed he left), from volume 16 pp. 95-101 (reports 19266 to 19285), in Arabic, English and Urdu.
- Al-Tabari's commentary on 12:33 closes at p. 89 (why prison was dearer, the verse on inclining), 12:34 (the answered prayer) and 12:35 (the signs seen, the prison as expiation, the grammarians on the lam and the 'hin') are filed in full and 12:36 is begun (the two youths), from volume 16 pp. 88-94 (reports 19246 to 19265), in Arabic, English and Urdu.
- Al-Tabari's commentary on 12:31 closes at p. 85 (the shares of beauty given to Joseph and his mother, the readings of 'hasha li-llah' and 'ma hadha basharan'), 12:32 is filed in full (the Aziz's wife admits her solicitation) and 12:33 is begun (why prison was dearer), from volume 16 pp. 80-87 (reports 19225 to 19243), in Arabic, English and Urdu.
- Al-Tabari's commentary on 5:16 closes at p. 146, 5:17 is filed in full (the refutation of the Messiah's divinity, God's dominion and power) and 5:18 is begun (the claim to be God's sons and beloved, and the question why He punishes them), from volume 10 pp. 146-152 (reports 11613 and 11614), in Arabic, English and Urdu.
- Al-Tabari's commentary on 5:14 closes at p. 140 (the enmity stirred up among the Christians alone, with the Nestorians, Jacobites and Melkites), 5:15 is filed in full (the Messenger who makes clear what was hidden, the stoning report, the light and the clear book) and 5:16 is begun (God's approval and the paths of peace), from volume 10 pp. 139-145 (reports 11607 to 11612), in Arabic, English and Urdu.
- Al-Tabari's commentary on 5:13 is filed from volume 10 pp. 125-135 (reports 11584 to 11595: the broken covenant and the curse, the readings 'qasiya' and 'qasiyya' of the hardened hearts, the altered words, the forgotten portion, the treachery of Banu al-Nadir, and whether 'pardon them' was abrogated) and 5:14 is begun (the Christians' covenant and the enmity stirred up among them, pp. 135-138, reports 11596 to 11606), in Arabic, English and Urdu.
- Modern Islam Browser, web section, batch 9 (content only, no deployment): two large Arabic websites, in Arabic, English and Urdu. Dorar al-Saniyya, the waqf foundation's site of Islamic encyclopedias, from its hadith encyclopedia to creed, fiqh and history, online by November 2001; and the Alukah Network, thirteen Arabic and English sites of scholarship and letters founded in 2006, whose sermons section the museum already holds.
- Modern Islam Browser, enterprise section, batch 05: six more Islamic banks with Arabic, English and Urdu prose — Gatehouse Bank (London), Bank Islam Brunei Darussalam, Pakistan's Faysal Bank (which lost its Shariah status in 2002 and regained it as a full Islamic bank in December 2022), Bangladesh's Al-Arafah Islami Bank and Social Islami Bank, and Turkey's state-owned Ziraat Katılım. The Bangladeshi banks' ownership changes, lawsuits and 2012 US Senate allegations are told with the banks' denials, no verdict. Content only, no deployment.
- Tafsir Browser: al-Tabari vol. 11, batch 18 (pp. 140-146, reports 12852-12863): 5:105 continues with the reports on whether the verse applies now or at the end of time (Abu Mazin's circle in Medina, Ibn Umar and Ibn Mas'ud, Jubayr ibn Nufayr, the hadith of Abu Tha'laba on the fifty workers), with the editor's chain notes, in Arabic, English and Urdu; the second view begins at the foot of p. 146.
- Modern Islam Browser, web section, batch 8 (content only, no deployment): three Arabic websites in Arabic, English and Urdu, each dated by its earliest archived page. Islamway, begun by two volunteers in late 1998 as 'The Islamway Radio' and now an archive of tens of thousands of sermons and recitations; the Ibn Baz website, online by November 1999 as the shaykh's official site and today a Zad Group project; and Islam Story, Ragheb el-Sergani's Islamic history site, online by April 2006.
- Modern Islam Browser, books section, batch 05: four more English translations of the meanings of the Qur'an, each with Arabic, English and Urdu prose: Ali Özek's team's translation (Istanbul 1992; The Majestic Qur'an, 2000), Musharraf Hussain's Majestic Qur'an (Nottingham 2018, with the imams' review and its errata), Abdur Raheem Kidwai's What is in the Quran? (2013) and Abdulaziz AlMubarak's strictly literal Qur'aan The Supreme (Beirut 2008). Content from the Münster Global Qur'an reviews. Content only, no deployment.
- Modern Islam Browser, books section, batch 04: seven Islamic publishers that were one-line draft cards now have full records with Arabic, English and Urdu prose: Darussalam (1986), the Islamic Texts Society (Cambridge, 1981), Kube Publishing (2007, with the Islamic Foundation imprint), Kazi Publications (Chicago, 1972), Goodword Books (Delhi, 1996), Ta-Ha Publishers (London, March 1980) and Turath Publishing (London, 1997). Three wrong founding years in the drafts are corrected from the publishers' own pages (Goodword 1990 → 1996, Turath 2000 → 1997, Kube 1984 → 2007), and "by Muslims" is kept only where a source states it. Content only, no deployment.
- Modern Islam Browser, enterprise section, batch 04: seven finance and halal-food records with Arabic, English and Urdu prose — new BankIslami Pakistan, Dukhan Bank (Qatar, 23rd on Forbes Middle East's 2025 bank list), Al Baraka Bank Pakistan and Kuwait International Bank; rebuilt Wahed (founded 2017, not 2015 as the draft said), Saffron Road and the Islamic Development Bank. Dukhan Bank's reported role in holding frozen Iranian funds is told with both the Iranian claim and the US denial. Content only, no deployment.
- Modern Islam Browser, enterprise section, batch 03: eleven records with Arabic, English and Urdu prose. Halal and standards bodies: Malaysia's JAKIM, Indonesia's halal agency BPJPH and the OIC's SMIIC. Islamic finance: the IsDB Group's trade finance arm ITFC, Takaful Malaysia, Albaraka Türk, the Dallah Al-Baraka group and the Dow Jones Islamic Market Index. Halal travel and giving: CrescentRating and LaunchGood. Kuveyt Türk is rebuilt from its draft. Content only, no deployment.
- Modern Islam Browser, web section, batch 7 (content only, no deployment): three apps from Pakistan, in Arabic, English and Urdu. Islam360, the Karachi Qur'an and hadith search app that grew from a 2009 desktop program and runs on donations; Quran Majeed, Pakdata's Qur'an app with recitations and translations in fifty languages; and Labbaik VR, a virtual-reality simulator that trains pilgrims in the rites of Hajj and Umrah. Store figures are dated; the makers' own claims are attributed.
